title: Ezekiel

stories.title: 🌩️ Ezekiel 1
summaryBullets: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was among the exiles by the River Kebar, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God. (1:1).
On the fifth day of the month— it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin— (1:2).
the word of the LORD came directly to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Kebar. And there the LORD’s hand was upon him. (1:3).
I looked and saw a whirlwind coming from the north, a great cloud with fire flashing back and forth and brilliant light all around it. In the center of the fire was a gleam like amber, (1:4).
and within it was the form of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: They had a human form, (1:5).
but each had four faces and four wings. (1:6).
Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the hooves of a calf, gleaming like polished bronze. (1:7).
Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. All four living creatures had faces and wings, (1:8).
and their wings were touching one another. They did not turn as they moved; each one went straight ahead. (1:9).
The form of their faces was that of a man, and each of the four had the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle. (1:10).
Such were their faces. Their wings were spread upward; each had two wings touching the wings of the creature on either side, and two wings covering its body. (1:11).
Each creature went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, without turning as they moved. (1:12).

In the midst of the living creatures was the appearance of glowing coals of fire, or of torches. Fire moved back and forth between the living creatures; it was bright, and lightning flashed out of it. (1:13).
The creatures were darting back and forth as quickly as flashes of lightning. (1:14).
When I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each creature with its four faces. (1:15).
The workmanship of the wheels looked like the gleam of beryl, and all four had the same likeness. Their workmanship looked like a wheel within a wheel. (1:16).
As they moved, they went in any of the four directions, without pivoting as they moved. (1:17).
Their rims were high and awesome, and all four rims were full of eyes all around. (1:18).
So as the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them, and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels also rose. (1:19).
Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, and the wheels would rise alongside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels. (1:20).

When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when the creatures stood still, the wheels stood still; and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose alongside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels. (1:21).
Spread out above the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of an awesome expanse, gleaming like crystal. (1:22).
And under the expanse, their wings stretched out toward one another. Each one also had two wings covering its body. (1:23).

When the creatures moved, I heard the sound of their wings like the roar of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army. When they stood still, they lowered their wings. (1:24).
And there came a voice from above the expanse over their heads as they stood still with their wings lowered. (1:25).
Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne with the appearance of sapphire, and on the throne high above was a figure like that of a man. (1:26).

From what seemed to be His waist up, I saw a gleam like amber, with what looked like fire within it all around. And from what seemed to be His waist down, I saw what looked like fire; and brilliant light surrounded Him. (1:27).

The appearance of the brilliant light all around Him was like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell facedown and heard a voice speaking. (1:28).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:1-4: Vision of the LORD in the temple.
Exodus 24:10: Sapphire-like pavement under God.
Daniel 7:9-10: Thrones and the Ancient of Days.
Revelation 4:2-8: Throne, living creatures, and rainbow.

translationNotes.note: Not a river but a major irrigation canal off the Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, near the city of Nippur. Its Akkadian name means the great canal, and it is named in cuneiform business records from the same region. Babylon settled deported communities along its banks to work the land, which is where Ezekiel and the Judean exiles were living.

translationNotes.term: The fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile
translationNotes.note: Ezekiel dates almost every oracle by counting from one event: the deportation of King Jehoiachin in 597 BC, recorded in 2 Kings 24:10-16. Verse 2 gives the fifth year, 593 BC. The book runs on that clock from beginning to end, so 8:1 falls in 592 BC, 24:1 is the day the siege of Jerusalem began, 33:21 is when the news of its fall arrived, and 40:1 falls in 573 BC.

Verse 1 opens with a thirtieth year and does not say thirty of what, then verse 2 supplies the exile date. Ezekiel was a priest, according to 1:3, and Numbers 4:3 sets thirty as the age at which a Levite entered full sanctuary service. He receives this vision at the age he should have begun serving in a temple he is a thousand miles away from.

A rare word used only in 1:4, 1:27 and 8:2, describing something with the glow of hot polished metal or of amber. English versions render it amber, gleaming bronze or glowing metal. Modern Hebrew later borrowed the word for electricity, which is a nineteenth-century coinage and has nothing to do with what Ezekiel saw.

Verses 15-21 describe a wheel beside each creature with a second wheel inside it, set crosswise, so the assembly could roll in any of the four directions without turning. The rims are full of eyes. The point of the design is stated in 1:12 and 1:17: it goes straight ahead wherever the spirit goes and never has to turn around.

Israel's worship placed God's presence above the cherubim in one fixed room in one building. This vision puts the same throne on wheels beside a canal in Babylonian territory. That is the whole force of chapter 1 for a deported priest, and it sets up chapters 10 and 11, where the throne leaves Jerusalem, and chapter 43, where it comes back.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel sees the LORD’s mobile throne-chariot: living creatures, wheels full of eyes, an expanse like crystal, and the radiant glory of God.

headings.text: Ezekiel’s Vision by the River Kebar

stories.title: 📜 Ezekiel 2
summaryBullets: “Son of man,” He said to me, “stand up on your feet and I will speak to you.” (2:1).
And as He spoke to me, the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and I heard Him speaking to me. (2:2).
“Son of man,” He said to me, “I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me. To this very day they and their fathers have rebelled against Me. (2:3).
They are obstinate and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you are to say to them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ (2:4).
And whether they listen or refuse to listen— for they are a rebellious house— they will know that a prophet has been among them. (2:5).

But you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Do not be afraid, though briers and thorns surround you, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their presence, though they are a rebellious house. (2:6).
But speak My words to them, whether they listen or refuse to listen, for they are rebellious. (2:7).
And you, son of man, listen to what I tell you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.” (2:8).
Then I looked and saw a hand reaching out to me, and in it was a scroll, (2:9).
which He unrolled before me. And written on the front and back of it were words of lamentation, mourning, and woe. (2:10).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 1:4-10: A prophet told not to fear their faces, with the LORD's words put into his mouth.
Isaiah 6:8-13: A commission given with the outcome named in advance, to a people who will hear and not understand.
Exodus 3:10-12: Moses sent to a people and given the promise that God will be with him.
Revelation 5:1-4: A scroll written inside and on the back, sealed, in the hand of the One on the throne.
Daniel 8:17: Daniel addressed as son of man and told to understand the vision.

translationNotes.note: It simply means human being, son of Adam. God uses it of Ezekiel more than ninety times and never uses his name after 1:3. Standing in front of the throne of chapter 1, the address keeps saying what he is: a mortal. This is not the same as the title in Daniel 7:13 that Jesus takes for Himself in the Gospels, which is a figure coming with the clouds of heaven.

The Hebrew word is the one used for armed revolt against a king, not for bad manners. Calling Israel a house of rebellion frames the whole book as a treason case, and the phrase recurs at 2:5, 2:6, 2:8, 3:9, 3:26, 12:2 and 24:3.

Verse 6 tells him he will be living among these. Scorpions in the Judean and Mesopotamian countryside were an everyday hazard, hiding under stones and in bedding, and their sting was a known danger to a sleeping man. The three named things are the ordinary hostile environment of the region, applied to his audience.

translationNotes.term: Written on the front and back
translationNotes.note: A scroll was normally written only on the inner face, since the outer side rubs against the roll and against the hand. Verse 10 says this one is written on both sides, which means the text has run past the space allowed for it. What fills it is named in the same verse: lamentation, mourning and woe.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands Ezekiel to stand and sends him to the rebellious Israelites with a message, warning him not to fear their resistance; God then presents him a scroll written with laments and mourning on both sides.

stories.title: 📜 Ezekiel 3
summaryBullets: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.” (3:1).
So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll. (3:2).
“Son of man,” He said to me, “eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.” So I ate, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. (3:3).
Then He said to me, “Son of man, go now to the house of Israel and speak My words to them. (3:4).
For you are not being sent to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language, but to the house of Israel — (3:5).
not to the many peoples of unfamiliar speech and difficult language whose words you cannot understand. Surely if I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you. (3:6).
But the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to you, since they are unwilling to listen to Me. For the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted. (3:7).
Behold, I will make your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads. (3:8).
I will make your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed at their presence, even though they are a rebellious house.” (3:9).
“Son of man,” He added, “listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart. (3:10).
Go to your people, the exiles; speak to them and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ whether they listen or refuse to listen.” (3:11).
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard a great rumbling sound behind me: “Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!” (3:12).
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another and the sound of the wheels beside them, a great rumbling sound. (3:13).
So the Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD upon me. (3:14).
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib who dwelt by the River Kebar. And for seven days I sat where they sat and remained there among them, overwhelmed. (3:15).
At the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (3:16).
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, give them a warning from Me. (3:17).

If I say to the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ but you do not warn him or speak out to warn him from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity, and I will hold you responsible for his blood. (3:18).
But if you warn a wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself. (3:19).

Now if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered. And I will hold you responsible for his blood. (3:20).
But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will indeed live because he heeded your warning, and you will have saved yourself.” (3:21).
And there the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.” (3:22).
So I got up and went out to the plain, and behold, the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown. (3:23).
Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house. (3:24).
And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people. (3:25).
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, though they are a rebellious house. (3:26).

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house. (3:27).
crossRefs: Revelation 10:8-11: John is told to take a little scroll and eat it, sweet in the mouth and bitter in the stomach.
Jeremiah 15:16: Your words were found and I ate them, and they became the joy of my heart.
Psalm 119:103: How sweet are Your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth.
Ezekiel 33:1-9: The watchman charge given again in the same words, after Jerusalem has fallen.
2 Samuel 18:24-27: A watchman on the roof of the gate calling down what he can see, the office as it actually worked.

translationNotes.note: The command in 3:1-3 is to swallow the message before delivering it, and the taste is honey. That is not a comment on the contents, which 2:10 has already said are lamentation and woe. The sweetness is in the receiving. John is given the same instruction in Revelation 10:9-10, with the added detail that it turned his stomach bitter afterward.

A real military post, not a metaphor. A city set a man on the wall or on the roof of the gatehouse to scan the approaches, and when he saw dust or armed men he sounded the ram's horn. 2 Samuel 18:24-27 and 2 Kings 9:17-20 show one at work, calling down what he can make out. The duty was absolute: a lookout who saw an army and said nothing had the deaths on him, which is exactly the accounting 3:18-21 sets out.

The exile settlement on the Kebar canal where Ezekiel lived, named in 3:15. The name comes from Akkadian and means mound of the flood, the term for an abandoned ruin heap; a tell is a mound built up from the debris of a town. The Judeans were resettled on a derelict site and told to make it work. The modern Israeli city took the name from this verse in 1910.

Verse 15 has him sit among them for seven days, stunned and silent. Seven days was the fixed period of mourning for the dead in Israel, seen in Genesis 50:10 and 1 Samuel 31:13, and Job's friends sit with him seven days in Job 2:13. The number tells the reader what he was doing without saying it: he was sitting shiva for his own people.

translationNotes.term: Tongue stuck to the roof of the mouth
translationNotes.note: Verses 26-27 impose a restriction that runs the length of the first half of the book: he may speak only when God gives him a word, and the muteness lifts in 33:22 when the news of Jerusalem's fall arrives. Between those two points his message is largely delivered by acted signs rather than speech, which is why chapters 4, 5 and 12 look the way they do.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel eats a scroll that tastes sweet, then is sent to speak God's words to the exiled Israelites despite their hardened resistance; God appoints him a watchman responsible for warning both the wicked and the righteous, then confines him to his house and binds his tongue until God speaks through him.

stories.title: 🧱 Ezekiel 4
summaryBullets: “Now you, son of man, take a brick, place it before you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem. (4:1).
Then lay siege against it: Construct a siege wall, build a ramp to it, set up camps against it, and place battering rams around it on all sides. (4:2).

Then take an iron plate and set it up as an iron wall between yourself and the city. Turn your face toward it so that it is under siege, and besiege it. This will be a sign to the house of Israel. (4:3).
Then lie down on your left side and place the iniquity of the house of Israel upon yourself. You are to bear their iniquity for the number of days you lie on your side. (4:4).
For I have assigned to you 390 days, according to the number of years of their iniquity. So you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel. (4:5).
When you have completed these days, lie down again, but on your right side, and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. I have assigned to you 40 days, a day for each year. (4:6).
You must turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and prophesy against it. (4:7).
Now behold, I will tie you up with ropes so you cannot turn from side to side until you have finished the days of your siege. (4:8).

But take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt; put them in a single container and make them into bread for yourself. This is what you are to eat during the 390 days you lie on your side. (4:9).
You are to weigh out twenty shekels of food to eat each day, and you are to eat it at set times. (4:10).
You are also to measure out a sixth of a hin of water to drink, and you are to drink it at set times. (4:11).
And you shall eat the food as you would a barley cake, after you bake it over dried human excrement in the sight of the people.” (4:12).
Then the LORD said, “This is how the Israelites will eat their defiled bread among the nations to which I will banish them.” (4:13).
“Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now I have not eaten anything found dead or mauled by wild beasts. No unclean meat has ever entered my mouth.” (4:14).
“Look,” He replied, “I will let you use cow dung instead of human excrement, and you may bake your bread over that.” (4:15).
Then He told me, “Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem. They will anxiously eat bread rationed by weight, and in despair they will drink water by measure. (4:16).
So they will lack food and water; they will be appalled at the sight of one another wasting away in their iniquity. (4:17).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 25:1-4: The siege of Jerusalem as it happened, with the famine and the breach of the wall.
Leviticus 26:26-29: Bread rationed out by weight and eaten without satisfaction, in the covenant curses.
Deuteronomy 28:52-57: Siege pressed against the high fortified walls until people eat their own children.
Numbers 14:34: A year for each day, forty years for the forty days of spying out the land.
Deuteronomy 23:12-14: The law requiring human waste to be buried outside the camp, the uncleanness 4:12-15 turns on.

translationNotes.note: A sun-dried mud brick, the standard building block of Mesopotamia and also its writing surface: scribes drew and wrote on damp clay. Verse 1 has Ezekiel scratch a plan of Jerusalem onto one, which is a Babylonian mapmaker's act. Clay tablets carrying city plans have been recovered from Mesopotamia, so the sign uses the local medium.

Verse 2 names the whole kit in order. The siege wall is a wall of circumvallation thrown up around the city so nothing gets in or out. The ramp is a packed earth and rubble slope built up against the wall to bring men and machines level with the top; the Assyrian assault ramp at Lachish still stands. The camps are the troop enclosures, and the battering rams are timber frames on wheels housing an iron-headed beam.

A flat iron griddle, ordinary kitchen equipment used for baking flatbread over a fire; the same word appears in Leviticus 2:5. Verse 3 has him stand it on edge between himself and the model city as an iron wall. A cooking plate becomes a barrier, in the chapter that is about to ration his food.

translationNotes.term: Twenty shekels of food a day
translationNotes.note: A shekel weighed about two fifths of an ounce (11.4 grams), so twenty shekels is roughly eight ounces (230 grams) of bread for a whole day, weighed out and eaten at set times. That is a starvation ration, and it is measured rather than served because under siege food stopped being a meal and became an allowance.

translationNotes.term: A sixth of a hin of water
translationNotes.note: A hin is about a gallon (3.8 litres), so a sixth of a hin is roughly two thirds of a quart, about 21 fluid ounces (0.6 litre), for a day. A working adult needs several times that in a hot climate. The measured water in 4:11 is the same message as the weighed bread: the city's cisterns are being counted out cup by cup.

Dried animal dung was the ordinary cooking fuel in a land short of firewood, and still is in parts of the region. What God first commands in 4:12 is human excrement, which Deuteronomy 23:12-14 requires to be buried outside the camp. Ezekiel protests in 4:14 that he has never eaten anything unclean, and the fuel is changed to cow dung. The horror is the point: under siege even the fire is defiled.

Verses 4-6 assign a day for each year, the same reckoning Numbers 14:34 uses. He lies 390 days on his left side for the northern kingdom and 40 on his right for Judah, 430 in all, which is the number of years Exodus 12:40 gives for Israel in Egypt. The bread of 4:9 is a famine loaf of six mixed grains and pulses, wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt, thrown together because no one ingredient is left in quantity.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel draws Jerusalem on clay and acts out its siege with an iron pan as a wall; he then lies on his left side for 390 days bearing Israel's sin, then on his right side for 40 days bearing Judah's sin, eating rationed bread baked over cow dung to symbolize how Jerusalem will face famine and defilement.

stories.title: 🧱 Ezekiel 5
summaryBullets: “As for you, son of man, take a sharp sword, use it as a barber’s razor, and shave your head and beard. Then take a set of scales and divide the hair. (5:1).

When the days of the siege have ended, you are to burn up a third of the hair inside the city; you are also to take a third and slash it with the sword all around the city; and you are to scatter a third to the wind. For I will unleash a sword behind them. (5:2).
But you are to take a few strands of hair and secure them in the folds of your garment. (5:3).
Again, take a few of these, throw them into the fire, and burn them. From there a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel. (5:4).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘This is Jerusalem, which I have set in the center of the nations, with countries all around her. (5:5).

But she has rebelled against My ordinances more wickedly than the nations, and against My statutes worse than the countries around her. For her people have rejected My ordinances and have not walked in My statutes.’ (5:6).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You have been more insubordinate than the nations around you; you have not walked in My statutes or kept My ordinances, nor have you even conformed to the ordinances of the nations around you.’ (5:7).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I Myself am against you, Jerusalem, and I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations. (5:8).
Because of all your abominations, I will do to you what I have never done before and will never do again. (5:9).
As a result, fathers among you will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter all your remnant to every wind.’ (5:10).

Therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled My sanctuary with all your detestable idols and abominations, I Myself will withdraw My favor; I will not look upon you with pity, nor will I spare you. (5:11).

A third of your people will die by plague or be consumed by famine within you, a third will fall by the sword outside your walls, and a third I will scatter to every wind and unleash a sword behind them. (5:12).
And when My anger is spent and I have vented My wrath against them, I will be appeased. And when I have spent My wrath on them, they will know that I, the LORD, in My zeal have spoken. (5:13).
I will make you a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of all who pass by. (5:14).
So you will be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I execute judgments against you in anger, wrath, and raging fury. I, the LORD, have spoken. (5:15).
When I shower you with the deadly arrows of famine and destruction that I will send to destroy you, I will intensify the famine against you and cut off your supply of food. (5:16).

I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will leave you childless. Plague and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will bring a sword against you. I, the LORD, have spoken.” (5:17).
crossRefs: Leviticus 21:5: Priests forbidden to shave their heads or the edges of their beards, the act Ezekiel is commanded to perform.
Leviticus 26:29: You will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters, the horror named again in 5:10.
Deuteronomy 28:63-64: Uprooted from the land and scattered among all the peoples, in the covenant curses.
2 Kings 25:8-12: The burning, the killing and the deportation, the three portions of hair carried out.
Deuteronomy 4:5-8: Israel set among the nations so they would see her statutes and call her wise, the standing 5:5-7 says she inverted.

translationNotes.term: A sword used as a razor
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew word covers both a barber's razor and a scribe's knife; verse 1 says to take a sharp sword and use it as one. Ezekiel is a priest, and Leviticus 21:5 forbids priests to shave the head or the beard at all. He is ordered to do in public the one thing his office forbids, with a weapon, which makes the act itself part of the message.

Verses 1-2 have him weigh the shorn hair on scales and split it in three: a third burned inside the model city, a third struck with the sword around it, a third scattered to the wind with the sword drawn after it. Verse 12 supplies the reading, plague and famine, sword, and dispersion. Weighing it links the sign to the weighed rations of the previous chapter.

translationNotes.term: A few strands tucked into the folds
translationNotes.note: Verse 3 tells him to take a small number of hairs and bind them into the hem of his robe, and 5:4 has some of even those thrown into the fire. The hem or fold of a garment was where a man carried what mattered; Haggai 2:12 and Proverbs 17:23 use it as a pocket. It is the remnant, and the chapter will not let even the remnant go untouched.

translationNotes.term: In the centre of the nations
translationNotes.note: Verse 5 says God set Jerusalem in the middle of the nations with lands all around her. Judah sat on the land bridge between Africa and Asia, on the trade and army road every empire used. The charge in 5:6-7 is that a nation placed where everyone would see her behaved worse than the peoples watching.

Verse 10 states it flatly, and it is not rhetoric. Leviticus 26:29 and Deuteronomy 28:53-57 list it among the covenant curses, 2 Kings 6:28-29 records it during the siege of Samaria, and Lamentations 2:20 and 4:10 record it during the siege this chapter is about. Starvation inside a sealed city ended there.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel shaves his head and beard, dividing the hair into thirds to symbolize Jerusalem's fate: one third burned, one third struck with a sword, one third scattered to the wind. God declares Jerusalem will face plague, famine, and sword because she has defiled his sanctuary and rebelled against him more than the nations around her.

stories.title: ⛰️ Ezekiel 6
summaryBullets: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (6:1).
“Son of man, set your face against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them. (6:2).

You are to say: ‘O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: I am about to bring a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places. (6:3).
Your altars will be demolished and your incense altars will be smashed; and I will cast down your slain before your idols. (6:4).
I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols and scatter your bones around your altars. (6:5).

Wherever you live, the cities will be laid waste and the high places will be demolished, so that your altars will be laid waste and desecrated, your idols smashed and obliterated, your incense altars cut down, and your works blotted out. (6:6).
The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD. (6:7).
Yet I will leave a remnant, for some of you will escape the sword when you are scattered among the nations and throughout the lands. (6:8).

Then in the nations to which they have been carried captive, your survivors will remember Me — how I have been grieved by their adulterous hearts that turned away from Me, and by their eyes that lusted after idols. So they will loathe themselves for the evil they have done and for all their abominations. (6:9).
And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not declare in vain that I would bring this calamity upon them. (6:10).

This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stomp your feet, and cry out “Alas!” because of all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel, who will fall by sword and famine and plague. (6:11).
He who is far off will die by the plague, he who is near will fall by the sword, and he who remains will die by famine. So I will vent My fury upon them. (6:12).

Then you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, and under every green tree and leafy oak— the places where they offered fragrant incense to all their idols. (6:13).
I will stretch out My hand against them, and wherever they live I will make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’” (6:14).
crossRefs: Leviticus 26:30-31: I will destroy your high places and pile your corpses on the lifeless forms of your idols.
Deuteronomy 12:2-3: Tear down the shrines on the high mountains and hills and under every green tree.
2 Kings 23:4-20: Josiah wrecks the high places and burns human bones on the altars, the demolition 6:4-6 describes.
Numbers 33:52: Destroy their carved images and cast idols and demolish all their high places.
Ezekiel 36:1-12: The mountains of Israel addressed a second time, now with a promise instead of a sentence.

translationNotes.note: Ezekiel addresses the terrain itself in 6:2-3, mountains, hills, ravines and valleys, because that is where the shrines were. Canaanite worship sites were open-air platforms on ridge tops and beside springs in the wadis, not buildings in towns. Speaking to the landscape is a way of naming every site at once.

A raised open-air worship platform with an altar, usually a standing stone, a wooden pole for Asherah, and space for feasting. They were the ordinary local shrines of the land, and Israel kept using them. Deuteronomy 12:2-3 orders them destroyed; 1 Kings and 2 Kings judge nearly every king of Judah by whether the high places came down.

Ezekiel's own word for idols, used nearly forty times in the book and almost nowhere else. It is built on a root for pellets or droppings, so it works out to something like dung-pellets. It is a deliberate insult chosen over the neutral words for image or idol, and English translations soften it to detestable things or idols.

Verse 5 says the dead bodies of the Israelites will be laid in front of their idols and their bones scattered around the altars. Contact with a corpse made a person and a place unclean under Numbers 19:11-16, and human bones on an altar put it permanently out of use. 2 Kings 23:14-16 records Josiah doing exactly that to the shrines at Bethel and across Judah.

Verse 14 draws a line from one end of the land to the other. The wilderness is the desert in the south; Diblah is at the northern end. Some English versions read Riblah instead, because the Hebrew letters for R and D differ only by the length of one stroke and are easily confused in copying. Riblah on the Orontes is where Nebuchadnezzar kept his field headquarters, named in Jeremiah 39:5 and 52:9.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands Ezekiel to prophesy judgment against Israel's mountains and high places, declaring he will destroy their altars and idols, kill their people, and scatter their bones; yet some will survive captivity and eventually remember him and loathe their idolatry.

stories.title: ⛰️ Ezekiel 7
summaryBullets: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (7:1).
“O son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: ‘The end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land. (7:2).
The end is now upon you, and I will unleash My anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations. (7:3).
I will not look on you with pity, nor will I spare you, but I will punish you for your ways and for the abominations among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’ (7:4).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Disaster! An unprecedented disaster — behold, it is coming! (7:5).
The end has come! The end has come! It has roused itself against you. Behold, it has come! (7:6).
Doom has come to you, O inhabitants of the land. The time has come; the day is near; there is panic on the mountains instead of shouts of joy. (7:7).
Very soon I will pour out My wrath upon you and vent My anger against you; I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations. (7:8).
I will not look on you with pity, nor will I spare you, but I will punish you for your ways and for the abominations among you. Then you will know that it is I, the LORD, who strikes the blow. (7:9).
Behold, the day is here! It has come! Doom has gone out, the rod has budded, arrogance has bloomed. (7:10).
Their violence has grown into a rod to punish their wickedness. None of them will remain: none of their multitude, none of their wealth, and nothing of value. (7:11).
The time has come; the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for wrath is upon the whole multitude. (7:12).

The seller will surely not recover what he sold while both remain alive. For the vision concerning the whole multitude will not be revoked, and because of their iniquity, not one of them will preserve his life. (7:13).
They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to war, for My wrath is upon the whole multitude. (7:14).
The sword is outside; plague and famine are within. Those in the country will die by the sword, and those in the city will be devoured by famine and plague. (7:15).
The survivors will escape and live in the mountains, moaning like doves of the valley, each for his own iniquity. (7:16).
Every hand will go limp, and every knee will turn to water. (7:17).
They will put on sackcloth, and terror will overwhelm them. Shame will cover all their faces, and all their heads will be shaved. (7:18).

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will seem unclean. Their silver and gold cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD. They cannot satisfy their appetites or fill their stomachs with wealth, for it became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity. (7:19).
His beautiful ornaments they transformed into pride and used them to fashion their vile images and detestable idols. Therefore I will make these into something unclean for them. (7:20).
And I will hand these things over as plunder to foreigners and loot to the wicked of the earth, who will defile them. (7:21).
I will turn My face away from them, and they will defile My treasured place. Violent men will enter it, and they will defile it. (7:22).
Forge the chain, for the land is full of crimes of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence. (7:23).
So I will bring the most wicked of nations to take possession of their houses. I will end the pride of the mighty, and their holy places will be profaned. (7:24).
Anguish is coming! They will seek peace, but find none. (7:25).
Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor after rumor. Then they will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction from the priests will perish, as will counsel from the elders. (7:26).

The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, and I will judge them by their own standards. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’” (7:27).
crossRefs: Amos 8:1-3: A basket of summer fruit, and the word that the end has come upon My people Israel.
Zephaniah 1:14-18: The great day of the LORD, when neither silver nor gold will be able to deliver them.
Isaiah 2:20: On that day men will throw away their idols of silver and gold to the moles and bats.
Proverbs 11:4: Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
Lamentations 4:1-2: The gold grown dim and the sacred stones poured out at the head of every street.

translationNotes.note: The word is hammered five times in 7:2-6. Amos 8:2 uses it with a pun, a basket of summer fruit, qayits, against the end, qets. Here there is no pun and no cushioning; the announcement is that the thing everyone has been treating as a distant threat has arrived.

Verse 19 says they will fling their silver into the streets and treat their gold as unclean, because it cannot satisfy hunger. Under siege, precious metal is worth what someone will exchange for it, and inside a sealed city nobody has grain to trade. 2 Kings 6:25 prices a donkey's head at eighty shekels of silver during the siege of Samaria, which is what that inversion looks like in practice.

Verse 12 tells the buyer not to rejoice and the seller not to mourn. Land in Israel was normally sold under the redemption and Jubilee rules of Leviticus 25, where the seller could expect it back and the buyer was really leasing the harvests. Verse 13 cancels that: the seller will not return to what he sold as long as they both live, because the whole population is going into exile.

Verse 23 orders a chain made, because the land is full of bloodshed. Prisoners of war were marched in linked neck irons or wrist fetters, and Assyrian and Babylonian reliefs show columns of captives chained in file. It is not a figure of speech; it is the standard equipment of a deportation.

Verse 26 lists the three sources of guidance failing together: vision from the prophet, instruction from the priest, counsel from the elders. Those were the three institutions of a working society, and Jeremiah 18:18 names the same three. When all three go, there is nowhere left to ask.

stories.keyTakeaway: God declares that the end has come upon Israel and will repay them according to their conduct and detestable practices; disaster, violence, and famine will overtake the land, their wealth will become worthless, and foreigners will plunder their houses.

stories.title: 🔥 Ezekiel 8
summaryBullets: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me; and there the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me. (8:1).
Then I looked and saw a figure like that of a man. From His waist down His appearance was like fire, and from His waist up He was as bright as the gleam of amber. (8:2).

He stretched out what looked like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. Then the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and carried me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court, where the idol that provokes jealousy was seated. (8:3).
And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the plain. (8:4).
“Son of man,” He said to me, “now lift up your eyes to the north.” So I lifted up my eyes to the north, and in the entrance north of the Altar Gate I saw this idol of jealousy. (8:5).

“Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what they are doing — the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing — to drive Me far from My sanctuary? Yet you will see even greater abominations.” (8:6).
Then He brought me to the entrance to the court, and I looked and saw a hole in the wall. (8:7).
“Son of man,” He told me, “dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall and discovered a doorway. (8:8).
Then He said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are committing here.” (8:9).
So I went in and looked, and engraved all around the wall was every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel. (8:10).
Before them stood seventy elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had a censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense was rising. (8:11).

“Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol? For they are saying, ‘The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.’” (8:12).
Again, He told me, “You will see them committing even greater abominations.” (8:13).
Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and I saw women sitting there, weeping for Tammuz. (8:14).
“Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Yet you will see even greater abominations than these.” (8:15).

So He brought me to the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there at the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east; and they were bowing to the east in worship of the sun. (8:16).

“Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Is it not enough for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are practicing here, that they must also fill the land with violence and continually provoke Me to anger? Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose! (8:17).
Therefore I will respond with wrath. I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. Although they shout loudly in My ears, I will not listen to them.” (8:18).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 21:1-7: Manasseh sets a carved Asherah image inside the house of which God had said My Name will be there.
Deuteronomy 4:15-19: The command against carved images and against bowing down to the sun, moon and host of heaven.
Exodus 24:1-11: Seventy elders of Israel go up with Moses and eat and drink before God, the body of men shown in the dark in 8:11.
Deuteronomy 4:23-24: The LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God, the jealousy the image in 8:3 provokes.
Jeremiah 7:17-18: Household worship of the queen of heaven in the streets of Jerusalem in the same period.

translationNotes.note: Chapter 8 is laid out as a guided inspection, each stop worse than the last. At the north gate, an image that provokes jealousy, 8:3-6. Through a hole in the wall, seventy elders in a hidden room, 8:7-13. At the north gate of the house, women weeping for Tammuz, 8:14-15. Between the porch and the altar, twenty-five men with their backs to the temple bowing east, 8:16. The route moves inward, so the worst of it is happening in the holiest place.

Verses 7-12 have Ezekiel dig through a wall to find a doorway, and inside a room with every kind of crawling creature and beast and all the idols of Israel carved around the walls, with seventy elders standing in the dark, each holding a censer. Seventy elders is the number of Israel's governing council, set in Exodus 24:1 and Numbers 11:16. What they say in 8:12 is the reason for the room: the LORD does not see us.

Tammuz is Dumuzi in Sumerian, the shepherd consort of the goddess Inanna or Ishtar. Mesopotamian ritual mourned his descent to the underworld each year with organised wailing by women, timed to the drying of the pastures in high summer. The Babylonian month named for him, which the Jewish calendar still carries, falls in June and July. Verse 14 puts that rite at the north gate of the temple in Jerusalem.

Verse 16 places twenty-five men between the porch and the altar, the most restricted ground in the temple courts, with their backs to the sanctuary and their faces to the sunrise. The temple faced east, so worshipping the rising sun meant turning your back on the house you were standing in. 2 Kings 23:5 and 23:11 record Josiah removing the sun priests and the horses dedicated to the sun.

translationNotes.term: Putting the branch to the nose
translationNotes.note: Verse 17 ends with a gesture nobody now can identify with certainty: they put the branch to their nose. It appears nowhere else in Scripture. The text reports it as one more thing being done in the temple and does not explain it, and no explanation should be invented for it.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel is lifted by the Spirit to Jerusalem, where a divine figure shows him idolatrous practices throughout the temple - including an idol of jealousy, seventy elders worshiping in a hidden chamber, women mourning Tammuz, and men bowing to the sun - and declares he will respond with anger and refuse to listen to their pleas.

headings.text: The Vision of Idolatry in the Temple

stories.title: 🔥 Ezekiel 9
summaryBullets: Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, saying, “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with a weapon of destruction in hand.” (9:1).

And I saw six men coming from the direction of the Upper Gate, which faces north, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand. With them was another man clothed in linen who had a writing kit at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze altar. (9:2).

Then the glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherubim, where it had been, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And He called to the man clothed in linen who had the writing kit at his side. (9:3).
“Go throughout the city of Jerusalem,” said the LORD, “and put a mark on the foreheads of the men sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there.” (9:4).
And as I listened, He said to the others, “Follow him through the city and start killing; do not show pity or spare anyone! (9:5).

Slaughter the old men, the young men and maidens, the women and children; but do not go near anyone who has the mark. Now begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple. (9:6).
Then He told them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!” So they went out and began killing throughout the city. (9:7).
While they were killing, I was left alone. And I fell facedown and cried out, “Oh, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?” (9:8).

He replied, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see.’ (9:9).
But as for Me, I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. I will bring their deeds down upon their own heads.” (9:10).
Then the man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his side reported back, “I have done as You commanded.” (9:11).
crossRefs: Exodus 12:7-13: Blood on the doorframes so that the destroyer passes over that house.
Revelation 7:2-3: An angel seals the servants of God on their foreheads before any harm is done.
Revelation 9:4: Only those without the seal of God on their foreheads may be harmed.
1 Peter 4:17: Judgment begins with the household of God, the order given in 9:6.
Exodus 28:39-43: Linen prescribed for those who serve in the sanctuary, the clothing of the man with the writing kit.

translationNotes.term: The writing kit at his side
translationNotes.note: A scribe's palette worn on the belt: a flat board of wood or ivory with hollows for cakes of black and red ink and a long slot holding cut reed pens, carried on a cord. Egyptian examples survive intact. Verse 2 puts one man carrying office equipment among six carrying weapons, and 9:11 has him report back that the paperwork is done.

The Hebrew says put a tav on the foreheads. Tav is the last letter of the alphabet, and in the old Hebrew script used in Ezekiel's day it was written as a simple cross or an X, the shape visible on inscriptions and seals of the period. It was also a general word for a signature mark, as in Job 31:35. The instruction is to sign a man's forehead.

Verse 4 gives the single criterion for the mark: grieving over the abominations being done in the city. Not resistance, not reform, not office. The people spared are the ones the previous chapter's worshippers would have counted as doing nothing.

Verse 6 sends the executioners to start at the temple, and the text notes they began with the elders in front of it. The holiest ground is the first hit, not the last refuge. 1 Peter 4:17 states the same order as a principle.

Linen was the fabric of sanctuary service, prescribed for the priests in Exodus 28 and required of the high priest on the Day of Atonement in Leviticus 16:4. The figure who marks and spares in chapters 9 and 10 is dressed as a priest and carries a scribe's tools, and he is the one told in 10:2 to take fire from between the cherubim.

stories.keyTakeaway: Six executioners arrive at the temple with a man in linen, who marks the foreheads of those grieving Jerusalem's sins before the others kill all the unmarked - from the sanctuary outward through the city. When Ezekiel protests, God explains the slaughter is justified by Israel's bloodshed and injustice.

stories.title: 🔥 Ezekiel 10
summaryBullets: And I looked and saw above the expanse, above the heads of the cherubim, the likeness of a throne of sapphire. (10:1).

And the LORD said to the man clothed in linen, “Go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim. Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city.” And as I watched, he went in. (10:2).
Now when the man went in, the cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple, and a cloud filled the inner court. (10:3).

Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherubim and stood over the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD. (10:4).
The sound of the wings of the cherubim could be heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks. (10:5).
When the LORD commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, “Take fire from within the wheelwork, from among the cherubim,” the man went in and stood beside a wheel. (10:6).
Then one of the cherubim reached out his hand and took some of the fire that was among them. And he put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who received it and went out. (10:7).
(The cherubim appeared to have the form of human hands under their wings.) (10:8).
Then I looked and saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. And the wheels gleamed like a beryl stone. (10:9).
As for their appearance, all four had the same form, like a wheel within a wheel. (10:10).

When they moved, they would go in any of the four directions, without turning as they moved. For wherever the head faced, the cherubim would go in that direction, without turning as they moved. (10:11).
Their entire bodies, including their backs, hands, and wings, were full of eyes all around, as were their four wheels. (10:12).
I heard the wheels being called “the whirling wheels.” (10:13).
Each of the cherubim had four faces: the first face was that of a cherub, the second that of a man, the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle. (10:14).
Then the cherubim rose upward. These were the living creatures I had seen by the River Kebar. (10:15).
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them, and even when they spread their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not veer away from their side. (10:16).
When the cherubim stood still, the wheels also stood still, and when they ascended, the wheels ascended with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels. (10:17).
Then the glory of the LORD moved away from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim. (10:18).

As I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose up from the ground, with the wheels beside them as they went. And they stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, with the glory of the God of Israel above them. (10:19).
These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the River Kebar, and I knew that they were cherubim. (10:20).
Each had four faces and four wings, with what looked like human hands under their wings. (10:21).
Their faces looked like the faces I had seen by the River Kebar. Each creature went straight ahead. (10:22).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 1:4-28: The same throne, living creatures and wheels, described at the Kebar canal.
Exodus 25:18-22: Cherubim of hammered gold over the ark, where God says He will meet with Moses and speak.
1 Kings 8:10-11: The cloud fills the house so the priests cannot stand to minister, the arrival that 10:18 reverses.
Isaiah 6:6-7: A live coal taken from the altar with tongs and carried to the prophet's mouth.
Ezekiel 43:1-5: The glory returns to the temple by the east gate, the road it leaves by here.

translationNotes.note: Not infants with wings. They are the guardian figures of God's throne: stationed at Eden's gate with a flaming sword in Genesis 3:24, worked in gold over the ark in Exodus 25:18-22, carved into the temple walls and doors in 1 Kings 6:29-35, and here bearing the throne itself. Composite winged guardian creatures flanking thrones and doorways are standard in the art of the whole region.

The departure is deliberately slow and is tracked step by step: from above the cherubim to the threshold in 10:4, back over the cherubim in 10:18, out to the east gate in 10:19, up from the middle of the city in 11:23, and finally to the hill east of Jerusalem. Nothing is destroyed until it has gone. The same route runs in reverse in 43:1-5.

Verse 2 sends the man in linen in among the wheels to take fire from between the cherubim and throw it over Jerusalem. The fire comes from the throne itself. Verse 7 has a cherub hand it to him, so the burning of the city in 2 Kings 25:9 is shown here as beginning with fire carried out of the sanctuary.

Verse 12 says the whole bodies of the cherubim, their backs, hands, wings and the wheels, were covered with eyes all around. It follows chapter 8, where the elders in the hidden room say the LORD does not see us. The vision answers that in the plainest way available.

In 1:10 the four faces are man, lion, ox and eagle. In 10:14 the ox has been replaced by the face of a cherub, and 10:20 states that Ezekiel now recognises the creatures from the Kebar as cherubim. The book records the identification changing as he understands what he saw the first time.

stories.keyTakeaway: A man in linen takes burning coals from among the cherubim and scatters them over the city as the LORD's glory rises from above the cherubim and moves toward the temple threshold. The cherubim, each with four faces and accompanied by four wheels covered in eyes, rise upward with the LORD's glory and move toward the east gate of the temple.

stories.title: 🔥 Ezekiel 11
summaryBullets: Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the gate of the house of the LORD that faces east. And there at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, who were leaders of the people. (11:1).
And the LORD said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who plot evil and give wicked counsel in this city. (11:2).
They are saying, ‘Is not the time near to build houses? The city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat.’ (11:3).
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, O son of man!” (11:4).

And the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me and told me to declare that this is what the LORD says: “That is what you are thinking, O house of Israel; and I know the thoughts that arise in your minds. (11:5).
You have multiplied those you killed in this city and filled its streets with the dead. (11:6).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: The slain you have laid within this city are the meat, and the city is the pot; but I will remove you from it. (11:7).
You fear the sword, so I will bring the sword against you, declares the Lord GOD. (11:8).
I will bring you out of the city and deliver you into the hands of foreigners, and I will execute judgments against you. (11:9).
You will fall by the sword, and I will judge you even to the borders of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (11:10).
The city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be the meat within it. I will judge you even to the borders of Israel. (11:11).
Then you will know that I am the LORD. For you have neither followed My statutes nor practiced My ordinances, but you have conformed to the ordinances of the nations around you.” (11:12).
Now as I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell facedown and cried out in a loud voice, “Oh, Lord GOD, will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end?” (11:13).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (11:14).

“Son of man, your brothers — your relatives, your fellow exiles, and the whole house of Israel — are those of whom the people of Jerusalem have said, ‘They are far away from the LORD; this land has been given to us as a possession.’ (11:15).

Therefore declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Although I sent them far away among the nations and scattered them among the countries, yet for a little while I have been a sanctuary for them in the countries to which they have gone.’ (11:16).

Therefore declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries to which you have been scattered, and I will give back to you the land of Israel.’ (11:17).
When they return to it, they will remove all its detestable things and all its abominations. (11:18).
And I will give them singleness of heart and put a new spirit within them; I will remove their heart of stone and give them a heart of flesh, (11:19).
so that they may follow My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God. (11:20).
But as for those whose hearts pursue detestable things and abominations, I will bring their conduct down upon their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.” (11:21).
Then the cherubim, with the wheels beside them, spread their wings, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them. (11:22).
And the glory of the LORD rose up from within the city and stood over the mountain east of the city. (11:23).
And the Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to Chaldea, to the exiles in the vision given by the Spirit of God. After the vision had gone up from me, (11:24).
I told the exiles everything the LORD had shown me. (11:25).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 24:3-13: The cooking pot taken up again and turned against the men who had used it as a slogan.
Jeremiah 24:4-7: The exiles named as the good figs, the reversal 11:15-16 makes against those left in Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 29:11-14: God's word to the exiles that He will be found by them where they are.
Ezekiel 36:26-27: A heart of flesh for a heart of stone, and God's own Spirit put within them.
Zechariah 14:4: Feet standing on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, the hill the glory stops on in 11:23.

translationNotes.term: This city is the pot and we are the meat
translationNotes.note: Verse 3 quotes a slogan going around Jerusalem. The men left in the city after the 597 BC deportation are saying the walls are the pot and they are the choice cuts inside it, safe while the fire burns outside. Verses 7-11 take the image apart: the meat is the people they killed, and they themselves will be taken out of the pot and judged at the border. Chapter 24 picks the same pot up again and boils it dry.

translationNotes.term: Judgment at the border of Israel
translationNotes.note: Verses 10-11 say they will fall by the sword at the border. That is where it happened. 2 Kings 25:18-21 and Jeremiah 52:24-27 record the officials of Jerusalem taken north to Riblah in the land of Hamath, at the far edge of the territory, and executed there.

Verse 13 records one of the twenty-five leaders dropping dead mid-oracle, and Ezekiel falling on his face and crying out that God is making a full end of the remnant. The book keeps the prophet's reaction in the text. The answer in 11:16-20 is the promise that comes next.

Verse 16 says that although God scattered them among the countries, He has been to them a sanctuary in small measure in the lands where they have gone. The people in Jerusalem were arguing in 11:15 that the exiles had forfeited the land and God with it. This answers that the presence went with the deported, not with the deed to the property.

translationNotes.term: Heart of stone for heart of flesh
translationNotes.note: Verses 19-20 promise one heart, a new spirit, the stone taken out and flesh put in, so that they walk in His statutes. The same pledge is repeated at greater length in 36:26-27, where God's own Spirit is added to it, and Jeremiah 31:33 states it as instruction written on the heart.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel prophesies against twenty-five leaders plotting evil in Jerusalem, warning they will be driven out and judged at Israel's borders; Pelatiah dies during the prophecy. God then promises to gather the scattered Israelites, give them new hearts, and remove their idols, while the glory of the LORD departs from the city.

stories.title: 🏃‍♂️ Ezekiel 12
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (12:1).
“Son of man, you are living in a rebellious house. They have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear, for they are a rebellious house. (12:2).
Therefore, son of man, pack your bags for exile. In broad daylight, set out from your place and go to another as they watch. Perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house. (12:3).
Bring out your baggage for exile by day, as they watch. Then in the evening, as they watch, go out like those who go into exile. (12:4).
As they watch, dig through the wall and carry your belongings out through it. (12:5).
And as they watch, lift your bags to your shoulder and take them out at dusk; cover your face so that you cannot see the land. For I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.” (12:6).

So I did as I was commanded. I brought out my bags for exile by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall by hand. I took my belongings out at dusk, carrying them on my shoulder as they watched. (12:7).
And in the morning the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (12:8).
“Son of man, hasn’t the rebellious house of Israel asked you, ‘What are you doing?’ (12:9).
Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are there.’ (12:10).
You are to say, ‘I am a sign to you.’ Just as it happened here, so will it be done to them; they will go into exile as captives. (12:11).
And at dusk the prince among them will lift his bags to his shoulder and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out. He will cover his face so he cannot see the land. (12:12).
But I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans; yet he will not see it, and there he will die. (12:13).
And I will scatter to every wind all the attendants around him and all his troops, and I will draw a sword to chase after them. (12:14).
And they will know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries. (12:15).
But I will spare a few of them from sword and famine and plague, so that in the nations to which they go, they can recount all their abominations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.” (12:16).
Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (12:17).
“Son of man, eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with quivering and anxiety. (12:18).

Then tell the people of the land that this is what the Lord GOD says about those living in Jerusalem and in the land of Israel: ‘They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dread, for their land will be stripped of everything in it because of the violence of all who dwell in it. (12:19).
The inhabited cities will be laid waste, and the land will become desolate. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’” (12:20).
Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (12:21).
“Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel: ‘The days go by, and every vision fails’? (12:22).

Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will put an end to this proverb, and in Israel they will no longer recite it.’ But say to them: ‘The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled. (12:23).
For there will be no more false visions or flattering divinations within the house of Israel, (12:24).

because I, the LORD, will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be fulfilled without delay. For in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak a message and bring it to pass, declares the Lord GOD.’” (12:25).
Furthermore, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (12:26).
“Son of man, take note that the house of Israel is saying, ‘The vision that he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about the distant future.’ (12:27).
Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘None of My words will be delayed any longer. The message I speak will be fulfilled, declares the Lord GOD.’” (12:28).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 25:4-7: Zedekiah slips out at night, is overtaken near Jericho, blinded and taken to Babylon.
Jeremiah 39:4-7: The parallel account of the king's escape through the gate between the two walls.
Jeremiah 52:7-11: The same flight and capture again, with the sons killed and the king led away in chains.
Amos 8:11-12: A famine of hearing the words of the LORD, the end of the delay 12:21-28 announces.
2 Peter 3:3-4: Scoffers asking where the promise of His coming is, the same complaint as the proverb in 12:22.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַנָּשִׂיא (ha-nasī’), Greek (LXX): ὁ ἄρχων, Aramaic: נְשִׂיאָה (nesiʾā)
translationNotes.note: Title used for the ruling king (historically Zedekiah) in 12:10-12.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִצֹּוד / רֶשֶׁת (mitsod / reshet), Greek: θήρα / δικτύον, Aramaic: מצודא / רשתא
translationNotes.note: Capture imagery for the fleeing leader (12:13).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא־יִמָּשֵׁךְ עוֹד (lo yimmāshekh ‘od), Greek: οὐκέτι χρονιεῖ, Aramaic: לָא יתמשך תוּב
translationNotes.note: God ends the proverb that visions fail or take too long (12:22-28).

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel acts out exile to show Jerusalem’s leaders and people will flee, be captured, and scattered; and God’s warnings will no longer be delayed.

stories.title: 🧱 Ezekiel 13
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (13:1).
“Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are now prophesying. Tell those who prophesy out of their own imagination: Hear the word of the LORD! (13:2).
This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit yet have seen nothing. (13:3).
Your prophets, O Israel, are like foxes among the ruins. (13:4).
You did not go up to the gaps or restore the wall around the house of Israel so that it would stand in the battle on the Day of the LORD. (13:5).
They see false visions and speak lying divinations. They claim, ‘Thus declares the LORD,’ when the LORD did not send them; yet they wait for the fulfillment of their message. (13:6).
Haven’t you seen a false vision and spoken a lying divination when you proclaim, ‘Thus declares the LORD,’ even though I have not spoken? (13:7).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have uttered vain words and seen false visions, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD. (13:8).

My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and speak lying divinations. They will not belong to the council of My people or be recorded in the register of the house of Israel, nor will they enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD. (13:9).
Because they have led My people astray, saying, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace, and whitewashing any flimsy wall that is built, (13:10).
tell those whitewashing the wall that it will fall. Rain will come in torrents, I will send hailstones plunging down, and a windstorm will burst forth. (13:11).
Surely when the wall has fallen, you will not be asked, ‘Where is the whitewash with which you covered it?’ (13:12).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: In My wrath I will release a windstorm, and in My anger torrents of rain and hail will fall with destructive fury. (13:13).

I will tear down the wall you whitewashed and level it to the ground, so that its foundation is exposed. The city will fall, and you will be destroyed within it. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (13:14).
And after I have vented My wrath against the wall and against those who whitewashed it, I will say to you: ‘The wall is gone, and so are those who whitewashed it — (13:15).
those prophets of Israel who prophesied to Jerusalem and saw a vision of peace for her when there was no peace, declares the Lord GOD.’ (13:16).
Now, O son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own imagination. Prophesy against them (13:17).

and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the women who sew magic charms on their wrists and make veils for the heads of people of every height, in order to ensnare their souls. Will you ensnare the souls of My people but preserve your own? (13:18).

You have profaned Me among My people for handfuls of barley and scraps of bread. By lying to My people who would listen, you have killed those who should not have died and spared those who should not have lived. (13:19).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: See, I am against the magic charms with which you ensnare souls like birds, and I will tear them from your arms. So I will free the souls you have ensnared like birds. (13:20).
I will also tear off your veils and deliver My people from your hands, so that they will no longer be prey in your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (13:21).

Because you have disheartened the righteous with your lies, even though I have caused them no grief, and because you have encouraged the wicked not to turn from their evil ways to save their lives, (13:22).
therefore you will no longer see false visions or practice divination. I will deliver My people from your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD.” (13:23).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 23:16-32: Prophets speaking visions from their own minds and stealing words from one another.
Deuteronomy 18:20-22: A prophet who speaks presumptuously in the LORD's name must die, and how to know one.
Jeremiah 6:14: They dress the wound of My people superficially, saying peace, peace, when there is no peace.
Micah 3:5-7: Prophets who cry peace when they are fed and declare war against anyone who does not fill their mouths.
Matthew 7:15-20: Watch out for false prophets in sheep's clothing, who are known by their fruit.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: טָפֵל (ṭāfel), Greek (LXX): κονία (whitewash), Aramaic: טפל (ṭafel)
translationNotes.note: Plastering a weak wall to hide cracks, image for covering lies (13:10-15).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כְּסָתוֹת (kesātōt), Greek (LXX): καταδέσεις, Aramaic: כסותין
translationNotes.note: Obscure term likely for binding charms used in occult practice (13:18-20).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צֹדְדוֹת נְפָשׁוֹת (tsodedot nefashot), Greek: θηρεύουσαι ψυχάς, Aramaic: ציידן נפשתא
translationNotes.note: Figure for trapping people’s lives through deceitful practices (13:18).

The 71-member Jewish supreme council in Jerusalem, presided over by the high priest. Held judicial, religious, and limited civil authority under Roman occupation. Tried Jesus (Mark 14:55), Peter and John (Acts 4), and Stephen (Acts 6:12). Dissolved after the temple's destruction in AD 70.

stories.keyTakeaway: God exposes self-made prophets and prophetesses who promise safety with lies; their whitewash will fail, and He will free the people they trap.

stories.title: 🪨 Ezekiel 14
summaryBullets: Then some of the elders of Israel came and sat down before me. (14:1).
And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (14:2).
“Son of man, these men have set up idols in their hearts and put wicked stumbling blocks before their faces. Should I consult with them in any way? (14:3).

Therefore speak to them and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘When any Israelite sets up idols in his heart and puts a wicked stumbling block before his face, and then comes to the prophet, I the LORD will answer him according to his great idolatry, (14:4).
so that I may take hold of the hearts of the people of Israel. For because of their idols, they are all estranged from Me.’ (14:5).
Therefore tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Repent and turn away from your idols; turn your faces away from all your abominations. (14:6).

For when any Israelite or any foreigner dwelling in Israel separates himself from Me, sets up idols in his heart, and puts a wicked stumbling block before his face, and then comes to the prophet to inquire of Me, I the LORD will answer him Myself. (14:7).
I will set My face against that man and make him a sign and a proverb; I will cut him off from among My people. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (14:8).
But if the prophet is enticed to speak a message, then it was I the LORD who enticed him, and I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from among My people Israel. (14:9).
They will bear their punishment— the punishment of the inquirer will be the same as that of the prophet— (14:10).

in order that the house of Israel may no longer stray from Me and no longer defile themselves with all their transgressions. Then they will be My people and I will be their God, declares the Lord GOD.’” (14:11).
And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (14:12).

“Son of man, if a land sins against Me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out My hand against it to cut off its supply of food, to send famine upon it, and to cut off from it both man and beast, (14:13).
then even if these three men— Noah, Daniel, and Job— were in it, their righteousness could deliver only themselves, declares the Lord GOD. (14:14).
Or if I send wild beasts through the land to leave it childless and desolate, with no man passing through it for fear of the beasts, (14:15).

then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if these three men were in it, they could not deliver their own sons or daughters. They alone would be delivered, but the land would be desolate. (14:16).
Or if I bring a sword against that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through it,’ so that I cut off from it both man and beast, (14:17).
then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if these three men were in it, they could not deliver their own sons or daughters. They alone would be delivered. (14:18).
Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out My wrath upon it through bloodshed, cutting off from it both man and beast, (14:19).

then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they could not deliver their own sons or daughters. Their righteousness could deliver only themselves. (14:20).

For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘How much worse will it be when I send against Jerusalem My four dire judgments— sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague— in order to cut off from it both man and beast? (14:21).

Yet , behold, some survivors will be left in it — sons and daughters who will be brought out. They will come out to you, and when you see their conduct and actions, you will be comforted regarding the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem — all that I have brought upon it. (14:22).
They will bring you consolation when you see their conduct and actions, and you will know that it was not without cause that I have done all these things within it,’ declares the Lord GOD.” (14:23).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 5:7-9: Judgment because of idolatry and adultery, the charge behind the elders' inquiry here.
Leviticus 26:21-26: Wild beasts, sword, plague and famine listed together in the covenant curses.
Genesis 6:8-9: Noah found favour with the LORD and was righteous and blameless among his generation.
Jeremiah 15:1: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me, My heart would not go out to this people.
James 5:11: Job named for his perseverance, and the outcome the Lord brought about.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גִּלּוּלִים עַל־לִבָּם (gillulīm ‘al libbām), Greek (LXX): τὰ βδελύγματα ἐπὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, Aramaic: גלוליא על לבהון
translationNotes.note: Internalized idolatry, not merely statues (14:3-5).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַרְבַּע שִׁפְטֵי רָע (arba‘ shifṭê ra‘), Greek: τέσσαρα κρίματα κακά, Aramaic: ארבע דינין בישין
translationNotes.note: Sword, famine, wild animals, plague (14:21).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הֵמָּה בְצִדְקָתָם יְנַצְּלוּ נַפְשָׁם (hemmah be-tsidqātām yənatsəlū nafshām), Greek: ἑαυτούς μόνους ῥύσονται, Aramaic: לנפשיהון בלחוד מצלין
translationNotes.note: Limits of borrowed righteousness (14:14-20).

stories.keyTakeaway: God confronts hidden idolatry, lists four deadly judgments, and says even the most righteous cannot shield a corrupt land; a remnant will explain the justice of what happened.

stories.title: 🌿 Ezekiel 15
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (15:1).
“Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any other branch among the trees in the forest? (15:2).
Can wood be taken from it to make something useful? Or can one make from it a peg on which to hang utensils? (15:3).
No, it is cast into the fire for fuel. The fire devours both ends, and the middle is charred. Can it be useful for anything? (15:4).
