Even when it was whole, it could not be made useful. How much less can it ever be useful when the fire has consumed it and charred it! (15:5).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I will give up the people of Jerusalem. (15:6).
And I will set My face against them. Though they may have escaped the fire, yet another fire will consume them. And when I set My face against them, you will know that I am the LORD. (15:7).
Thus I will make the land desolate, because they have acted unfaithfully,’ declares the Lord GOD.” (15:8).
crossRefs: Isaiah 5:1-7: The vineyard song, where God looks for good grapes and finds only wild ones.
Jeremiah 2:21: I planted you as a choice vine of sound stock, and you turned into a corrupt, wild vine.
Psalm 80:8-16: A vine brought out of Egypt and planted, its walls broken down and its wood burned with fire.
Hosea 10:1-2: Israel a luxuriant vine that pours out fruit for itself and builds more altars.
John 15:5-6: A branch that does not remain is thrown away, withers, is gathered and burned.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵץ הַגֶּפֶן (‘ets ha-gefen), Greek (LXX): ξύλον ἀμπέλου, Aramaic: אעא דגפנא
translationNotes.note: Emphasizes wood’s unsuitability for building (15:2-5).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָתַתִּיו לָאֵשׁ (natattiv la’esh), Greek: δέδωκα εἰς πῦρ, Aramaic: יהביתיה לנור
translationNotes.note: Judgment image of being burned (15:6).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מָעַל (maʿal, ‘treachery’), Greek: ἀπιστία, Aramaic: מעלא
translationNotes.note: Covenant betrayal leading to judgment (15:8).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is compared to vine wood; good for fruit but useless as timber; so in unfaithfulness it is fit only for fire.

stories.title: 💔 Ezekiel 16
summaryBullets: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (16:1).
“Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations (16:2).
and tell her that this is what the Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites. Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite. (16:3).
On the day of your birth your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water for cleansing. You were not rubbed with salt or wrapped in cloths. (16:4).
No one cared enough for you to do even one of these things out of compassion for you. Instead, you were thrown out into the open field, because you were despised on the day of your birth. (16:5).
Then I passed by and saw you wallowing in your blood, and as you lay there in your blood I said to you, ‘Live!’ There I said to you, ‘Live!’ (16:6).
I made you thrive like a plant of the field. You grew up and matured and became very beautiful. Your breasts were formed and your hair grew, but you were naked and bare. (16:7).

Then I passed by and saw you, and you were indeed old enough for love. So I spread My cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I pledged Myself to you, entered into a covenant with you, and you became Mine, declares the Lord GOD. (16:8).
Then I bathed you with water, rinsed off your blood, and anointed you with oil. (16:9).
I clothed you in embroidered cloth and gave you sandals of fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk. (16:10).
I adorned you with jewelry, and I put bracelets on your wrists and a chain around your neck. (16:11).
I put a ring in your nose, earrings on your ears, and a beautiful crown upon your head. (16:12).

So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was made of fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You became very beautiful and rose to be queen. (16:13).
Your fame spread among the nations on account of your beauty, for it was perfect in the splendor I bestowed on you, declares the Lord GOD. (16:14).
But because of your fame, you trusted in your beauty and played the harlot. You lavished your favors on everyone who passed by, and your beauty was theirs for the asking. (16:15).
You took some of your garments and made colorful high places for yourself, and on them you prostituted yourself. Such things should not have happened; never should they have occurred! (16:16).
You also took the fine jewelry of gold and silver I had given you, and you made male idols with which to prostitute yourself. (16:17).
You took your embroidered garments to cover them, and you set My oil and incense before them. (16:18).
And you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you— the fine flour, oil, and honey that I had fed you. That is what happened, declares the Lord GOD. (16:19).
You even took the sons and daughters you bore to Me and sacrificed them as food to idols. Was your prostitution not enough? (16:20).
You slaughtered My children and delivered them up through the fire to idols. (16:21).
And in all your abominations and acts of prostitution, you did not remember the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your own blood. (16:22).
Woe! Woe to you, declares the Lord GOD. And in addition to all your other wickedness, (16:23).
you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every public square. (16:24).
At the head of every street you built your lofty shrines and degraded your beauty. With increasing promiscuity, you spread your legs to all who passed by. (16:25).
You prostituted yourself with your lustful neighbors, the Egyptians, and increased your promiscuity to provoke Me to anger. (16:26).

Therefore I stretched out My hand against you and reduced your portion. I gave you over to the desire of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct. (16:27).
Then you prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, because you were not yet satisfied. Even after that, you were still not satisfied. (16:28).
So you extended your promiscuity to Chaldea, the land of merchants — but even with this you were not satisfied! (16:29).
How weak-willed is your heart, declares the Lord GOD, while you do all these things, the acts of a shameless prostitute! (16:30).
But when you built your mounds at the head of every street and made your lofty shrines in every public square, you were not even like a prostitute, because you scorned payment. (16:31).
You adulterous wife! You receive strangers instead of your own husband! (16:32).
Men give gifts to all their prostitutes, but you gave gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from everywhere for your illicit favors. (16:33).
So your prostitution is the opposite of that of other women: No one solicited your favors, and you paid a fee instead of receiving one; so you are the very opposite! (16:34).
Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the LORD! (16:35).

This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you poured out your wealth and exposed your nakedness in your promiscuity with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children which you gave to them, (16:36).

therefore I will surely gather all the lovers with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and expose you before them, and they will see you completely naked. (16:37).
And I will sentence you to the punishment of women who commit adultery and those who shed blood; so I will bring upon you the wrath of your bloodshed and jealousy. (16:38).

Then I will deliver you into the hands of your lovers, and they will level your mounds and tear down your lofty shrines. They will strip off your clothes, take your fine jewelry, and leave you naked and bare. (16:39).
They will bring a mob against you, who will stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords. (16:40).
Then they will burn down your houses and execute judgment against you in the sight of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers. (16:41).
So I will lay to rest My wrath against you, and My jealousy will turn away from you. Then I will be calm and no longer angry. (16:42).

Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but enraged Me with all these things, I will surely bring your deeds down upon your own head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not committed this lewdness on top of all your other abominations? (16:43).
Behold, all who speak in proverbs will quote this proverb about you: ‘Like mother, like daughter.’ (16:44).

You are the daughter of your mother, who despised her husband and children. You are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite. (16:45).
Your older sister was Samaria, who lived with her daughters to your north; and your younger sister was Sodom, who lived with her daughters to your south. (16:46).
And you not only walked in their ways and practiced their abominations, but soon you were more depraved than they were. (16:47).
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did as you and your daughters have done. (16:48).
Now this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: She and her daughters were arrogant, overfed, and complacent; they did not help the poor and needy. (16:49).
Thus they were haughty and committed abominations before Me. Therefore I removed them, as you have seen. (16:50).

Furthermore, Samaria did not commit half the sins you did. You have multiplied your abominations beyond theirs, and all the abominations you have committed have made your sisters appear righteous. (16:51).

So now you must bear your disgrace, since you have brought justification for your sisters. For they appear more righteous than you, because your sins were more vile than theirs. So you too must bear your shame and disgrace, since you have made your sisters appear righteous. (16:52).
But I will restore Sodom and her daughters from captivity, as well as Samaria and her daughters. And I will restore you along with them. (16:53).
So you will bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you did to comfort them. (16:54).
And your sisters, Sodom with her daughters and Samaria with her daughters, will return to their former state. You and your daughters will also return to your former state. (16:55).
Did you not treat your sister Sodom as an object of scorn in the day of your pride, (16:56).

before your wickedness was uncovered? Even so, you are now scorned by the daughters of Edom and all those around her, and by the daughters of the Philistines— all those around you who despise you. (16:57).
You will bear the consequences of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD. (16:58).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you according to your deeds, since you have despised the oath by breaking the covenant. (16:59).
But I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you. (16:60).
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of My covenant with you. (16:61).
So I will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD, (16:62).
so that when I make atonement for all you have done, you will remember and be ashamed and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, declares the Lord GOD.” (16:63).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 32:10-12: God finds His people in a desert waste and guards them like the pupil of His eye.
Hosea 2:2-13: The unfaithful wife stripped and shamed, and her lovers shown to be no help.
Hosea 2:14-23: The same wife led into the wilderness and betrothed again in righteousness and mercy.
Jeremiah 7:31: Sons and daughters burned in Topheth, the practice charged against Jerusalem in 16:20-21.
Isaiah 54:5-8: For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will bring you back.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פֵּרַשְׂתִּי כְנָפִי (perashti kenāfī), Greek (LXX): ἐξέτεινα τὴν πτέρυγά μου, Aramaic: פרשתי כנפי
translationNotes.note: Idiomatic for entering a marriage covenant (16:8).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: זוֹנָה / זָנָה (zonāh / zānāh), Greek: πόρνη / πορνεύω, Aramaic: זונתא / זני
translationNotes.note: Sexual and spiritual betrayal imagery throughout the chapter.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הֶעֱבַרְתְּ לָהֶם בָּאֵשׁ (heʿevart lahem ba’esh), Greek: παρέδωκας διὰ πυρός, Aramaic: העברת להון בנורא
translationNotes.note: Burning sons and daughters to idols (16:20-21).

The central highland region between Judea and Galilee; capital of the northern kingdom of Israel from 880 BC until Assyrian deportation in 722 BC. The mixed-population descendants who remained ('Samaritans') were despised by Judeans as ethnically and religiously impure. Jesus' choice to travel through Samaria (John 4) and to make a Samaritan the hero of His parable (Luke 10) deliberately upends that prejudice.

stories.keyTakeaway: God raised Jerusalem as His own, but she betrayed Him with violent idolatry and child sacrifice; judgment falls, yet God promises to remember His covenant and establish an everlasting one.

stories.title: 🦅 Ezekiel 17
summaryBullets: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (17:1).
“Son of man, pose a riddle; speak a parable to the house of Israel (17:2).
and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar. (17:3).
He plucked off its topmost shoot, carried it to the land of merchants, and planted it in a city of traders. (17:4).
He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil; he placed it by abundant waters and set it out like a willow. (17:5).
It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with branches turned toward him; yet its roots remained where it stood. So it became a vine and yielded branches and sent out shoots. (17:6).

But there was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers. And behold, this vine bent its roots toward him. It stretched out its branches to him from its planting bed, so that he might water it. (17:7).
It had been planted in good soil by abundant waters in order to yield branches and bear fruit and become a splendid vine.’ (17:8).

So you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Will it flourish? Will it not be uprooted and stripped of its fruit so that it shrivels? All its foliage will wither! It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots. (17:9).
Even if it is transplanted, will it flourish? Will it not completely wither when the east wind strikes? It will wither on the bed where it sprouted.’” (17:10).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (17:11).

“Now say to this rebellious house: ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them, ‘Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, carried off its king and officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon. (17:12).
He took a member of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. Then he carried away the leading men of the land, (17:13).
so that the kingdom would be brought low, unable to lift itself up, surviving only by keeping his covenant. (17:14).

But this king rebelled against Babylon by sending his envoys to Egypt to ask for horses and a large army. Will he flourish? Will the one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and yet escape?’ (17:15).
‘As surely as I live,’ declares the Lord GOD, ‘he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who enthroned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke. (17:16).
Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are built and siege walls constructed to destroy many lives. (17:17).
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Seeing that he gave his hand in pledge yet did all these things, he will not escape!’ (17:18).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘As surely as I live, I will bring down upon his head My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke. (17:19).
I will spread My net over him and catch him in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon and execute judgment upon him there for the treason he committed against Me. (17:20).
All his choice troops will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.’ (17:21).

This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain. (17:22).

I will plant it on the mountain heights of Israel so that it will bear branches; it will yield fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it, taking shelter in the shade of its branches. (17:23).

Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD. I bring the tall tree down and make the low tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.’” (17:24).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 24:17-20: Nebuchadnezzar makes Mattaniah king and renames him Zedekiah, who then rebels against him.
2 Kings 25:1-7: The siege, the flight and the capture, the outcome the riddle in 17:11-21 announces.
Jeremiah 37:5-10: Zedekiah's appeal to Egypt and the failure of the Egyptian relief force.
Psalm 80:8-11: A vine brought out of Egypt and planted, spreading its branches to the sea.
Ezekiel 31:3-9: A great tree with nations sheltering under its branches, the same imagery as 17:22-24.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חִידָה / מָשָׁל (ḥīdāh / māshāl), Greek (LXX): αἴνιγμα / παραβολή, Aramaic: חידא / מתלא
translationNotes.note: God tells Ezekiel to speak a riddle and parable (17:2).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָלָה / בְּרִית (’ālāh / berit), Greek: ὅρκος / διαθήκη, Aramaic: מוֹמָתָא / קְיָמָא
translationNotes.note: Zedekiah’s sworn loyalty to Babylon is called a covenant (17:13) (17:18-19).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קֹטֶרֶת רַךְ (qōteret rakh), Greek: ἄκρον τρυφερόν, Aramaic: קטרת רכא
translationNotes.note: A small shoot God plants to become a noble cedar (17:22-24).

stories.keyTakeaway: Judah’s ruler broke his sworn oath to Babylon by turning to Egypt, ensuring ruin; yet God promises to plant His own sprig that grows into a great tree.

headings.text: The Parable of Two Eagles and a Vine

stories.title: ⚖️ Ezekiel 18
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (18:1).
“What do you people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge’? (18:2).
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel. (18:3).
Behold, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die. (18:4).
Now suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right: (18:5).
He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife or approach a woman during her period. (18:6).
He does not oppress another, but restores the pledge to the debtor. He does not commit robbery, but gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing. (18:7).
He does not engage in usury or take excess interest, but he withholds his hand from iniquity and executes true justice between men. (18:8).
He follows My statutes and faithfully keeps My ordinances. That man is righteous; surely he will live, declares the Lord GOD. (18:9).
Now suppose that man has a violent son, who sheds blood or does any of these things, (18:10).
though the father has done none of them: Indeed, the son eats at the mountain and defiles his neighbor’s wife. (18:11).
He oppresses the poor and needy; he commits robbery and does not restore a pledge. He lifts his eyes to idols; he commits abominations. (18:12).
He engages in usury and takes excess interest. Will this son live? He will not! Since he has committed all these abominations, he will surely die; his blood will be on his own head. (18:13).
Now suppose this son has a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, considers them, and does not do likewise: (18:14).
He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife. (18:15).
He does not oppress another, or retain a pledge, or commit robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing. (18:16).

He withholds his hand from harming the poor and takes no interest or usury. He keeps My ordinances and follows My statutes. Such a man will not die for his father’s iniquity. He will surely live. (18:17).
As for his father, he will die for his own iniquity, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was wrong among his people. (18:18).
Yet you may ask, ‘Why shouldn’t the son bear the iniquity of his father?’ Since the son has done what is just and right, carefully observing all My statutes, he will surely live. (18:19).

The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear the iniquity of his father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of his son. The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him. (18:20).
But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all My statutes, and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die. (18:21).
None of the transgressions he has committed will be held against him. Because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live. (18:22).
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord GOD. Wouldn’t I prefer that he turn from his ways and live? (18:23).

But if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices iniquity, committing the same abominations as the wicked, will he live? None of the righteous acts he did will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die. (18:24).
Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Hear now, O house of Israel: Is it My way that is unjust? Is it not your ways that are unjust? (18:25).
If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices iniquity, he will die for this. He will die because of the iniquity he has committed. (18:26).
But if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life. (18:27).
Because he considered and turned from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die. (18:28).
Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Are My ways unjust, O house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unjust? (18:29).

Therefore, O house of Israel, I will judge you, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent and turn from all your transgressions, so that your iniquity will not become your downfall. (18:30).
Cast away from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed, and fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, O house of Israel? (18:31).
For I take no pleasure in anyone’s death, declares the Lord GOD. So repent and live! (18:32).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 24:16: Fathers are not put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each dies for his own sin.
Exodus 20:5: Visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, the line the sour grapes proverb leaned on.
2 Kings 14:5-6: Amaziah spares the sons of his father's assassins, citing that law by name.
Jeremiah 31:29-30: The sour grapes proverb cancelled, with each man dying for his own iniquity.
Acts 3:19: Repent and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away, the call 18:30-32 makes.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֶפֶשׁ (nephesh, ‘person/life’), Greek (LXX): ψυχή, Aramaic: נפש (nafsh)
translationNotes.note: “The soul who sins shall die” means the person who sins dies (18:4) (18:20).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שׁוּב (shuv), Greek (LXX): ἐπιστρέφω, Aramaic: תוּב (tuv)
translationNotes.note: Key verb for turning from sin to God (18:21) (18:30-32).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָבוֹת אָכְלוּ בֹּסֶר (avot akhlu boser), Greek (LXX): οἱ πατέρες ἔφαγον ὄμφακα, Aramaic: אבות אכלו בוסר
translationNotes.note: A saying God forbids them to use as an excuse (18:2-3).

stories.keyTakeaway: God ends the excuse of inherited guilt: the person who sins dies; the person who turns back lives. He takes no pleasure in anyone’s death and calls people to repent.

headings.text: The Soul Who Sins Will Die

stories.title: 🦁 Ezekiel 19
summaryBullets: “As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel (19:1).
and say: ‘What was your mother? A lioness among the lions! She lay down among the young lions; she reared her cubs. (19:2).
She brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men. (19:3).
When the nations heard of him, he was trapped in their pit. With hooks they led him away to the land of Egypt. (19:4).
When she saw that she had waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion. (19:5).
He prowled among the lions, and became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men. (19:6).
He broke down their strongholds and devastated their cities. The land and everything in it shuddered at the sound of his roaring. (19:7).
Then the nations set out against him from the provinces on every side. They spread their net over him; he was trapped in their pit. (19:8).
With hooks they caged him and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into captivity so that his roar was heard no longer on the mountains of Israel. (19:9).
Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water; it was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant waters. (19:10).
It had strong branches, fit for a ruler’s scepter. It towered high above the thick branches, conspicuous for its height and for its dense foliage. (19:11).
But it was uprooted in fury, cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were stripped off and they withered; the fire consumed them. (19:12).
Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land. (19:13).
Fire has gone out from its main branch and devoured its fruit; on it no strong branch remains fit for a ruler’s scepter.’ This is a lament and shall be used as a lament.” (19:14).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 23:31-34: Jehoahaz reigns three months, is put in chains at Riblah and dies in Egypt.
2 Kings 24:8-15: Jehoiachin reigns three months and is carried off to Babylon with his mother.
2 Kings 24:17-20: Zedekiah placed on the throne by Babylon and rebelling against him, the last of these rulers.
Genesis 49:9: Judah is a lion's cub, the family image the lament turns against Judah's kings.
Psalm 80:8-16: A vine ravaged and burned, the second half of this poem in another voice.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קִינָה (qināh), Greek (LXX): θρῆνος, Aramaic: קינתא (qinata)
translationNotes.note: Formal funeral dirge form used throughout the poem (19:1) (19:14).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֹחַ / חָח (ḥoaḥ/ḥaḥ), Greek (LXX): ἄγκιστρα, Aramaic: חוחין
translationNotes.note: Capture gear used to drag the lion/prince (19:4) (19:9).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֵׁבֶט (shevet), Greek (LXX): ῥάβδος, Aramaic: שבטא
translationNotes.note: Royal staff; the vine had branches fit for scepters (19:11-12).

stories.keyTakeaway: A funeral song mourns Judah’s failed rulers; first taken to Egypt, then to Babylon; and the nation’s strength withered from within.

headings.text: A Lament for the Princes of Israel

stories.title: 🔥 Ezekiel 20
summaryBullets: In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and they sat down before me. (20:1).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (20:2).

“Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: Have you come to inquire of Me? As surely as I live, I will not be consulted by you, declares the Lord GOD. (20:3).
Will you judge them, will you judge them, son of man? Confront them with the abominations of their fathers (20:4).

and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I chose Israel, I swore an oath to the descendants of the house of Jacob and made Myself known to them in the land of Egypt. With an uplifted hand I said to them, ‘I am the LORD your God.’ (20:5).
On that day I swore to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands. (20:6).
And I said to them: ‘Each of you must throw away the abominations before his eyes, and you must not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’ (20:7).

But they rebelled against Me and refused to listen. None of them cast away the abominations before their eyes, and they did not forsake the idols of Egypt. So I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and vent My anger against them in the land of Egypt. (20:8).

But I acted for the sake of My name, that it should not be profaned in the eyes of the nations among whom they were living, in whose sight I had revealed Myself to Israel by bringing them out of the land of Egypt. (20:9).
So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness. (20:10).
And I gave them My statutes and made known to them My ordinances— for the man who does these things will live by them. (20:11).
I also gave them My Sabbaths as a sign between us, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them. (20:12).

Yet the house of Israel rebelled against Me in the wilderness. They did not follow My statutes and they rejected My ordinances— though the man who does these things will live by them — and they utterly profaned My Sabbaths. Then I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and put an end to them in the wilderness. (20:13).
But I acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out. (20:14).

Moreover, with an uplifted hand I swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land that I had given them— a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands — (20:15).
because they kept rejecting My ordinances, refusing to walk in My statutes, and profaning My Sabbaths; for their hearts continually went after their idols. (20:16).
Yet I looked on them with pity and did not destroy them or bring them to an end in the wilderness. (20:17).
In the wilderness I said to their children: ‘Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers or keep their ordinances or defile yourselves with their idols. (20:18).
I am the LORD your God; walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them. (20:19).
Keep My Sabbaths holy, that they may be a sign between us, so that you may know that I am the LORD your God.’ (20:20).

But the children rebelled against Me. They did not walk in My statutes or carefully observe My ordinances — though the man who does these things will live by them — and they profaned My Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out My wrath upon them and vent My anger against them in the wilderness. (20:21).
But I withheld My hand and acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out. (20:22).
However, with an uplifted hand I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands. (20:23).
For they did not practice My ordinances, but they rejected My statutes and profaned My Sabbaths, fixing their eyes on the idols of their fathers. (20:24).
I also gave them over to statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live. (20:25).
And I pronounced them unclean through their gifts — the sacrifice of every firstborn in the fire — so that I might devastate them, in order that they would know that I am the LORD. (20:26).
Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel, and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: In this way also your fathers blasphemed Me by their unfaithfulness against Me. (20:27).

When I brought them into the land that I swore to give them and they saw any high hill or leafy tree, there they offered their sacrifices, presented offerings that provoked Me, sent up their fragrant incense, and poured out their drink offerings. (20:28).
So I asked them: ‘What is this high place to which you go?’ (And to this day it is called Bamah.) (20:29).
Therefore tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: Will you defile yourselves the way your fathers did, prostituting yourselves with their abominations? (20:30).

When you offer your gifts, sacrificing your sons in the fire, you continue to defile yourselves with all your idols to this day. So should I be consulted by you, O house of Israel? As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will not be consulted by you! (20:31).
When you say, ‘Let us be like the nations, like the peoples of the lands, serving wood and stone,’ what you have in mind will never come to pass. (20:32).
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured wrath I will rule over you. (20:33).
With a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured wrath I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands to which you have been scattered. (20:34).
And I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, where I will enter into judgment with you face to face. (20:35).
Just as I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord GOD. (20:36).
I will make you pass under the rod and will bring you into the bond of the covenant. (20:37).

And I will purge you of those who rebel and transgress against Me. I will bring them out of the land in which they dwell, but they will not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (20:38).

And as for you, O house of Israel, this is what the Lord GOD says: Go and serve your idols, every one of you. But afterward, you will surely listen to Me, and you will no longer defile My holy name with your gifts and idols. (20:39).

For on My holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Me in the land. There I will accept them and will require your offerings and choice gifts, along with all your holy sacrifices. (20:40).

When I bring you from the peoples and gather you from the lands to which you have been scattered, I will accept you as a pleasing aroma. And I will show My holiness through you in the sight of the nations. (20:41).
Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I swore to give your fathers. (20:42).
There you will remember your ways and all the deeds with which you have defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done. (20:43).
Then you will know, O house of Israel, that I am the LORD, when I have dealt with you for the sake of My name and not according to your wicked ways and corrupt acts, declares the Lord GOD.” (20:44).
Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (20:45).
“Son of man, set your face toward the south, preach against it, and prophesy against the forest of the Negev. (20:46).

Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear the word of the LORD! This is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to ignite in you a fire, and it will devour all your trees, both green and dry. The blazing flame will not be quenched, and by it every face from south to north will be scorched. (20:47).
Then all people will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it will not be quenched.” (20:48).
Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD, they are saying of me, ‘Is he not just telling parables?’” (20:49).
crossRefs: Exodus 16:23: Sabbaths as a sign.
Numbers 14:11-20: God spares for His name among the nations.
Deuteronomy 12:31: Do not burn sons or daughters in fire.
Ezekiel 36:22-24: Later promise: for My name’s sake I will gather you.

translationNotes.term: For the sake of My name
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְמַעַן שְׁמִי (lema‘an shemī), Greek (LXX): ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου, Aramaic: מטול שמי
translationNotes.note: Reason God gives for restraining full destruction (20:9) (20:14) (20:22).

translationNotes.term: I gave them statutes that were not good (difficult line)
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גַּם־אֲנִי נָתַתִּי לָהֶם חֻקִּים לֹא טוֹבִים (gam-ʾani natatti lahem ḥuqqim lo tovim), Greek (LXX): ἔδωκα αὐτοῖς δικαιώματα οὐκ ἀγαθά, Aramaic: יהבית להון חוקין לא טבין
translationNotes.note: Judicial giving over (cf. 20:25-26) after persistent idolatry; the phrase signals consequence, not that God’s own law was evil.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּמוֹת (bamot), Greek (LXX): ὑψηλά, Aramaic: במתא
translationNotes.note: Local shrines where idolatry and child sacrifice occurred (20:28-31).

stories.keyTakeaway: Across generations Israel rebels, but God acts for His name’s sake; judging, purging, and ultimately gathering them to accept them again.

stories.title: 🗡️ Ezekiel 21
summaryBullets: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (21:1).
“Son of man, set your face against Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries. Prophesy against the land of Israel (21:2).
and tell her that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am against you, and I will draw My sword from its sheath and cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked. (21:3).
Because I will cut off both the righteous and the wicked, My sword will be unsheathed against everyone from south to north. (21:4).
Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have taken My sword from its sheath, not to return it again.’ (21:5).
But you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with a broken heart and bitter grief. (21:6).

And when they ask, ‘Why are you groaning?’ you are to say, ‘Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will melt, and every hand will go limp. Every spirit will faint, and every knee will turn to water.’ Yes, it is coming and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD.” (21:7).
Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (21:8).
“Son of man, prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord says: ‘A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished — (21:9).
it is sharpened for the slaughter, polished to flash like lightning! Should we rejoice in the scepter of My son? The sword despises every such stick. (21:10).
The sword is appointed to be polished, to be grasped in the hand. It is sharpened and polished, to be placed in the hand of the slayer. (21:11).
Cry out and wail, O son of man, for the sword is wielded against My people; it is against all the princes of Israel! They are tossed to the sword with My people; therefore strike your thigh. (21:12).
Surely testing will come! And what if even the scepter, which the sword despises, does not continue?’ declares the Lord GOD. (21:13).
‘So then, son of man, prophesy and strike your hands together. Let the sword strike two times, even three. It is a sword that slays, a sword of great slaughter closing in on every side! (21:14).
So that their hearts may melt and many may stumble, I have appointed at all their gates a sword for slaughter. Yes, it is ready to flash like lightning; it is drawn for slaughter. (21:15).
Slash to the right; set your blade to the left— wherever your blade is directed. (21:16).
I too will strike My hands together, and I will satisfy My wrath.’ I, the LORD, have spoken.” (21:17).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (21:18).
“Now you, son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to take, both starting from the same land. And make a signpost where the road branches off to each city. (21:19).
Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah into fortified Jerusalem. (21:20).
For the king of Babylon stands at the fork in the road, at the junction of the two roads, to seek an omen: He shakes the arrows, he consults the idols, he examines the liver. (21:21).

In his right hand appears the portent for Jerusalem, where he is to set up battering rams, to call for the slaughter, to lift a battle cry, to direct the battering rams against the gates, to build a ramp, and to erect a siege wall. (21:22).
It will seem like a false omen to the eyes of those who have sworn allegiance to him, but it will draw attention to their guilt and take them captive. (21:23).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you have drawn attention to your guilt, exposing your transgressions, so that your sins are revealed in all your deeds — because you have come to remembrance — you shall be taken in hand. (21:24).
And you, O profane and wicked prince of Israel, the day has come for your final punishment.’ (21:25).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Remove the turban, and take off the crown. Things will not remain as they are: Exalt the lowly and bring low the exalted. (21:26).
A ruin, a ruin, I will make it a ruin! And it will not be restored until the arrival of Him to whom it belongs, to whom I have assigned the right of judgment.’ (21:27).

Now prophesy, son of man, and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says concerning the Ammonites and their contempt: ‘A sword! A sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to consume, to flash like lightning— (21:28).
while they offer false visions for you and lying divinations about you— to be placed on the necks of the wicked who are slain, whose day has come, the time of their final punishment. (21:29).
Return the sword to its sheath! In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you. (21:30).
I will pour out My anger upon you; I will breathe the fire of My fury against you; I will hand you over to brutal men, skilled in destruction. (21:31).
You will be fuel for the fire. Your blood will stain your own land. You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.’” (21:32).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 25:1-7: Babylon besieges Jerusalem and the king is taken, the road the omens in 21:18-23 choose.
Deuteronomy 18:10-12: Divination, omen reading and consulting the dead forbidden to Israel.
Jeremiah 27:6-8: Nations handed over to Nebuchadnezzar, and any that will not serve him punished.
Genesis 49:10: The sceptre will not depart from Judah until He comes to whom it belongs.
2 Samuel 7:16: Your house and your kingdom will endure forever, the promise standing behind 21:27.

translationNotes.note: Methods named: arrows (belomancy), household gods (תְּרָפִים teraphim), and liver inspection (hepatoscopy) (21:21).

translationNotes.note: Symbols of office removed from the prince (21:26).

translationNotes.term: Until he comes whose right it is
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עַד־בּוֹא אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הַמִּשְׁפָּט (ʿad-bo’ asher-lo hamishpat), Greek (LXX): ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἐστι τὸ κρίμα, Aramaic: עד ייתי דיליה דינא
translationNotes.note: Transfer of rule promised to the rightful one (21:27).
