stories.title: 🔥 Ezekiel 22
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (22:1).
“As for you, son of man, will you judge her? Will you pass judgment on the city of bloodshed? Then confront her with all her abominations (22:2).
and tell her that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘O city who brings her own doom by shedding blood within her walls and making idols to defile herself, (22:3).

you are guilty of the blood you have shed, and you are defiled by the idols you have made. You have brought your days to a close and have come to the end of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the lands. (22:4).
Those near and far will mock you, O infamous city, full of turmoil. (22:5).
See how every prince of Israel within you has used his power to shed blood. (22:6).
Father and mother are treated with contempt. Within your walls the foreign resident is exploited, the fatherless and the widow are oppressed. (22:7).
You have despised My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths. (22:8).
Among you are slanderous men bent on bloodshed; within you are those who eat on the mountain shrines and commit acts of indecency. (22:9).
In you they have uncovered the nakedness of their fathers; in you they violate women during their menstrual impurity. (22:10).
One man commits an abomination with his neighbor’s wife; another wickedly defiles his daughter-in-law; and yet another violates his sister, his own father’s daughter. (22:11).
In you they take bribes to shed blood. You engage in usury, take excess interest, and extort your neighbors. But Me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD. (22:12).
Now look, I strike My hands together against your unjust gain and against the blood you have shed in your midst. (22:13).
Will your courage endure or your hands be strong in the day I deal with you? I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will act. (22:14).
I will disperse you among the nations and scatter you throughout the lands; I will purge your uncleanness. (22:15).
And when you have defiled yourself in the eyes of the nations, then you will know that I am the LORD.’” (22:16).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (22:17).
“Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to Me. All of them are copper, tin, iron, and lead inside the furnace; they are but the dross of silver. (22:18).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because all of you have become dross, behold, I will gather you into Jerusalem. (22:19).
Just as one gathers silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin into the furnace to melt with a fiery blast, so I will gather you in My anger and wrath, leave you there, and melt you. (22:20).
Yes, I will gather you together and blow on you with the fire of My wrath, and you will be melted within the city. (22:21).
As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted within the city. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out My wrath upon you.’” (22:22).
And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (22:23).
“Son of man, say to her, ‘In the day of indignation, you are a land that has not been cleansed, upon which no rain has fallen.’ (22:24).
The conspiracy of the princes in her midst is like a roaring lion tearing its prey. They devour the people, seize the treasures and precious things, and multiply the widows within her. (22:25).

Her priests do violence to My law and profane My holy things. They make no distinction between the holy and the common, and they fail to distinguish between the clean and the unclean. They disregard My Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them. (22:26).
Her officials within her are like wolves tearing their prey, shedding blood, and destroying lives for dishonest gain. (22:27).
Her prophets whitewash these deeds by false visions and lying divinations, saying, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ when the LORD has not spoken. (22:28).
The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy and have exploited the foreign resident without justice. (22:29).
I searched for a man among them to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, so that I should not destroy it. But I found no one. (22:30).
So I have poured out My indignation upon them and consumed them with the fire of My fury. I have brought their ways down upon their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.” (22:31).
crossRefs: Leviticus 18:6-20: The forbidden sexual relations listed one by one, the statutes charged in 22:10-11.
Leviticus 19:33-34: Do not mistreat the foreigner living among you, but love him as yourself.
Exodus 22:21-24: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, or God will hear their cry, the charge in 22:7.
Isaiah 59:15-16: The LORD saw that there was no justice and no one to intervene, matching 22:30.
Micah 3:9-11: Rulers who judge for a bribe, priests who teach for a price and prophets who divine for money.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: דָּמִים (damim), Greek (LXX): αἵματα, Aramaic: דמיא
translationNotes.note: Plural form used for violent killings and guilt (22:2-4).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֹמֵד בַּפֶּרֶץ (‘omed baperetz), Greek (LXX): ἑστὼς ἐν τῷ θραύσματι, Aramaic: קאים בפרץ
translationNotes.note: Image of repairing a broken wall / interceding to stop judgment (22:30).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוּר / צָרַף (kur / tsaraf), Greek (LXX): κάμινος / δοκιμάζω, Aramaic: אתון / צרף
translationNotes.note: Refining metaphor for severe judgment (22:18-22).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is charged with bloodshed, sexual crimes, corruption, and oppressive violence; God will refine in the furnace of judgment, and none is found to intercede.

stories.title: 💔 Ezekiel 23
summaryBullets: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (23:1).
“Son of man, there were two women, daughters of the same mother, (23:2).
and they played in Egypt, prostituting themselves from their youth. Their breasts were fondled there, and their virgin bosoms caressed. (23:3).
The older was named Oholah, and her sister was named Oholibah. They became Mine and gave birth to sons and daughters. As for their identities, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem. (23:4).
Oholah prostituted herself while she was still Mine. She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians — warriors (23:5).
clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all desirable young men, horsemen mounted on steeds. (23:6).
She offered sexual favors to all the elite of Assyria. She defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she lusted. (23:7).
She did not give up the prostitution she began in Egypt, when men slept with her in her youth, caressed her virgin bosom, and poured out their lust upon her. (23:8).
Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, the Assyrians for whom she lusted. (23:9).
They exposed her nakedness, seized her sons and daughters, and put her to the sword. Thus she became a byword among women, and they executed judgment against her. (23:10).
Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet in her lust and prostitution she was more depraved than her sister. (23:11).
She too lusted after the Assyrians — governors and commanders, warriors dressed in splendor, horsemen riding on steeds, all desirable young men. (23:12).
And I saw that she too had defiled herself; both of them had taken the same path. (23:13).
But Oholibah carried her prostitution even further. She saw the men portrayed on the wall, images of the Chaldeans, engraved in vermilion, (23:14).
wearing belts on their waists and flowing turbans on their heads; all of them looked like officers of the Babylonians in Chaldea, the land of their birth. (23:15).
At the sight of them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea. (23:16).
Then the Babylonians came to her, to the bed of love, and in their lust they defiled her. But after she had been defiled by them, she turned away in disgust. (23:17).
When Oholibah openly prostituted herself and exposed her nakedness, I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister. (23:18).
Yet she multiplied her promiscuity, remembering the days of her youth, when she had prostituted herself in the land of Egypt (23:19).
and lusted after their lovers, whose genitals were like those of donkeys and whose emission was like that of stallions. (23:20).
So you revisited the indecency of your youth, when the Egyptians caressed your bosom and pressed your young breasts. (23:21).
Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will incite your lovers against you, those from whom you turned away in disgust. And I will bring them against you from every side — (23:22).

the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, the men of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them— all desirable young men, governors and commanders, officers and men of renown, mounted on horses. (23:23).

They will come against you with a host of peoples, with weapons, chariots, and wagons. They will array themselves against you on every side with buckler and shield and helmet. I will delegate judgment to them, and they will punish you according to their own standards. (23:24).

And I will set My jealous rage against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your noses and ears, and your survivors will fall by the sword. They will seize your sons and daughters, and your remnant will be consumed by fire. (23:25).
They will strip off your clothes and take your fine jewelry. (23:26).
So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt, and you will not lift your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.’ (23:27).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Surely I will deliver you into the hands of those you hate, from whom you turned away in disgust. (23:28).
They will treat you with hatred, take all for which you have worked, and leave you naked and bare, so that the shame of your prostitution will be exposed. Your indecency and promiscuity (23:29).
have brought these things upon you, because you have prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols. (23:30).
Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.’ (23:31).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You will drink your sister’s cup, a cup deep and wide. It will bring scorn and derision, for it holds so much. (23:32).
You will be filled with drunkenness and grief, with a cup of devastation and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria. (23:33).
You will drink it and drain it; you will dash it to pieces, and tear your breasts. For I have spoken,’ declares the Lord GOD. (23:34).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your indecency and prostitution.’” (23:35).
Then the LORD said to me: “Son of man, will you pass judgment against Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations. (23:36).

For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols. They have even sacrificed their children, whom they bore to Me, in the fire as food for their idols. (23:37).
They have also done this to Me: On that very same day, they defiled My sanctuary and profaned My Sabbaths. (23:38).
On the very day they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered My sanctuary to profane it. Yes, they did this inside My house. (23:39).
Furthermore, you sisters sent messengers for men who came from afar; and behold, when they arrived, you bathed for them, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry. (23:40).
You sat on a couch of luxury with a table spread before it, on which you had set My incense and My oil, (23:41).
accompanied by the sound of a carefree crowd. Drunkards were brought in from the desert along with men from the rabble, who put bracelets on your wrists and beautiful crowns on your head. (23:42).
Then I said of her who had grown old in adulteries: ‘Now let them use her as a prostitute, for that is all she is!’ (23:43).
And they slept with her as with a prostitute; they slept with Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women. (23:44).
But righteous men will sentence them to the punishment of those who commit adultery and bloodshed, because they are adulteresses with blood on their hands. (23:45).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Bring a mob against them and consign them to terror and plunder. (23:46).
The mob will stone them and cut them down with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn down their houses. (23:47).
So I will put an end to indecency in the land, and all the women will be admonished not to imitate your behavior. (23:48).
They will repay you for your indecency, and you will bear the consequences of your sins of idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’” (23:49).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 17:6-18: Fall of Samaria and its sins.
2 Kings 25:1-12: Fall of Jerusalem to Babylon.
Jeremiah 3:6-11: Faithless Israel and treacherous Judah.
Hosea 2:2-13: Idolatry pictured as adultery.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָהֳלָה (‘Oholah, “Her tent”) / אָהֳלִיבָה (‘Oholibah, “My tent is in her”), Greek (LXX): Οολά / Οολιβά, Aramaic: אהלא / אהלי בה
translationNotes.note: Names explain the allegory: Samaria (its own tent) vs. Jerusalem (God’s tent/temple in her).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: זָנָה (zanah), Greek (LXX): πορνεία, Aramaic: זנה
translationNotes.note: Metaphor for covenant unfaithfulness with other gods and nations throughout ch. 23.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גִּלָּה עֶרְוָה (gillāh ‘ervah), Greek (LXX): ἀπεκάλυψαν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην, Aramaic: גלוי ערותא
translationNotes.note: Public shame and sexual violence imagery used for conquest (23:10) (23:18) (23:29).

The central highland region between Judea and Galilee; capital of the northern kingdom of Israel from 880 BC until Assyrian deportation in 722 BC. The mixed-population descendants who remained ('Samaritans') were despised by Judeans as ethnically and religiously impure. Jesus' choice to travel through Samaria (John 4) and to make a Samaritan the hero of His parable (Luke 10) deliberately upends that prejudice.

stories.keyTakeaway: Two sisters, Oholah who is Samaria and Oholibah who is Jerusalem, prostitute themselves with Assyria, Babylon, and Egypt, defiling themselves with idols and sacrificing their children in the fire; God rouses their former lovers against them to strip and mutilate them, seize their sons and daughters, stone them and cut them down with swords, and burn their houses, putting an end to lewdness in the land.

stories.title: 🍲 Ezekiel 24
summaryBullets: In the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (24:1).
“Son of man, write down today’s date, for on this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem. (24:2).
Now speak a parable to this rebellious house and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Put the pot on the fire; put it on and pour in the water. (24:3).
Put in the pieces of meat, every good piece— thigh and shoulder — fill it with choice bones. (24:4).
Take the choicest of the flock and pile the fuel beneath it. Bring it to a boil and cook the bones in it.’ (24:5).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot now rusted, whose rust will not come off! Empty it piece by piece; cast no lots for its contents. (24:6).
For the blood she shed is still within her; she poured it out on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust. (24:7).
In order to stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have placed her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.’ (24:8).
Yes, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Woe to the city of bloodshed! I, too, will pile the kindling high. (24:9).
Pile on the logs and kindle the fire; cook the meat well and mix in the spices; let the bones be burned. (24:10).
Set the empty pot on its coals until it becomes hot and its copper glows. Then its impurity will melt within; its rust will be consumed. (24:11).
It has frustrated every effort; its thick rust has not been removed, even by the fire. (24:12).
Because of the indecency of your uncleanness I tried to cleanse you, but you would not be purified from your filthiness. You will not be pure again until My wrath against you has subsided. (24:13).
I, the LORD, have spoken; the time is coming, and I will act. I will not refrain or show pity, nor will I relent. I will judge you according to your ways and deeds,’ declares the Lord GOD.” (24:14).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (24:15).
“Son of man, behold, I am about to take away the desire of your eyes with a fatal blow. But you must not mourn or weep or let your tears flow. (24:16).
Groan quietly; do not mourn for the dead. Put on your turban and strap your sandals on your feet; do not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners.” (24:17).
So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. And the next morning I did as I had been commanded. (24:18).
Then the people asked me, “Won’t you tell us what these things you are doing mean to us?” (24:19).
So I answered them, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (24:20).

Tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I am about to desecrate My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and the delight of your soul. And the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.’ (24:21).
Then you will do as I have done: You will not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners. (24:22).
Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your sins, and you will groan among yourselves. (24:23).
‘Thus Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do everything that he has done. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’ (24:24).
And you, son of man, know that on the day I take away their stronghold, their pride and joy — the desire of their eyes which uplifted their souls — and their sons and daughters as well, (24:25).
on that day a fugitive will come and tell you the news. (24:26).
On that day your mouth will be opened to him who has escaped; you will speak and no longer be mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD.” (24:27).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 25:1-4: The siege begins on the tenth day of the tenth month, the day 24:1-2 records from Babylonia.
Ezekiel 11:3-11: The cooking pot slogan the men of Jerusalem used, taken up here and boiled dry.
Leviticus 17:13: Blood poured out and covered with earth, the opposite of the exposed blood in 24:7-8.
Leviticus 21:1-4: A priest may not defile himself for the dead except for his nearest kin, the background to 24:16-17.
Jeremiah 16:5-7: No mourning, no comfort and no funeral meal, the same sign given to another prophet.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֶלְאָה (ḥel’āh), Greek (LXX): ἰὸς / ρύπος, Aramaic: חליותא
translationNotes.note: Image for deep, stubborn guilt that fire must consume (24:6) (24:11-12).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַחְמַד עֵינֶיךָ (maḥmad ‘eineikha), Greek (LXX): τὰ ἐπιθυμήματα τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου, Aramaic: מחמד עיניך
translationNotes.note: Tender phrase for Ezekiel’s wife (24:16-25).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹת (’ot), Greek (LXX): σημεῖον, Aramaic: אתא
translationNotes.note: Ezekiel’s acted message, no public mourning, interprets the coming shock (24:24).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is a filthy pot set to boil and burn; Ezekiel’s silent grief over his wife is a sign that the people will lose the temple and be unable to mourn in the usual ways.

headings.text: The Parable of the Cooking Pot

stories.title: 🌍 Ezekiel 25
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (25:1).
“Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them. (25:2).

Tell the Ammonites to hear the word of the Lord GOD, for this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you exclaimed, “Aha!” when My sanctuary was profaned, when the land of Israel was laid waste, and when the house of Judah went into exile, (25:3).
therefore I will indeed give you as a possession to the people of the East. They will set up their camps and pitch their tents among you. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk. (25:4).
I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels, and Ammon a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’ (25:5).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you clapped your hands and stomped your feet and rejoiced over the land of Israel with a heart full of contempt, (25:6).

therefore I will indeed stretch out My hand against you and give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and exterminate you from the countries. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD.’ (25:7).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because Moab and Seir said, “Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,” (25:8).
therefore I will indeed expose the flank of Moab beginning with its frontier cities — Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim — the glory of the land. (25:9).
I will give it along with the Ammonites as a possession to the people of the East, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations. (25:10).
So I will execute judgments on Moab, and they will know that I am the LORD.’ (25:11).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and in so doing incurred grievous guilt, (25:12).

therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will stretch out My hand against Edom and cut off from it both man and beast. I will make it a wasteland, and from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword. (25:13).
I will take My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel, and they will deal with Edom according to My anger and wrath. Then they will know My vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.’ (25:14).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because the Philistines acted in vengeance, taking vengeance with malice of soul to destroy Judah with ancient hostility, (25:15).
therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I will stretch out My hand against the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast. (25:16).
I will execute great vengeance against them with furious reproof. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay My vengeance upon them.’” (25:17).
crossRefs: Amos 1:13-15: Oracle against Ammon for ripping open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge its border.
Obadiah 1:10-14: Edom standing aside on the day of Jacob's calamity, and looting in the day of disaster.
Zephaniah 2:8-11: Moab and Ammon reproved for their taunts and their boasting against the LORD's people.
Jeremiah 40:13-14: Baalis king of the Ammonites sends Ishmael to assassinate the governor of Judah.
Psalm 137:7: Remember the Edomites, who cried tear it down to its foundations on the day Jerusalem fell.

translationNotes.note: A general name for the tribes of the desert east and southeast of the Jordan, the Arabian frontier. Verses 4 and 10 hand Ammon and Moab to them: their tents pitched on the land, their herds eating the crops. It is not conquest by an empire but the slow loss of settled farmland to nomads, which is what happened to the transjordan plateau.

Verse 3 quotes Ammon saying Aha over the temple when it was profaned, over the land when it was made desolate, and over Judah when it went into exile. Each of the four oracles in this chapter turns on what a neighbour said or did while Judah fell, so the charge is not conquest but gloating.

A group closely tied to the Philistines and named alongside them in 1 Samuel 30:14 and Zephaniah 2:5. David's personal bodyguard was drawn from the Cherethites and Pelethites, in 2 Samuel 8:18 and 15:18, so foreign soldiers from this coastal people served the kings of Judah. Verse 16 names them for judgment with the Philistines.

Verses 12-17 use the word for both sides. Edom and Philistia took vengeance on Judah with an old hatred, and God says He will take vengeance on them. In Hebrew usage the word covers the legal repayment owed for blood, not merely private spite; Deuteronomy 32:35 reserves it to God.

stories.keyTakeaway: Neighboring nations that mocked, plundered, or took revenge against Judah will themselves be invaded, depopulated, and judged.

stories.title: 🚢 Ezekiel 26
summaryBullets: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (26:1).
“Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, ‘Aha! The gate to the nations is broken; it has swung open to me; now that she lies in ruins I will be filled,’ (26:2).
therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, O Tyre, I am against you, and I will raise up many nations against you, as the sea brings up its waves. (26:3).
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and demolish her towers. I will scrape the soil from her and make her a bare rock. (26:4).
She will become a place to spread nets in the sea, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. She will become plunder for the nations, (26:5).
and the villages on her mainland will be slain by the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’ (26:6).

For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I will bring against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses and chariots, with cavalry and a great company of troops. (26:7).
He will slaughter the villages of your mainland with the sword; he will set up siege works against you, build a ramp to your walls, and raise his shields against you. (26:8).
He will direct the blows of his battering rams against your walls and tear down your towers with his axes. (26:9).
His multitude of horses will cover you in their dust. When he enters your gates as an army entering a breached city, your walls will shake from the noise of cavalry, wagons, and chariots. (26:10).
The hooves of his horses will trample all your streets. He will slaughter your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground. (26:11).
They will plunder your wealth and pillage your merchandise. They will demolish your walls, tear down your beautiful homes, and throw your stones and timber and soil into the water. (26:12).
So I will silence the sound of your songs, and the music of your lyres will no longer be heard. (26:13).
I will make you a bare rock, and you will become a place to spread the fishing nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.’ (26:14).
This is what the Lord GOD says to Tyre: ‘Will not the coastlands quake at the sound of your downfall, when the wounded groan at the slaughter in your midst? (26:15).

All the princes of the sea will descend from their thrones, remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. Clothed with terror, they will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled over you. (26:16).

Then they will lament for you, saying, “How you have perished, O city of renown inhabited by seafaring men— she who was powerful on the sea, along with her people, who imposed terror on all peoples! (26:17).
Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your downfall; the islands in the sea are dismayed by your demise.”’ (26:18).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘When I make you a desolate city like other deserted cities, and when I raise up the deep against you so that the mighty waters cover you, (26:19).

then I will bring you down with those who descend to the Pit, to the people of antiquity. I will make you dwell in the earth below like the ancient ruins, with those who descend to the Pit, so that you will no longer be inhabited or set in splendor in the land of the living. (26:20).
I will make you an object of horror, and you will be no more. You will be sought, but will never be found,’ declares the Lord GOD.” (26:21).
crossRefs: Isaiah 23:1-18: The parallel oracle against Tyre, with the ships of Tarshish told to wail.
Jeremiah 25:15-22: The cup of wrath passed to the kings of Tyre and Sidon among the nations.
Ezekiel 29:17-20: Nebuchadnezzar's army worn out at Tyre for no wages, and given Egypt instead.
Amos 1:9-10: Tyre condemned for handing over a whole population to Edom and forgetting a covenant of brothers.
Revelation 18:11-19: Merchants and sea captains standing off and mourning a fallen trading power.

translationNotes.note: The name means rock, and the city was built on one. Tyre had two parts: a mainland town on the Phoenician coast, and the real stronghold on a rocky island roughly half a mile (800 m) offshore, with a harbour on each side. Attackers could take the mainland and still be looking at a walled island across open water, which is why Tyre outlasted sieges that flattened everything else on the coast.

Nebuchadnezzar besieged Tyre for thirteen years, a figure Josephus gives in Against Apion 1.21 citing Phoenician records. Ezekiel 29:18 describes what that cost his army: every head rubbed bald and every shoulder raw from hauling siege materials, and no wages from Tyre at the end of it. The mainland fell; the island did not surrender to him.

translationNotes.term: A bare rock for spreading nets
translationNotes.note: Verses 4-5 and 14 say the soil will be scraped off and the place left as bare rock where fishermen dry their nets. That is not poetry about desolation in general; it is the specific afterlife of a stripped coastal site. Nets were spread on flat rock to dry and be mended, and the verse describes a commercial superpower's ground put to the humblest use on the shore.

translationNotes.term: Stones, timber and soil thrown into the water
translationNotes.note: Verse 12 describes the rubble of the city being dumped into the sea. In 332 BC Alexander the Great, unable to reach the island, had his engineers build a causeway out to it from the mainland using the debris of the mainland town, and took the island after seven months. The causeway silted up over the centuries, and Tyre has been joined to the shore ever since.

translationNotes.term: Princes of the sea coming down from their thrones
translationNotes.note: Verse 16 has the rulers of the coastal cities step off their thrones, take off their robes and embroidered garments, and sit on the ground shaking. Sitting on the ground, stripped of the marks of office, was the recognised posture of mourning; Job's friends do it in Job 2:13. These are trading partners watching their market collapse.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tyre’s pride at Jerusalem’s ruin brings its own ruin; siege, demolition, and a shoreline scraped clean like bare rock.

stories.title: ⛵ Ezekiel 27
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (27:1).
“Now you, son of man, take up a lament for Tyre. (27:2).
Tell Tyre, who dwells at the gateway to the sea, merchant of the peoples on many coasts, that this is what the Lord GOD says: You have said, O Tyre, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’ (27:3).
Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders perfected your beauty. (27:4).
They constructed all your planking with cypress from Senir. They took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you. (27:5).
Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; of wood from the coasts of Cyprus they made your deck, inlaid with ivory. (27:6).
Of embroidered fine linen from Egypt they made your sail, which served as your banner. Of blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah they made your awning. (27:7).
The men of Sidon and Arvad were your oarsmen. Your men of skill, O Tyre, were there as your captains. (27:8).
The elders of Gebal were aboard as shipwrights, repairing your leaks. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came alongside to barter for your merchandise. (27:9).
Men of Persia, Lydia, and Put served as warriors in your army. They hung their shields and helmets on your walls; they gave you splendor. (27:10).
Men of Arvad and Helech manned your walls all around, and the men of Gammad were in your towers. They hung their shields around your walls; they perfected your beauty. (27:11).
Tarshish was your merchant because of your great wealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares. (27:12).
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants. They exchanged slaves and bronze utensils for your merchandise. (27:13).
The men of Beth-togarmah exchanged horses, war horses, and mules for your wares. (27:14).
The men of Dedan were your clients; many coastlands were your market; they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony. (27:15).
Aram was your customer because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your wares. (27:16).
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, cakes and honey, oil and balm for your merchandise. (27:17).
Because of your many products and your great wealth of goods, Damascus traded with you wine from Helbon, wool from Zahar, (27:18).
and casks of wine from Izal for your wares. Wrought iron, cassia, and sweet cane were exchanged for your merchandise. (27:19).
Dedan was your merchant in saddlecloths for riding. (27:20).
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers, trading in lambs, rams, and goats. (27:21).
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; for your wares they exchanged gold, the finest of all spices, and precious stones. (27:22).
Haran, Canneh, and Eden traded with you, and so did the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad. (27:23).
In your marketplace they traded with you fine garments of blue, embroidered work, and multicolored rugs with cords tightly twisted and knotted. (27:24).
The ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise. And you were filled with heavy cargo in the heart of the sea. (27:25).
Your oarsmen have brought you onto the high seas, but the east wind will shatter you in the heart of the sea. (27:26).

Your wealth, wares, and merchandise, your sailors, captains, and shipwrights, your merchants and all the warriors within you, with all the other people on board, will sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your downfall. (27:27).
The countryside will shake when your sailors cry out. (27:28).
All who handle the oars will abandon their ships. The sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore. (27:29).
They will raise their voices for you and cry out bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes. (27:30).
They will shave their heads for you and wrap themselves in sackcloth. They will weep over you with anguish of soul and bitter mourning. (27:31).
As they wail and mourn over you, they will take up a lament for you: ‘Who was ever like Tyre, silenced in the middle of the sea? (27:32).
When your wares went out to sea, you satisfied many nations. You enriched the kings of the earth with your abundant wealth and merchandise. (27:33).
Now you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and the people among you have gone down with you. (27:34).
All the people of the coastlands are appalled over you. Their kings shudder with fear; their faces are contorted. (27:35).
Those who trade among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end and will be no more.’” (27:36).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 26:1-14: The oracle against Tyre that this funeral song follows.
1 Kings 5:1-12: Hiram of Tyre supplies cedar, cypress and skilled men to Solomon, the same trade at its height.
1 Kings 10:22: A fleet of trading ships returning every three years with gold, silver, ivory, apes and baboons.
Isaiah 23:8-9: Tyre's merchants called princes and her traders the honoured of the earth.
Revelation 18:11-13: A long cargo list of luxury goods, ending with the bodies and souls of men.

translationNotes.note: Verses 5-7 build Tyre as a ship out of imports, and every item is a real trade route. Planks of cypress from Senir, which is Mount Hermon; a mast of cedar from Lebanon; oars from the oaks of Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee; a deck of pine inlaid with ivory from the coasts of Cyprus; a sail of embroidered Egyptian linen used as the ship's colours; and an awning of blue and purple cloth from Elishah. Nothing in the vessel is local except the skill.

The blue and purple of 27:7 and 27:16 was Phoenicia's signature product, extracted from a gland in murex sea snails. It took thousands of shells to make a few grams of dye, and mounds of crushed murex shells still lie at Tyre and Sidon. The cloth was so costly that purple marked royalty across the ancient world, and the trade was still running in the New Testament: Lydia of Thyatira in Acts 16:14 is a dealer in purple cloth.

translationNotes.term: The trade list, region by region
translationNotes.note: Verses 12-24 read like a customs ledger. Tarshish in the far west sends silver, iron, tin and lead. Javan, Tubal and Meshech in Anatolia and Greece trade slaves and bronze vessels. Beth-togarmah sends horses, war horses and mules. Dedan brings ivory tusks and ebony; Aram turquoise, purple, embroidery, fine linen, coral and rubies. Judah and Israel supply wheat from Minnith, cakes, honey, oil and balm. Damascus sends wine of Helbon and wool. Arabia and Kedar drive in lambs, rams and goats. Sheba and Raamah bring gold, the finest spices and precious stones.

Verse 9 names the elders and skilled men of Gebal as the ones who sealed the ship's seams. Gebal is Byblos, a Phoenician port north of Beirut, and its craftsmen worked on Solomon's temple according to 1 Kings 5:18. Caulking meant driving fibre and pitch into the plank joints to make a hull watertight, which is the job every wooden ship depends on.

Verse 13 lists what Javan, Tubal and Meshech brought to market: human beings and bronze vessels, in the same clause. The Hebrew reads persons of men. Amos 1:9 charges Tyre with delivering an entire population into slavery. The trade list does not separate people from goods, and neither does the charge.

translationNotes.term: The ship broken in the heart of the seas
translationNotes.note: Verses 26-36 end the lament by sinking the vessel with everything aboard: rowers, pilots, caulkers, merchants and soldiers, plus the whole cargo. Verses 30-32 describe the mourning of the coastal traders in detail, dust on the head, rolling in ashes, shaved heads, sackcloth. The chapter is a funeral song for an economy.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tyre’s global trading glory is portrayed as a splendid ship that breaks and sinks; its goods, sailors, and reputation lost to the deep.

stories.title: 👑 Ezekiel 28
summaryBullets: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (28:1).

“Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre that this is what the Lord GOD says: Your heart is proud, and you have said, ‘I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the sea.’ Yet you are a man and not a god, though you have regarded your heart as that of a god. (28:2).
Behold, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you! (28:3).
By your wisdom and understanding you have gained your wealth and amassed gold and silver for your treasuries. (28:4).
By your great skill in trading you have increased your wealth, but your heart has grown proud because of it. (28:5).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you regard your heart as the heart of a god, (28:6).
behold, I will bring foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and will defile your splendor. (28:7).
They will bring you down to the Pit, and you will die a violent death in the heart of the seas. (28:8).
Will you still say, ‘I am a god,’ in the presence of those who slay you? You will be only a man, not a god, in the hands of those who wound you. (28:9).
You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners. For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.” (28:10).
Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (28:11).
“Son of man, take up a lament for the king of Tyre and tell him that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty. (28:12).

You were in Eden, the garden of God. Every kind of precious stone adorned you: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald. Your mountings and settings were crafted in gold, prepared on the day of your creation. (28:13).
You were anointed as a guardian cherub, for I had ordained you. You were on the holy mountain of God; you walked among the fiery stones. (28:14).
From the day you were created you were blameless in your ways— until wickedness was found in you. (28:15).

By the vastness of your trade, you were filled with violence, and you sinned. So I drove you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I banished you, O guardian cherub, from among the fiery stones. (28:16).
Your heart grew proud of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom because of your splendor; so I cast you to the earth; I made you a spectacle before kings. (28:17).

By the multitude of your iniquities and the dishonesty of your trading you have profaned your sanctuaries. So I made fire come from within you, and it consumed you. I reduced you to ashes on the ground in the eyes of all who saw you. (28:18).
All the nations who know you are appalled over you. You have come to a horrible end and will be no more.’” (28:19).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (28:20).
“Son of man, set your face against Sidon and prophesy against her. (28:21).

And you are to declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I am against you, O Sidon, and I will be glorified within you. They will know that I am the LORD when I execute judgments against her and demonstrate My holiness through her. (28:22).
I will send a plague against her and shed blood in her streets; the slain will fall within her, while the sword is against her on every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD. (28:23).
For the people of Israel will no longer face a pricking brier or a painful thorn from all around them who treat them with contempt. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.’ (28:24).

This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, I will show Myself holy among them in the sight of the nations. Then they will dwell in their own land, which I have given to My servant Jacob. (28:25).

And there they will dwell securely, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell securely when I execute judgments against all those around them who treat them with contempt. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.’” (28:26).
crossRefs: Isaiah 14:12-15: Taunt over a proud king cast down.
Ezekiel 27:1-36: Tyre’s trade and glory pictured as a ship.
Obadiah 1:3-4: Pride brought down.
Amos 1:9-10: Word against Tyre.

translationNotes.note: The chapter uses two different titles for two different oracles. Verses 1-10 address the nagid, the ruler or prince, and the charge is that he claims to be a god while being a man, which 28:9 answers by pointing at his death. Verses 11-19 shift to the melekh, the king, and become a lament using the language of Eden and a guardian cherub. The change of word marks the change of speech.

Verse 3 taunts the ruler of Tyre with being wiser than Daniel, and 14:14 and 14:20 name the same figure alongside Noah and Job as a byword for righteousness. Daniel was a contemporary, taken to Babylon in 605 BC and already famous at the Babylonian court for interpreting what nobody else could, which is exactly the reputation the taunt trades on.

translationNotes.term: Sitting in the seat of gods in the heart of the seas
translationNotes.note: Verse 2 puts the boast in the ruler's own mouth: I am a god, I sit in the seat of gods, in the heart of the seas. The island city with water on every side made that claim look literal. Verse 8 supplies the answer in the same terms, that he will die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas.

Verse 13 lists nine gems as the covering of the king of Tyre, all of which appear among the twelve on the high priest's breastpiece in Exodus 28:17-20. The verse also mentions his settings and mountings of gold, prepared on the day he was created. It is jeweller's language, applied to a trading city whose wealth was worn.

The older of the two great Phoenician ports, about twenty-five miles (40 km) up the coast from Tyre, named for the fishing that gave it its name. Genesis 10:15 lists Sidon as the firstborn of Canaan, and Jezebel in 1 Kings 16:31 was a Sidonian king's daughter who brought Baal worship into Israel with her. Verses 20-24 give Sidon its own short oracle after the long one against Tyre.

Verse 24 closes the whole run of oracles against the nations around Israel, chapters 25 to 32, with an image from clearing ground. Numbers 33:55 warned that the peoples left in the land would be barbs in Israel's eyes and thorns in her sides. Verses 25-26 then promise a return where the people build houses and plant vineyards and live securely.

stories.keyTakeaway: Tyre’s arrogant ruler is told he is mortal and will be killed. A lament pictures the king’s rise and violent fall using Eden and cherub language. Sidon is judged, and Israel is promised secure return.
