A Lament for the King of Tyre

stories.title: 🐊 Ezekiel 29
summaryBullets: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (29:1).
“Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt. (29:2).

Speak to him and tell him that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Pharaoh king of Egypt, O great monster who lies among his rivers, who says, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it myself.’ (29:3).

But I will put hooks in your jaws and cause the fish of your streams to cling to your scales. I will haul you up out of your rivers, and all the fish of your streams will cling to your scales. (29:4).

I will leave you in the desert, you and all the fish of your streams. You will fall on the open field and will not be taken away or gathered for burial. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the air. (29:5).
Then all the people of Egypt will know that I am the LORD. For you were only a staff of reeds to the house of Israel. (29:6).
When Israel took hold of you with their hands, you splintered, tearing all their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke, and their backs were wrenched. (29:7).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will bring a sword against you and cut off from you man and beast. (29:8).
The land of Egypt will become a desolate wasteland. Then they will know that I am the LORD. Because you said, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it,’ (29:9).
therefore I am against you and against your rivers. I will turn the land of Egypt into a ruin, a desolate wasteland from Migdol to Syene, and as far as the border of Cush. (29:10).
No foot of man or beast will pass through, and it will be uninhabited for forty years. (29:11).

I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and her cities will lie desolate for forty years among the ruined cities. And I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries. (29:12).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations to which they were scattered. (29:13).
I will restore Egypt from captivity and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin. There they will be a lowly kingdom. (29:14).
Egypt will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again exalt itself above the nations. For I will diminish Egypt so that it will never again rule over the nations. (29:15).
Egypt will never again be an object of trust for the house of Israel, but will remind them of their iniquity in turning to the Egyptians. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.” (29:16).
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (29:17).

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to labor strenuously against Tyre. Every head was made bald and every shoulder made raw. But he and his army received no wages from Tyre for the labor they expended on it. (29:18).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who will carry off its wealth, seize its spoil, and remove its plunder. This will be the wages for his army. (29:19).
I have given him the land of Egypt as the reward for his labor, because it was done for Me, declares the Lord GOD. (29:20).
In that day I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth to speak among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.” (29:21).
crossRefs: Isaiah 19:1-15: Oracle against Egypt.
Jeremiah 46:2-26: Egypt’s defeat under Nebuchadnezzar.
Exodus 7:17-18: Nile struck (river theme).
Ezekiel 26:7: Nebuchadnezzar named as God’s instrument.

translationNotes.note: The word covers any great river or sea beast; here it is the Nile crocodile, up to sixteen feet (5 m) long and the most dangerous animal in Egypt. Verse 3 has Pharaoh lying in the middle of his own river channels saying the Nile is mine, I made it, and 29:4 puts hooks in his jaws and drags him out onto dry land with the fish of his river stuck to his scales.

Verses 6-7 say Egypt was a reed staff to Israel: taken hold of, it splintered and tore the hand; leaned on, it snapped and wrenched the back. Nile reeds grow tall and look like a walking staff and will not hold weight. The Assyrian field commander uses the identical taunt about Egypt in 2 Kings 18:21 and Isaiah 36:6.

Verse 10 measures Egypt end to end. Migdol is a frontier fort in the northeast delta, on the road in from Canaan. Syene is Aswan at the first cataract of the Nile, the southern border with Cush, some six hundred miles (950 km) upriver. It is the same span as saying the whole country.

Verses 11-13 set a term of forty years for Egypt's desolation and the scattering of its people, followed by a gathering back and a restoration as a lowly kingdom that will never again rule the nations. Forty is the number of the wilderness years in Numbers 14:34. The chapter states both the sentence and its end.

Verses 17-20 are dated to the twenty-seventh year, about 571 BC, the latest date in the book. God says Nebuchadnezzar's army laboured against Tyre until every head was bald and every shoulder rubbed raw and got no wages for it, so Egypt is given to him as the payment. It is a blunt piece of accounting, and it treats the Babylonian king as a contractor being settled up.

stories.keyTakeaway: Pharaoh is pictured as a crocodile-like monster dragged from the Nile. Egypt faces ruin, forty years of scattering, later reduced status, and is handed to Babylon as payment.

stories.title: 🌩️ Ezekiel 30
summaryBullets: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (30:1).
“Son of man, prophesy and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Wail, ‘Alas for that day!’ (30:2).
For the day is near, the Day of the LORD is near. It will be a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations. (30:3).
A sword will come against Egypt, and there will be anguish in Cush when the slain fall in Egypt, its wealth is taken away, and its foundations are torn down. (30:4).
Cush, Put, and Lud, and all the various peoples, as well as Libya and the men of the covenant land, will fall with Egypt by the sword. (30:5).
For this is what the LORD says: The allies of Egypt will fall, and her proud strength will collapse. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within her, declares the Lord GOD. (30:6).
They will be desolate among desolate lands, and their cities will lie among ruined cities. (30:7).
Then they will know that I am the LORD when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are shattered. (30:8).
On that day messengers will go out from Me in ships to frighten Cush out of complacency. Anguish will come upon them on the day of Egypt’s doom. For it is indeed coming. (30:9).
This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to the hordes of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. (30:10).
He and his people with him, the most ruthless of the nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain. (30:11).
I will make the streams dry up and sell the land to the wicked. By the hands of foreigners I will bring desolation upon the land and everything in it. I, the LORD, have spoken. (30:12).
This is what the Lord GOD says: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince in Egypt, and I will instill fear in that land. (30:13).
I will lay waste Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgment on Thebes. (30:14).
I will pour out My wrath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the crowds of Thebes. (30:15).
I will set fire to Egypt, Pelusium will writhe in anguish, Thebes will be split open, and Memphis will face daily distress. (30:16).
The young men of On and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and those cities will go into captivity. (30:17).
The day will be darkened in Tahpanhes when I break the yoke of Egypt and her proud strength comes to an end. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity. (30:18).
So I will execute judgment on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD.” (30:19).
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (30:20).
“Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. See, it has not been bound up for healing, or splinted for strength to hold the sword. (30:21).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break his arms, both the strong one and the one already broken, and will make the sword fall from his hand. (30:22).
I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands. (30:23).
I will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king and place My sword in his hand, but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, who will groan before him like a mortally wounded man. (30:24).

I will strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall limp. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I place My sword in the hand of Babylon’s king, and he wields it against the land of Egypt. (30:25).
I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.” (30:26).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 46:2-12: Egypt’s defeat.
Isaiah 20:3-6: Sign against Egypt and Cush.
Nahum 3:8-10: No-Amon (Thebes) falls.
Ezekiel 29:19-20: Egypt as Babylon’s wages.

translationNotes.note: Verses 13-18 walk up and down the country. Memphis, called Noph, is the old capital at the head of the delta near modern Cairo. Zoan is Tanis in the northeast delta. Thebes, called No, is the great southern religious capital four hundred miles (640 km) upriver. Sin is the fortress of Pelusium on the eastern frontier; On is Heliopolis, centre of sun worship; Pi-beseth is Bubastis; Tehaphnehes is the border post Jeremiah was carried to in Jeremiah 43:7.

Upper Egypt, the long southern stretch of the Nile valley above the delta. The name comes from Egyptian and means the southern land. Egypt was always two countries administratively, the delta in the north and the valley in the south, which is why Pathros is listed separately from Egypt in 29:14, 30:14 and Jeremiah 44:1.

Verse 5 lists Egypt's allies and mercenaries. Cush is the kingdom on the Nile south of Egypt, in modern Sudan. Put is on the North African coast west of Egypt. Lud supplied bowmen, named as archers in Jeremiah 46:9 and Isaiah 66:19. Egypt fought its late wars largely with hired foreign troops, and the verse says they fall with her.

Verses 21-24 use the arm as the seat of military strength, and describe a fracture that is not set or splinted so it cannot hold a sword again. Verse 22 breaks both arms, the strong one and the one already broken. The already-broken arm is a plain reference to Hophra's failed relief march on Jerusalem, recorded in Jeremiah 37:5-8.

Verse 3 announces a day near at hand, a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations. The phrase is used across the prophets, in Joel 2:1-2, Amos 5:18-20 and Zephaniah 1:14-18, for a decisive intervention. Here it is applied to a specific historical event, Babylon's campaign against Egypt, rather than to the end of all things.

stories.keyTakeaway: Egypt and its partner nations collapse under Babylon’s sword. Cities fall, idols fail, Pharaoh’s power is broken, and Egypt is scattered.

stories.title: 🌲 Ezekiel 31
summaryBullets: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (31:1).
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: ‘Who can be compared to your greatness? (31:2).
Look at Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches that shaded the forest. It towered on high; its top was among the clouds. (31:3).
The waters made it grow; the deep springs made it tall, directing their streams all around its base and sending their channels to all the trees of the field. (31:4).
Therefore it towered higher than all the trees of the field. Its branches multiplied, and its boughs grew long as it spread them out because of the abundant waters. (31:5).
All the birds of the air nested in its branches, and all the beasts of the field gave birth beneath its boughs; all the great nations lived in its shade. (31:6).
It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its limbs, for its roots extended to abundant waters. (31:7).

The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it; the cypresses could not compare with its branches, nor the plane trees match its boughs. No tree in the garden of God could compare with its beauty. (31:8).
I made it beautiful with its many branches, the envy of all the trees of Eden, which were in the garden of God.’ (31:9).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Since it became great in height and set its top among the clouds, and it grew proud on account of its height, (31:10).
I delivered it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, for him to deal with it according to its wickedness. I have banished it. (31:11).

Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches have fallen on the mountains and in every valley; its boughs lay broken in all the earth’s ravines. And all the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it. (31:12).
All the birds of the air nested on its fallen trunk, and all the beasts of the field lived among its boughs. (31:13).

This happened so that no other trees by the waters would become great in height and set their tops among the clouds, and no other well-watered trees would reach them in height. For they have all been consigned to death, to the depths of the earth, among the mortals who descend to the Pit.’ (31:14).

This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘On the day it was brought down to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the deep because of it; I held back its rivers; its abundant waters were restrained. I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it. (31:15).

I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who descend to the Pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the well-watered trees, were consoled in the earth below. (31:16).
They too descended with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword. As its allies they had lived in its shade among the nations. (31:17).

Who then is like you in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? You also will be brought down to the depths of the earth to be with the trees of Eden. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD.’” (31:18).
crossRefs: Isaiah 10:12-19: Assyria’s pride judged.
Daniel 4:10-14: A great tree cut down (parallel image).
Ezekiel 32:18-32: Nations in Sheol.
Genesis 2:8-10: Eden and waters (imagery backdrop).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תְּהוֹם (tehom), Greek (LXX): ἄβυσσος, Aramaic: תהומא
translationNotes.note: Source that made the cedar flourish (31:4).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל / בּוֹר (She’ol / bor), Greek (LXX): ᾅδης / λάκκος, Aramaic: שאולא / בורא
translationNotes.note: Realm of the dead to which the great tree descends (31:15-17).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲרֵלִים (ʿarelim), Greek (LXX): ἀπερικέριστοι, Aramaic: ערילין
translationNotes.note: Group designation for the dishonored dead in these laments (31:18).

The Old Testament realm of the dead; a shadowy underworld where both righteous and wicked descend (Genesis 37:35; Psalm 16:10). Not necessarily a place of torment; more a state of cessation and silence. The Septuagint and New Testament render it with the Greek word hades.

stories.keyTakeaway: Assyria; the giant cedar; fell because of pride. Pharaoh is told he will share the same fate: cut down and taken to the pit.

stories.title: 🪦 Ezekiel 32
summaryBullets: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (32:1).

“Son of man, take up a lament for Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him: ‘You are like a lion among the nations; you are like a monster in the seas. You thrash about in your rivers, churning up the waters with your feet and muddying the streams.’ (32:2).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will spread My net over you with a company of many peoples, and they will draw you up in My net. (32:3).
I will abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field. I will cause all the birds of the air to settle upon you, and all the beasts of the earth to eat their fill of you. (32:4).
I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains. (32:5).
I will drench the land with the flow of your blood, all the way to the mountains — the ravines will be filled. (32:6).
When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light. (32:7).
All the shining lights in the heavens I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land,’ declares the Lord GOD. (32:8).
‘I will trouble the hearts of many peoples, when I bring about your destruction among the nations, in countries you do not know. (32:9).

I will cause many peoples to be appalled over you, and their kings will shudder in horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them. On the day of your downfall each of them will tremble every moment for his life.’ (32:10).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you! (32:11).
I will make your hordes fall by the swords of the mighty, the most ruthless of all nations. They will ravage the pride of Egypt and all her multitudes will be destroyed. (32:12).
I will slaughter all her cattle beside the abundant waters. No human foot will muddy them again, and no cattle hooves will disturb them. (32:13).
Then I will let her waters settle and will make her rivers flow like oil,’ declares the Lord GOD. (32:14).
‘When I make the land of Egypt a desolation and empty it of all that filled it, when I strike down all who live there, then they will know that I am the LORD.’ (32:15).
This is the lament they will chant for her; the daughters of the nations will chant it. Over Egypt and all her multitudes they will chant it, declares the Lord GOD.” (32:16).
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (32:17).
“Son of man, wail for the multitudes of Egypt, and consign her and the daughters of the mighty nations to the depths of the earth with those who descend to the Pit: (32:18).
Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and be placed with the uncircumcised! (32:19).
They will fall among those slain by the sword. The sword is appointed! Let them drag her away along with all her multitudes. (32:20).
Mighty chiefs will speak from the midst of Sheol about Egypt and her allies: ‘They have come down and lie with the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword.’ (32:21).
Assyria is there with her whole company; her graves are all around her. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword. (32:22).
Her graves are set in the depths of the Pit, and her company is all around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword— those who once spread terror in the land of the living. (32:23).

Elam is there with all her multitudes around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword— those who went down uncircumcised to the earth below, who once spread their terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who descend to the Pit. (32:24).

Among the slain they prepare a resting place for Elam with all her hordes, with her graves all around her. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, although their terror was once spread in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who descend to the Pit. They are placed among the slain. (32:25).

Meshech and Tubal are there with all their multitudes, with their graves all around them. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living. (32:26).

They do not lie down with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were placed under their heads, whose shields rested on their bones, although the terror of the mighty was once in the land of the living. (32:27).
But you too will be shattered and lie down among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. (32:28).
Edom is there, and all her kings and princes, who despite their might are laid among those slain by the sword. They lie down with the uncircumcised, with those who descend to the Pit. (32:29).

All the leaders of the north and all the Sidonians are there; they went down in disgrace with the slain, despite the terror of their might. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their shame with those who descend to the Pit. (32:30).
Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude— Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD. (32:31).

For I will spread My terror in the land of the living, so that Pharaoh and all his multitude will be laid to rest among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.” (32:32).
crossRefs: Isaiah 27:1: Sea monster imagery.
Jeremiah 46:2-12: Egypt struck at the River Euphrates.
Ezekiel 29:3-5: Pharaoh as Nile monster with hooks.
Psalm 88:10-12: Shades in the grave (Sheol).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תַּנִּין (tannin), Greek (LXX): δράκων, Aramaic: תנינא
translationNotes.note: Used for Pharaoh’s river/sea image (32:2-3).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קִינָה (qināh), Greek (LXX): θρῆνος, Aramaic: קינתא
translationNotes.note: Formal funeral song for irreversible downfall (32:2) (32:16).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲרֵלִים חַלְלֵי־חָרֶב (ʿarelim ḥallelei-ḥerev), Greek (LXX): ἀπερικέριστοι τετρωμένοι μαχαίρᾳ, Aramaic: ערילין קטילין בסייפא
translationNotes.note: Fixed refrain for dishonored dead in the pit lists (32:19-32).

The Old Testament realm of the dead; a shadowy underworld where both righteous and wicked descend (Genesis 37:35; Psalm 16:10). Not necessarily a place of torment; more a state of cessation and silence. The Septuagint and New Testament render it with the Greek word hades.

stories.keyTakeaway: Two dirges declare Pharaoh’s capture and Egypt’s slaughter, then place Egypt among fallen powers in the grave; laid with the uncircumcised, killed by the sword.

headings.text: A Lament for Pharaoh King of Egypt

stories.title: 📣 Ezekiel 33
summaryBullets: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (33:1).
“Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: ‘Suppose I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land choose a man from among them, appointing him as their watchman, (33:2).
and he sees the sword coming against that land and blows the ram’s horn to warn the people. (33:3).
Then if anyone hears the sound of the horn but fails to heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head. (33:4).
Since he heard the sound of the horn but failed to heed the warning, his blood will be on his own head. If he had heeded the warning, he would have saved his life. (33:5).

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and fails to blow the horn to warn the people, and the sword comes and takes away a life, then that one will be taken away in his iniquity, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.’ (33:6).
As for you, O son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so hear the word from My mouth and give them the warning from Me. (33:7).

If I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you will surely die,’ but you do not speak out to dissuade him from his way, then that wicked man will die in his iniquity, yet I will hold you accountable for his blood. (33:8).
But if you warn the wicked man to turn from his way, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life. (33:9).

Now as for you, son of man, tell the house of Israel that this is what they have said: ‘Our transgressions and our sins are heavy upon us, and we are wasting away because of them! How can we live?’ (33:10).

Say to them: ‘As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked should turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! For why should you die, O house of Israel?’ (33:11).

Therefore, son of man, say to your people: ‘The righteousness of the righteous man will not deliver him in the day of his transgression; neither will the wickedness of the wicked man cause him to stumble on the day he turns from his wickedness. Nor will the righteous man be able to survive by his righteousness on the day he sins.’ (33:12).

If I tell the righteous man that he will surely live, but he then trusts in his righteousness and commits iniquity, then none of his righteous works will be remembered; he will die because of the iniquity he has committed. (33:13).
But if I tell the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right— (33:14).
if he restores a pledge, makes restitution for what he has stolen, and walks in the statutes of life without practicing iniquity— then he will surely live; he will not die. (33:15).
None of the sins he has committed will be held against him. He has done what is just and right; he will surely live. (33:16).
Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But it is their way that is not just. (33:17).
If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he will die for it. (33:18).
But if a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will live because of this. (33:19).
Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.” (33:20).
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and reported, “The city has been taken!” (33:21).

Now the evening before the fugitive arrived, the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened and I was no longer mute. (33:22).
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (33:23).

“Son of man, those living in the ruins in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land. But we are many; surely the land has been given to us as a possession.’ (33:24).
Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You eat meat with the blood in it, lift up your eyes to your idols, and shed blood. Should you then possess the land? (33:25).
You have relied on your swords, you have committed detestable acts, and each of you has defiled his neighbor’s wife. Should you then possess the land?’ (33:26).

Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘As surely as I live, those in the ruins will fall by the sword, those in the open field I will give to be devoured by wild animals, and those in the strongholds and caves will die by plague. (33:27).
I will make the land a desolate waste, and the pride of her strength will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will become desolate, so that no one will pass through. (33:28).
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have made the land a desolate waste because of all the abominations they have committed.’ (33:29).

As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you near the city walls and in the doorways of their houses. One speaks to another, each saying to his brother, ‘Come and hear the message that has come from the LORD!’ (33:30).

So My people come to you as usual, sit before you, and hear your words; but they do not put them into practice. Although they express love with their mouths, their hearts pursue dishonest gain. (33:31).
Indeed, you are to them like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument. They hear your words but do not put them into practice. (33:32).
So when it comes to pass— and surely it will come— then they will know that a prophet has been among them.” (33:33).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 3:16-21: First watchman charge.
2 Kings 25:1-21: Fall of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 6:17: Watchmen’s warnings ignored.
Deuteronomy 30:19: Choose life.

translationNotes.note: Verses 2-6 describe a working military post exactly as it operated. The townspeople pick a man, set him on the wall, and he watches the approaches; when he sees the sword coming he blows the ram's horn. The shofar carried further than a shout and was the standard alarm and signal instrument, used in Judges 3:27, Nehemiah 4:18-20 and Joel 2:1. The legal accounting in 33:4-6 is the ordinary rule for a sentry: the man who ignores the alarm dies by his own fault, and the man who never sounds it answers for the blood.

Verse 21 dates the arrival of the news to the twelfth year of the exile, tenth month, fifth day, about January 585 BC. A man who escaped the fall walked the roughly nine hundred miles (1,450 km) to the Judean settlements in Babylonia to say the city has been taken. Verse 22 records that Ezekiel's mouth was opened the evening before he came, ending the restriction imposed in 3:26.

Verse 24 quotes the people still in the wrecked land: Abraham was only one man, and he possessed the land; we are many, so the land is surely given to us as a possession. The reply in 33:25-26 answers on conduct, not on arithmetic: they eat meat with the blood, look to their idols, shed blood, and each defiles his neighbour's wife.

translationNotes.term: Like a singer of love songs
translationNotes.note: Verses 30-32 describe how the exiles treated the prophet once the city had actually fallen and he had been proved right. They gathered by the walls and in the doorways to hear him, and 33:32 says that to them he was like one who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument well. They came for the performance. They heard the words and did not do them.

translationNotes.term: I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked
translationNotes.note: Verse 11 is stated as an oath: as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from his way and live. It repeats 18:23 and 18:32 and sits at the head of the chapter about the watchman's duty, which is why the warning is given at all.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel is reappointed as watchman. Each person is responsible to turn from sin. News arrives: Jerusalem has fallen. Many hear but do not do.

stories.title: 🐑 Ezekiel 34
summaryBullets: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (34:1).

“Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Woe to the shepherds of Israel, who only feed themselves! Should not the shepherds feed their flock? (34:2).
You eat the fat, wear the wool, and butcher the fattened sheep, but you do not feed the flock. (34:3).
You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bound up the injured, brought back the strays, or searched for the lost. Instead, you have ruled them with violence and cruelty. (34:4).
They were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for all the wild beasts. (34:5).
My flock went astray on all the mountains and every high hill. They were scattered over the face of all the earth, with no one to search for them or seek them out.’ (34:6).
Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: (34:7).

‘As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because My flock lacks a shepherd and has become prey and food for every wild beast, and because My shepherds did not search for My flock but fed themselves instead, (34:8).
therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD!’ (34:9).

This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will demand from them My flock and remove them from tending the flock, so that they can no longer feed themselves. For I will deliver My flock from their mouths, and it will no longer be food for them.’ (34:10).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out. (34:11).

As a shepherd looks for his scattered sheep when he is among the flock, so I will look for My flock. I will rescue them from all the places to which they were scattered on a day of clouds and darkness. (34:12).

I will bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the countries, and bring them into their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines, and in all the settlements of the land. (34:13).

I will feed them in good pasture, and the lofty mountains of Israel will be their grazing land. There they will lie down in a good grazing land; they will feed in rich pasture on the mountains of Israel. (34:14).
I will tend My flock and make them lie down, declares the Lord GOD. (34:15).
I will seek the lost, bring back the strays, bind up the broken, and strengthen the weak; but the sleek and strong I will destroy. I will shepherd them with justice.’ (34:16).
This is what the Lord GOD says to you, My flock: ‘I will judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the goats. (34:17).

Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of the pasture with your feet? Is it not enough for you to drink the clear waters? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet? (34:18).
Why must My flock feed on what your feet have trampled, and drink what your feet have muddied?’ (34:19).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says to them: ‘Behold, I Myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep. (34:20).
Since you shove with flank and shoulder, butting all the weak ones with your horns until you have scattered them abroad, (34:21).
I will save My flock, and they will no longer be prey. I will judge between one sheep and another. (34:22).
I will appoint over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he will feed them. He will feed them and be their shepherd. (34:23).
I, the LORD, will be their God, and My servant David will be a prince among them. I, the LORD, have spoken. (34:24).
I will make with them a covenant of peace and rid the land of wild animals, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the forest. (34:25).
I will make them and the places around My hill a blessing. I will send down showers in season— showers of blessing. (34:26).

The trees of the field will give their fruit, and the land will yield its produce; My flock will be secure in their land. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have broken the bars of their yoke and delivered them from the hands that enslaved them. (34:27).
They will no longer be prey for the nations, and the beasts of the earth will not consume them. They will dwell securely, and no one will frighten them. (34:28).
And I will raise up for them a garden of renown, and they will no longer be victims of famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations. (34:29).
Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are My people,’ declares the Lord GOD. (34:30).
‘You are My flock, the sheep of My pasture, My people, and I am your God,’ declares the Lord GOD.” (34:31).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 23:1-6: Woe to shepherds; righteous ruler promised.
Psalm 23:1: The LORD as shepherd.
2 Samuel 7:8-16: Promise to David’s house.
Hosea 2:18: Peace with beasts (parallel to covenant of peace).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רֹעִים / רֹעֶה (roʿim / roʿeh), Greek (LXX): ποιμήν, Aramaic: רָעְיָא (raʿyā)
translationNotes.note: Leaders pictured as caretakers of the people (34:2-4).

summaryBullets: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (35:1).
“Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it, (35:2).
and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Mount Seir. I will stretch out My hand against you and make you a desolate waste. (35:3).
I will turn your cities into ruins, and you will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (35:4).

therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will give you over to bloodshed and it will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, it will pursue you. (35:6).
I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and will cut off from it those who come and go. (35:7).

therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will treat you according to the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred against them, and I will make Myself known among them when I judge you. (35:11).

This is what the Lord GOD says: Because the enemy has said of you, ‘Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession,’ (36:2).

therefore prophesy and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Because they have made you desolate and have trampled you on every side, so that you became a possession of the rest of the nations and were taken up in slander by the lips of their talkers, (36:3).

therefore, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD. This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate ruins and abandoned cities, which have become a spoil and a mockery to the rest of the nations around you. (36:4).

Therefore, prophesy concerning the land of Israel and tell the mountains and hills, the ravines and valleys, that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I have spoken in My burning zeal because you have endured the reproach of the nations. (36:6).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I have sworn with an uplifted hand that surely the nations around you will endure reproach of their own. (36:7).
But you, O mountains of Israel, will produce branches and bear fruit for My people Israel, for they will soon come home. (36:8).
For behold, I am on your side; I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown. (36:9).
I will multiply the people upon you — the house of Israel in its entirety. The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt. (36:10).

I will fill you with people and animals, and they will multiply and be fruitful. I will make you as inhabited as you once were, and I will make you prosper more than before. Then you will know that I am the LORD. (36:11).
Yes, I will cause My people Israel to walk upon you; they will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, and you will no longer deprive them of their children. (36:12).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: Because people say to you, ‘You devour men and deprive your nation of its children,’ (36:13).
therefore you will no longer devour men or deprive your nation of its children, declares the Lord GOD. (36:14).
I will no longer allow the taunts of the nations to be heard against you, and you will no longer endure the reproach of the peoples or cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD.” (36:15).
Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (36:16).
“Son of man, when the people of Israel lived in their land, they defiled it by their own ways and deeds. Their behavior before Me was like the uncleanness of a woman’s impurity. (36:17).
So I poured out My wrath upon them because of the blood they had shed on the land, and because they had defiled it with their idols. (36:18).
I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands. I judged them according to their ways and deeds. (36:19).
And wherever they went among the nations, they profaned My holy name, because it was said of them, ‘These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave His land.’ (36:20).
But I had concern for My holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they had gone. (36:21).

Therefore tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: It is not for your sake that I will act, O house of Israel, but for My holy name, which you profaned among the nations to which you went. (36:22).

For I will take you from among the nations and gather you out of all the countries, and I will bring you back into your own land. (36:24).
I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your impurities and all your idols. (36:25).
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. (36:26).
And I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes and to carefully observe My ordinances. (36:27).
Then you will live in the land that I gave your forefathers; you will be My people, and I will be your God. (36:28).
I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine upon you. (36:29).

Then you will remember your evil ways and wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and abominations. (36:31).
It is not for your sake that I will act, declares the Lord GOD — let it be known to you. Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, O house of Israel! (36:32).
This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be resettled and the ruins to be rebuilt. (36:33).

Then they will say, ‘This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden. The cities that were once ruined, desolate, and destroyed are now fortified and inhabited.’ (36:35).
Then the nations around you that remain will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was destroyed, and I have replanted what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it. (36:36).

stories.title: 🦴 Ezekiel 37
summaryBullets: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me out by His Spirit and set me down in the middle of the valley, and it was full of bones. (37:1).
He led me all around among them, and I saw a great many bones on the floor of the valley, and indeed, they were very dry. (37:2).
Then He asked me, “Son of man, can these bones come to life?” “O Lord GOD,” I replied, “only You know.” (37:3).
And He said to me, “Prophesy concerning these bones and tell them, ‘Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD! (37:4).
This is what the Lord GOD says to these bones: I will cause breath to enter you, and you will come to life. (37:5).
I will attach tendons to you and make flesh grow upon you and cover you with skin. I will put breath within you so that you will come to life. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’” (37:6).
So I prophesied as I had been commanded. And as I prophesied, there was suddenly a noise, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone. (37:7).
As I looked on, tendons appeared on them, flesh grew, and skin covered them; but there was no breath in them. (37:8).

Then He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and tell the breath that this is what the Lord GOD says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live!” (37:9).
So I prophesied as He had commanded me, and the breath entered them, and they came to life and stood on their feet — a vast army. (37:10).
Then He said to me, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Look, they are saying, ‘Our bones are dried up, and our hope has perished; we are cut off.’ (37:11).
Therefore prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘O My people, I will open your graves and bring you up from them, and I will bring you back to the land of Israel. (37:12).
Then you, My people, will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them. (37:13).
I will put My Spirit in you and you will live, and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD.’” (37:14).
Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (37:15).

“And you, son of man, take a single stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Judah and to the Israelites associated with him.’ Then take another stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Joseph— the stick of Ephraim— and to all the house of Israel associated with him.’ (37:16).
Then join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand. (37:17).
When your people ask you, ‘Won’t you explain to us what you mean by these?’ (37:18).

you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah. I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand.’ (37:19).
When the sticks on which you write are in your hand and in full view of the people, (37:20).

you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the Israelites out of the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land. (37:21).

I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over all of them. Then they will no longer be two nations and will never again be divided into two kingdoms. (37:22).

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols or detestable images, or with any of their transgressions. I will save them from all their apostasies by which they sinned, and I will cleanse them. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God. (37:23).
My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for all of them. They will follow My ordinances and keep and observe My statutes. (37:24).

They will live in the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They will live there forever with their children and grandchildren, and My servant David will be their prince forever. (37:25).
And I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary among them forever. (37:26).
My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be My people. (37:27).
Then the nations will know that I the LORD sanctify Israel, when My sanctuary is among them forever.’” (37:28).
crossRefs: Hosea 1:11: Judah and Israel gathered under one head.
Isaiah 11:12-13: Ephraim’s envy and Judah’s hostility end.
Leviticus 26:11-12: God dwelling among His people.
Ezekiel 34:23-24: “My servant David” shepherds them.

translationNotes.note: Judean burial worked in two stages. A body was laid on a rock-cut bench in the family tomb; about a year later, when the flesh was gone, the bones were gathered into a pit or niche at the back of the chamber with the bones of earlier generations. That is the literal sense of being gathered to your fathers, in Judges 2:10 and 2 Kings 22:20. Verses 1-2 show the opposite in every detail: bones spread over open ground, out of any tomb, unsorted, and sun-bleached dry. It is the picture of an army destroyed and left where it fell.

One Hebrew word does all three jobs, and 37:5-14 plays on it ten times. God says He will put ruach into the bones; Ezekiel prophesies to the ruach; the ruach comes from the four ruachot; and 37:14 says I will put My ruach in you and you will live. English has to keep switching between breath, wind and Spirit, and the single thread is lost.

Verse 11 gives the interpretation in the people's own words, which is what the vision is answering: our bones are dried up, our hope has perished, we are cut off. The vision is the reply to a sentence the exiles were actually saying. Verse 12 answers it with graves opened and a return to the land of Israel.

translationNotes.term: Bone to bone, then sinews, flesh and skin
translationNotes.note: Verses 7-8 rebuild in anatomical order and stop short. There is a rattling, the bones join, then sinews, then flesh, then skin over the top, and 37:8 notes that there was no breath in them. The whole army stands complete and dead until 37:9-10. The two-stage build matches Genesis 2:7, where the body is formed first and then breathed into.

translationNotes.term: Two sticks joined in the hand
translationNotes.note: Verses 16-19 have him write on two wooden staves, one for Judah and one for Joseph, which is Ephraim, and hold them so they become one piece in his hand. The two names are the two kingdoms that split in 931 BC after Solomon; the northern ten tribes had been gone since Assyria took Samaria in 722 BC. Verse 22 states the meaning: one nation, one king, never again two.

Verses 24-25 name the coming king as My servant David, prince over them forever, and 34:23-24 says the same. David himself had been dead some four centuries. The title is used the way the text uses it, for a ruler of David's line, and 37:26 adds an everlasting covenant of peace with God's sanctuary among them.

stories.keyTakeaway: Ezekiel prophesies in a valley of dry bones, and the bones come together, flesh covers them, and breath from the four winds makes them live and stand, a vast army; God says the bones are the whole house of Israel, whom he will bring up from their graves and settle in their own land. Two sticks written for Judah and for Joseph become one in his hand: one nation, one king, his servant David, an everlasting covenant of peace, and his sanctuary among them forever.

stories.title: 🛡️ Ezekiel 38
summaryBullets: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (38:1).
“Son of man, set your face against Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him (38:2).
and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. (38:3).

I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out with all your army — your horses, your horsemen in full armor, and a great company armed with shields and bucklers, all brandishing their swords. (38:4).
Persia, Cush, and Put will accompany them, all with shields and helmets, (38:5).
as well as Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the far north with all its troops— the many nations with you. (38:6).
Get ready; prepare yourself, you and all your company gathered around you; you will be their guard. (38:7).

After a long time you will be summoned. In the latter years you will enter a land that has recovered from war, whose people were gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate. They had been brought out from the nations, and all now dwell securely. (38:8).
You and all your troops, and many peoples with you will go up, advancing like a thunderstorm; you will be like a cloud covering the land. (38:9).
This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day, thoughts will arise in your mind, and you will devise an evil plan. (38:10).
You will say, ‘I will go up against a land of unwalled villages; I will come against a quiet people who dwell securely, all of them living without walls or bars or gates— (38:11).

in order to seize the spoil and carry off the plunder, to turn a hand against the desolate places now inhabited and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions and who live at the center of the land.’ (38:12).

Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish with all its villages will ask, ‘Have you come to capture the plunder? Have you assembled your hordes to carry away loot, to make off with silver and gold, to take cattle and goods, to seize great spoil?’ (38:13).
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and tell Gog that this is what the Lord GOD says: On that day when My people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not take notice of this? (38:14).
And you will come from your place out of the far north— you and many peoples with you, all riding horses— a mighty horde, a huge army. (38:15).

You will advance against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will happen in the latter days, O Gog, that I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I show Myself holy in you before their eyes. (38:16).

This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you the one of whom I have spoken in former days through My servants, the prophets of Israel, who in those times prophesied for years that I would bring you against them? (38:17).
Now on that day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, My wrath will flare up. (38:18).
In My zeal and fiery rage I proclaim that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel. (38:19).

The fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls upon the ground, and all mankind on the face of the earth will tremble at My presence. The mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground. (38:20).
And I will summon a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD, and every man’s sword will be against his brother. (38:21).
I will execute judgment upon him with plague and bloodshed. I will pour out torrents of rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur on him and on his troops and on the many nations with him. (38:22).
I will magnify and sanctify Myself, and I will reveal Myself in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD. (38:23).
crossRefs: Genesis 10:2: Magog, Meshech, Tubal and Gomer listed among the sons of Japheth.
Ezekiel 39:1-6: The same invader named again and destroyed on the mountains of Israel.
Revelation 20:7-9: Gog and Magog named in a later and separate scene, surrounding the camp of the saints.
Ezekiel 36:22-28: God's name vindicated before the nations and His Spirit given, the restoration Gog attacks.
Joel 3:9-14: Nations summoned, weapons made ready, and multitudes gathered in the valley of decision.

translationNotes.note: Verse 2 names Gog as a person, of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Magog, Meshech and Tubal are all listed in Genesis 10:2 among the sons of Japheth, so the text places them in the northern branch of the table of nations. Meshech and Tubal appear in Assyrian records as Mushki and Tabal, kingdoms in eastern Anatolia, in what is now Turkey. The text names them; it does not identify them with any modern state.

translationNotes.term: Chief prince, or prince of Rosh
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew rosh means head or chief, so the phrase can read chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, which is how most English versions take it, or prince of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal, treating Rosh as a place. The ancient Greek translation read it as a name. The wording is genuinely open, and 38:3 and 39:1 repeat it identically.

Verse 6 adds two more of Gog's allies from the far north, both from the same Genesis 10:2-3 list. Gomer appears in Assyrian records as the Gimirrai, the people the Greeks called Cimmerians, who came down out of the steppe into Anatolia. Beth-togarmah is Til-garimmu in Assyrian texts, in eastern Anatolia, and Ezekiel 27:14 names it as the source of Tyre's horses and mules.

Verse 4 says God will turn him around and put hooks in his jaws and bring him out with his whole army. Assyrian and Babylonian records and reliefs show captives led by a ring or hook through the lip or nose, and 2 Kings 19:28 and Ezekiel 29:4 use the same image. The aggressor of this chapter arrives on a leash.

Verses 8-11 describe the target: a people brought back from the sword and gathered out of many nations, living securely, a land of unwalled villages with no bars and no gates. Every settlement of consequence in the ancient world was walled. Describing an unwalled country is describing a place that has stopped expecting an attack, which is precisely what makes it worth attacking.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against Gog of Magog, declaring that He will turn him around with hooks and bring him and his allied armies against Israel; when Gog attacks the restored land, God's anger will erupt in earthquakes, internal conflict among Gog's troops, plague, bloodshed, and supernatural devastation to display His holiness to the nations.

stories.title: 🛡️ Ezekiel 39
summaryBullets: “As for you, O son of man, prophesy against Gog and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. (39:1).
I will turn you around, drive you along, bring you up from the far north, and send you against the mountains of Israel. (39:2).
Then I will strike the bow from your left hand and dash down the arrows from your right hand. (39:3).
On the mountains of Israel you will fall — you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to every kind of ravenous bird and wild beast. (39:4).
You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. (39:5).
I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD. (39:6).
So I will make My holy name known among My people Israel and will no longer allow it to be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel. (39:7).
Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken. (39:8).

Then those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out, kindle fires, and burn up the weapons— the bucklers and shields, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them for fuel. (39:9).

They will not gather wood from the countryside or cut it from the forests, for they will use the weapons for fuel. They will loot those who looted them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD. (39:10).

And on that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. It will block those who travel through, because Gog and all his hordes will be buried there. So it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog. (39:11).
For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land. (39:12).
All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I display My glory, declares the Lord GOD. (39:13).
And men will be employed to continually pass through the land to cleanse it by burying the invaders who remain on the ground. At the end of the seven months they will begin their search. (39:14).
As they pass through the land, anyone who sees a human bone will set up a pillar next to it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog. (39:15).
(Even the city will be named Hamonah.) And so they will cleanse the land. (39:16).

And as for you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Call out to every kind of bird and to every beast of the field: ‘Assemble and come together from all around to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you, a great feast on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood. (39:17).
You will eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth as though they were rams, lambs, goats, and bulls — all the fattened animals of Bashan. (39:18).
At the sacrifice I am preparing, you will eat fat until you are gorged and drink blood until you are drunk. (39:19).
And at My table you will eat your fill of horses and riders, of mighty men and warriors of every kind,’ declares the Lord GOD. (39:20).
I will display My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment that I execute and the hand that I lay upon them. (39:21).
From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God. (39:22).

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to Me. So I hid My face from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, so that they all fell by the sword. (39:23).
I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and transgressions, and I hid My face from them. (39:24).
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for My holy name. (39:25).
They will forget their disgrace and all the treachery they committed against Me, when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to frighten them. (39:26).
When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, I will show My holiness in them in the sight of many nations. (39:27).
Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, when I regather them to their own land, not leaving any of them behind after their exile among the nations. (39:28).
And I will no longer hide My face from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.” (39:29).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 38:1-9: The invasion announced, the allies named and the hooks put in Gog's jaws.
Revelation 19:17-18: Birds called to the great supper of God to eat the flesh of kings and captains.
Genesis 10:2: Magog, Meshech and Tubal among the sons of Japheth in the table of nations.
Numbers 19:11-16: Anyone who touches a dead body is unclean for seven days, the law behind the burial detail in 39:14-16.
Joel 2:28-29: God pours out His Spirit on His people, the promise 39:29 makes in the same words.

translationNotes.note: Verses 9-10 say the towns of Israel will burn the invaders' gear for seven years and will not need to gather wood from the field or cut it from the forests. Ancient weapons were largely wood: bow staves, arrow shafts, spear and javelin shafts, shields of hide over a wooden frame, and war clubs. It burns. The measure of the defeat is given as a fuel supply.

Verses 11-16 set out a public health operation, not a poem. All Israel buries for seven months to cleanse the land; after that, men are employed full time to walk the ground, and when one of them sees a human bone he sets up a marker beside it until the gravediggers come and bury it. Numbers 19:11-16 makes contact with a corpse or a bone a source of seven-day uncleanness, so leaving bones lying in open country made the land itself unusable.

Verse 11 gives the burial ground a name meaning the multitude of Gog, and 39:16 gives a nearby town the name Hamonah, multitude. Naming a place for what happened there is standard practice in the Old Testament; compare the Valley of Achor in Joshua 7:26 and Jeremiah's renaming of Topheth as the Valley of Slaughter in Jeremiah 7:32.

translationNotes.term: A sacrificial feast for birds and beasts
translationNotes.note: Verses 17-20 invite every bird and wild animal to a sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, to eat flesh and drink blood, and to fill themselves at God's table with horses, riders and warriors. Calling the battlefield a sacrifice inverts the normal order, where the worshippers eat. Revelation 19:17-18 takes up the same summons.

The refrain then they will know that I am the LORD runs through Ezekiel more than sixty times, and 39:21-29 gathers it up: the nations will know, and the house of Israel will know from that day forward. Verse 23 states the point of the whole book in one sentence, that the exile happened because of their unfaithfulness, not because God was unable to protect them.

stories.keyTakeaway: God will destroy Gog and his forces on Israel's mountains, feed the birds and animals with their bodies, and have Israel spend seven months burying the dead and seven years burning the weapons as fuel. After demonstrating his power to the nations, God will restore Israel's fortunes, gather them from exile, and pour out his Spirit on them.

stories.title: 🏛️ Ezekiel 40
summaryBullets: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month — in the fourteenth year after Jerusalem had been struck down — on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He took me there. (40:1).
In visions of God He took me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose southern slope was a structure that resembled a city. (40:2).
So He took me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He was standing in the gateway with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand. (40:3).

“Son of man,” he said to me, “look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Report to the house of Israel everything you see.” (40:4).

And I saw a wall surrounding the temple area. Now the length of the measuring rod in the man’s hand was six long cubits (each measuring a cubit and a handbreadth), and he measured the wall to be one rod thick and one rod high. (40:5).
Then he came to the gate facing east and climbed its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate to be one rod deep. (40:6).
Each gate chamber was one rod long and one rod wide, and there were five cubits between the gate chambers. The inner threshold of the gate by the portico facing inward was one rod deep. (40:7).
Then he measured the portico of the gateway inside; (40:8).
it was eight cubits deep, and its jambs were two cubits thick. And the portico of the gateway faced the temple. (40:9).
There were three gate chambers on each side of the east gate, each with the same measurements, and the gateposts on either side also had the same measurements. (40:10).
And he measured the width of the gateway entrance to be ten cubits, and its length was thirteen cubits. (40:11).
In front of each gate chamber was a wall one cubit high, and the gate chambers were six cubits square. (40:12).
Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one gate chamber to the roof of the opposite one; the distance was twenty-five cubits from doorway to doorway. (40:13).
Next he measured the gateposts to be sixty cubits high. The gateway extended around to the gatepost of the courtyard. (40:14).
And the distance from the entrance of the gateway to the far end of its inner portico was fifty cubits. (40:15).

The gate chambers and their side pillars had beveled windows all around the inside of the gateway. The porticos also had windows all around on the inside. Each side pillar was decorated with palm trees. (40:16).
Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were chambers and a pavement laid out all around the court. Thirty chambers faced the pavement, (40:17).
which flanked the gateways and corresponded to the length of the gates; this was the lower pavement. (40:18).
Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the outside of the inner court; it was a hundred cubits on the east side as well as on the north. (40:19).
He also measured the length and width of the gateway of the outer court facing north. (40:20).
Its three gate chambers on each side, its side pillars, and its portico all had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. (40:21).
Its windows, portico, and palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, with its portico opposite them. (40:22).
There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was on the east. He measured the distance from gateway to gateway to be a hundred cubits. (40:23).
Then he led me to the south side, and I saw a gateway facing south. He measured its side pillars and portico, and they had the same measurements as the others. (40:24).
Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around, like the other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. (40:25).
Seven steps led up to it, and its portico was opposite them; it had palm trees on its side pillars, one on each side. (40:26).
The inner court also had a gate facing south, and he measured the distance from gateway to gateway toward the south to be a hundred cubits. (40:27).
Next he brought me into the inner court through the south gate, and he measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others. (40:28).

Its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. (40:29).
(The porticoes around the inner court were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits deep.) (40:30).
Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees. Eight steps led up to it. (40:31).
And he brought me to the inner court on the east side, and he measured the gateway; it had the same measurements as the others. (40:32).

Its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. (40:33).
Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side. Eight steps led up to it. (40:34).
Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it. It had the same measurements as the others, (40:35).
as did its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico. It also had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. (40:36).
Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side. Eight steps led up to it. (40:37).
There was a chamber with a doorway by the portico in each of the inner gateways. There the burnt offering was to be washed. (40:38).
Inside the portico of the gateway were two tables on each side, on which the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were to be slaughtered. (40:39).
Outside, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gateway, there were two tables on one side and two more tables on the other side of the gate’s portico. (40:40).
So there were four tables inside the gateway and four outside — eight tables in all — on which the sacrifices were to be slaughtered. (40:41).

There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, each a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit high. On these were placed the utensils used to slaughter the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices. (40:42).
The double-pronged hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside of the room, and the flesh of the offering was to be placed on the tables. (40:43).
Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, were two chambers, one beside the north gate and facing south, and another beside the south gate and facing north. (40:44).
Then the man said to me: “The chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple, (40:45).
and the chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him.” (40:46).
Next he measured the court. It was square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide. And the altar was in front of the temple. (40:47).

Then he brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the side pillars of the portico to be five cubits on each side. The width of the gateway was fourteen cubits and its sidewalls were three cubits on either side. (40:48).
The portico was twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, and ten steps led up to it. There were columns by the side pillars, one on each side. (40:49).
crossRefs: Exodus 25:8-9: Make the sanctuary exactly according to the pattern shown on the mountain.
1 Kings 6:1-38: Solomon's temple laid out room by room with its measurements, the building this vision is measured against.
Ezekiel 8:1-18: The earlier temple vision, where the same prophet is carried to Jerusalem and shown what was inside.
Zechariah 2:1-5: A man with a measuring line going out to measure Jerusalem, and told the city will have no walls.
Revelation 21:15-17: An angel with a golden measuring rod measuring a city, its gates and its wall.

translationNotes.note: Verse 3 gives the surveyor two tools: a flax cord for long distances and a rigid reed for short ones. The reed is a cut cane, and 40:5 says it runs six long cubits, which makes it about ten feet six inches (3.2 m). That is why so many walls, thresholds and chambers in this chapter come out at exactly one rod, six rods or the like: the man is laying the same stick down over and over.

A common cubit is the forearm from elbow to fingertip, about eighteen inches (45 cm). A handbreadth is the width of four fingers, about three inches (7.5 cm). Verse 5 says every cubit in this vision is a cubit plus a handbreadth, roughly twenty-one inches (53 cm). Every number in chapters 40 to 48 has to be read on that larger scale, so the complex is about a sixth bigger than the same figures would give in ordinary cubits.

translationNotes.term: The date, and why it matters
translationNotes.note: Verse 1 fixes it three ways: the twenty-fifth year of the exile, the beginning of the year on the tenth day, and the fourteenth year after Jerusalem was struck down. That is about 573 BC. The tenth day of the first month is the day the Passover lamb was selected in Exodus 12:3. Fourteen years after the temple was burned, a priest with no sanctuary is given a complete set of building measurements.

The gates of 40:6-16 are not doorways but buildings: a long passage with three guard rooms on each side, jambs between them, a portico at the inner end, and windows. Six-chambered gates of exactly this plan have been excavated at Israelite cities, and 2 Samuel 18:24 and 18:33 describe a king sitting between the two gates and going up to the chamber over the gateway. This is the standard Iron Age fortified gate, drawn to scale.

Verses 38-43 describe the working end of the sacrificial system: rooms for rinsing the burnt offering, eight tables of dressed stone for slaughtering, four tables for the utensils, and double-pronged hooks a handbreadth long fixed around the walls for hanging carcasses. It is a butchery, described as one, with the fittings named.

The date palm appears on every gate jamb in this chapter and through chapter 41, alternating with cherubim on the walls. Solomon's temple carried the same decoration according to 1 Kings 6:29-35. The palm was the tree of the oasis and of Jericho, the city of palms, and it is the standard motif of a fruitful, guarded place in the art of the whole region.

stories.keyTakeaway: A bronze-faced man shows Ezekiel a detailed vision of a temple complex, measuring its outer and inner gates, courtyards, and entrances; all gates have the same measurements and palm tree decorations, with tables for sacrifices and rooms for priests stationed throughout.

headings.text: The Man with a Measuring Rod
The Gates of the Inner Court

stories.title: 🏛️ Ezekiel 41
summaryBullets: Then the man brought me into the outer sanctuary and measured the side pillars to be six cubits wide on each side. (41:1).

The width of the entrance was ten cubits, and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on each side. He also measured the length of the outer sanctuary to be forty cubits, and the width to be twenty cubits. (41:2).
And he went into the inner sanctuary and measured the side pillars at the entrance to be two cubits wide. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side were seven cubits wide. (41:3).
Then he measured the room adjacent to the inner sanctuary to be twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.” (41:4).
Next he measured the wall of the temple to be six cubits thick, and the width of each side room around the temple was four cubits. (41:5).

The side rooms were arranged one above another in three levels of thirty rooms each. There were ledges all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side rooms, so that the supports would not be fastened into the wall of the temple itself. (41:6).

The side rooms surrounding the temple widened at each successive level, because the structure surrounding the temple ascended by stages corresponding to the narrowing of the temple wall as it rose upward. And so a stairway went up from the lowest story to the highest, through the middle one. (41:7).
I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it, forming the foundation of the side rooms. It was the full length of a rod, six long cubits. (41:8).
The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side rooms of the temple (41:9).
and the outer chambers was twenty cubits wide all around the temple. (41:10).
The side rooms opened into this area, with one entrance on the north and another on the south. The open area was five cubits wide all around. (41:11).
Now the building that faced the temple courtyard on the west was seventy cubits wide, and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, with a length of ninety cubits. (41:12).
Then he measured the temple to be a hundred cubits long, and the temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long. (41:13).
The width of the temple courtyard on the east, including the front of the temple, was a hundred cubits. (41:14).

Next he measured the length of the building facing the temple courtyard at the rear of the temple, including its galleries on each side; it was a hundred cubits. The outer sanctuary, the inner sanctuary, and the porticoes facing the court, (41:15).

as well as the thresholds and the beveled windows and the galleries all around with their three levels opposite the threshold, were overlaid with wood on all sides. They were paneled from the ground to the windows, and the windows were covered. (41:16).
In the space above the outside of the entrance to the inner sanctuary on all the walls, spaced evenly around the inner and outer sanctuary, (41:17).
were alternating carved cherubim and palm trees. Each cherub had two faces: (41:18).
the face of a man was toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion was toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved all the way around the temple. (41:19).
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the outer sanctuary from the floor to the space above the entrance. (41:20).
The outer sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe, and the doorframe of the sanctuary was similar. (41:21).
There was an altar of wood three cubits high and two cubits square. Its corners, base, and sides were of wood. And the man told me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.” (41:22).
Both the outer sanctuary and the inner sanctuary had double doors, (41:23).
and each door had two swinging panels. There were two panels for one door and two for the other. (41:24).
Cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls were carved on the doors of the outer sanctuary, and there was a wooden canopy outside, on the front of the portico. (41:25).
There were beveled windows and palm trees on the sidewalls of the portico. The side rooms of the temple also had canopies. (41:26).
crossRefs: 1 Kings 6:2-22: Solomon's temple with the same three-part plan, the porch, the main hall and the inner sanctuary.
Exodus 26:31-34: The veil separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle.
1 Kings 6:29-35: Cherubim and palm trees carved on the walls and doors of Solomon's temple.
Exodus 25:18-22: Cherubim over the ark, the guardian figures repeated across the walls in 41:18-20.
Hebrews 9:1-8: The two rooms of the sanctuary explained, with entry to the inner one restricted to one man once a year.

translationNotes.term: A perfect square, twenty by twenty
translationNotes.note: Verse 4 measures the innermost room at twenty cubits by twenty and the man says this is the Most Holy Place. In long cubits that is about thirty-five feet (10.6 m) square. 1 Kings 6:20 gives Solomon's inner sanctuary the same twenty by twenty footprint.
