The room the high priest entered once a year is the smallest space in the complex and the one everything else is arranged around.

Verses 5-11 describe thirty rooms per level stacked three high around the outside of the temple building, each level wider than the one below because the outer wall of the house steps back at each stage. The chamber beams rested on those ledges rather than being let into the sanctuary wall, so no timber was driven into the holy structure. 1 Kings 6:5-10 describes the same arrangement in Solomon's building.

Verses 18-20 carve cherubim and palm trees alternating all round the walls, each cherub showing a human face toward the palm on one side and a lion's face toward the palm on the other. The living creatures of chapter 1 had four faces. Carved in relief on a flat wall, only two can be seen, which is exactly what the text describes.

translationNotes.term: A wooden altar before the LORD
translationNotes.note: Verse 22 measures it at three cubits high and two square, with corners, base and sides of wood, and the man calls it the table that is before the LORD. In the tabernacle and Solomon's temple this is the altar of incense of Exodus 30:1-6 and the table of the bread of the Presence of Exodus 25:23-30. It is the only furnishing named inside the building in the whole vision.

Verses 23-25 give both the main hall and the inner sanctuary a pair of doors, each door made of two swinging leaves so it folds back on itself. Hinged in sockets top and bottom rather than on strap hinges, this was the standard way to build a wide doorway that had to open in a confined porch. The same carved cherubim and palms are on the door leaves as on the walls.

stories.keyTakeaway: The man with the measuring rod measures the temple itself: the outer sanctuary forty by twenty cubits, the inner room a twenty-cubit square he calls the Most Holy Place, with three stories of side rooms around it; wood paneling carved with alternating cherubim and palm trees covers walls and doors, each cherub with the face of a man and the face of a young lion, and a wooden altar stands as the table before the LORD.

stories.title: 🏛️ Ezekiel 42
summaryBullets: Then the man led me out northward into the outer court, and he brought me to the group of chambers opposite the temple courtyard and the outer wall on the north side. (42:1).
The building with the door facing north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide. (42:2).
Gallery faced gallery in three levels opposite the twenty cubits that belonged to the inner court and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court. (42:3).
In front of the chambers was an inner walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. Their doors were on the north. (42:4).
Now the upper chambers were smaller because the galleries took more space from the chambers on the lower and middle floors of the building. (42:5).
For they were arranged in three stories, and unlike the courts, they had no pillars. So the upper chambers were set back further than the lower and middle floors. (42:6).
An outer wall in front of the chambers was fifty cubits long and ran parallel to the chambers and the outer court. (42:7).
For the chambers on the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long. (42:8).
And below these chambers was the entrance on the east side as one enters them from the outer court. (42:9).
On the south side along the length of the wall of the outer court were chambers adjoining the courtyard and opposite the building, (42:10).
with a passageway in front of them, just like the chambers that were on the north. They had the same length and width, with similar exits and dimensions. (42:11).
And corresponding to the doors of the chambers that were facing south, there was a door in front of the walkway that was parallel to the wall extending eastward. (42:12).

Then the man said to me, “The north and south chambers facing the temple courtyard are the holy chambers where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will place the most holy offerings— the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings— for the place is holy. (42:13).

Once the priests have entered the holy area, they must not go out into the outer court until they have left behind the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They are to put on other clothes before they approach the places that are for the people.” (42:14).
Now when the man had finished measuring the interior of the temple area, he led me out by the gate that faced east, and he measured the area all around: (42:15).
With a measuring rod he measured the east side to be five hundred cubits long. (42:16).
He measured the north side to be five hundred cubits long. (42:17).
He measured the south side to be five hundred cubits long. (42:18).
And he came around and measured the west side to be five hundred cubits long. (42:19).
So he measured the area on all four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, to separate the holy from the common. (42:20).
crossRefs: Leviticus 6:14-18: The grain offering eaten by the priests in a holy place, the meals the chambers of 42:13 are for.
Leviticus 10:10: Distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean.
Exodus 28:40-43: The garments made for the priests to serve in, which 42:14 says must be left behind.
Numbers 18:8-10: The most holy offerings given to the priests, to be eaten by the males in a most holy place.
Ezekiel 44:17-19: The same rule about changing out of the linen garments before going out to the people.

translationNotes.note: Rooms built into the temple courts, used as offices, stores and dining rooms. Verse 13 says the priests eat the most holy offerings there and lay up the grain, sin and guilt offerings. Under Leviticus 6:16 and Numbers 18:9-10 the priests' portion had to be eaten inside the sanctuary precinct, so the building is a purpose-made refectory and strongroom.

translationNotes.term: Changing out of the holy garments
translationNotes.note: Verse 14 makes it a rule of movement: a priest who has been serving may not walk out into the outer court until he has taken off the clothes he ministered in, because those garments are holy. 44:19 repeats it and adds the reason, so that he does not transmit holiness to the people by touching them with the cloth. Holiness in these chapters behaves like something that can be carried on fabric.

Verses 15-20 close the survey by measuring the outer boundary on all four sides: five hundred cubits each way, a perfect square, with a wall around it. Verse 20 states the wall's whole purpose in one line, to separate the holy from the common. In long cubits that is roughly 875 feet (267 m) on a side, about seventeen acres.

Verse 4 puts a passage in front of the chamber blocks, ten cubits wide and a hundred long, with the doors opening onto it from the north. The vision keeps describing circulation, where a person walks and which way a door faces, because the whole point of the layout is controlling who goes where.

stories.keyTakeaway: The man shows Ezekiel priests' rooms on the north and south sides of the temple courtyard where holy offerings will be stored and eaten; priests must change out of their ministry garments before leaving the holy area. He then measures the entire temple complex and finds it forms a perfect square, five hundred cubits on each side, with a wall separating the holy from the common.

stories.title: 🏛️ Ezekiel 43
summaryBullets: Then the man brought me back to the gate that faces east, (43:1).
and I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of many waters, and the earth shone with His glory. (43:2).
The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when He came to destroy the city and like the visions I had seen by the River Kebar. I fell facedown, (43:3).
and the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east. (43:4).
Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple. (43:5).
While the man was standing beside me, I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple, (43:6).

and He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will never again defile My holy name — neither they nor their kings — by their prostitution and by the funeral offerings for their kings at their deaths. (43:7).

When they placed their threshold next to My threshold and their doorposts beside My doorposts, with only a wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by the abominations they committed. Therefore I have consumed them in My anger. (43:8).
Now let them remove far from Me their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings, and I will dwell among them forever. (43:9).
As for you, son of man, describe the temple to the people of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities. Let them measure the plan, (43:10).

and if they are ashamed of all they have done, then make known to them the design of the temple— its arrangement and its exits and entrances— its whole design along with all its statutes, forms, and laws. Write it down in their sight, so that they may keep its complete design and all its statutes and may carry them out. (43:11).
This is the law of the temple: All its surrounding territory on top of the mountain will be most holy. Yes, this is the law of the temple. (43:12).

These are the measurements of the altar in long cubits (a cubit and a handbreadth): Its gutter shall be a cubit deep and a cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge. And this is the height of the altar: (43:13).

The space from the gutter on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the ledge one cubit wide. The space from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge shall be four cubits, and the ledge one cubit wide. (43:14).
The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, and four horns shall project upward from the hearth. (43:15).
The altar hearth shall be square at its four corners, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide. (43:16).
The ledge shall also be square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, with a rim of half a cubit and a gutter of a cubit all around it. The steps of the altar shall face east.” (43:17).

Then He said to me: “Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is constructed, so that burnt offerings may be sacrificed on it and blood may be splattered on it: (43:18).
You are to give a young bull from the herd as a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are of the family of Zadok, who approach Me to minister before Me, declares the Lord GOD. (43:19).

You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the rim; thus you will cleanse the altar and make atonement for it. (43:20).
Then you are to take away the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the appointed part of the temple area outside the sanctuary. (43:21).
On the second day you are to present an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and the altar is to be cleansed as it was with the bull. (43:22).
When you have finished the purification, you are to present a young, unblemished bull and an unblemished ram from the flock. (43:23).
You must present them before the LORD; the priests are to sprinkle salt on them and sacrifice them as a burnt offering to the LORD. (43:24).
For seven days you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering; you are also to provide a young bull and a ram from the flock, both unblemished. (43:25).
For seven days the priests are to make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; so they shall consecrate it. (43:26).
At the end of these days, from the eighth day on, the priests are to present your burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.’” (43:27).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 10:18-19: The glory leaves the temple by the east gate, the road it returns on here.
Ezekiel 11:22-23: The glory stops on the mountain east of the city, the direction it comes back from in 43:2.
Exodus 40:34-35: The cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory fills the tabernacle so Moses cannot enter.
1 Kings 8:10-11: The cloud fills the house so the priests cannot stand to minister at Solomon's dedication.
Leviticus 8:33-35: The seven days of ordination at the tent of meeting, the pattern the altar rite in 43:25-26 follows.

translationNotes.term: The glory returns from the east
translationNotes.note: Verses 1-5 reverse chapters 10 and 11 exactly. It left by the east gate and stopped on the mountain east of the city; it comes back the same way, and 43:3 has Ezekiel say this is the vision he saw when he came to destroy the city and the vision he saw by the Kebar canal. He falls on his face, as in 1:28, 3:23 and 44:4.

Verse 7 calls the place the throne and the place of the soles of God's feet, where He will dwell among the Israelites forever. 1 Chronicles 28:2 and Psalm 132:7 use the same footstool language of the ark and the sanctuary. Isaiah 66:1 says heaven is His throne and the earth His footstool, so the phrase is a claim about presence, not about size.

Verse 8 gives the specific complaint about the old arrangement: they set their threshold by God's threshold and their doorpost beside His, with only a wall between. The royal palace in Jerusalem stood immediately next to the temple, and 2 Kings 16:18 and 23:11 record royal fittings inside the temple precinct. The new layout puts the sanctuary in its own walled square with the palace nowhere near it.

Verses 13-17 build the altar in stepped tiers with a gutter round the base, ledges, a hearth on top and horns at its four corners, reached by steps on the east so the priest climbs facing west, away from the sunrise. The Hebrew word for the hearth is ariel, which sounds like lion of God or altar hearth; Isaiah 29:1-2 uses the same word of Jerusalem itself.

translationNotes.term: Seven days to consecrate an altar
translationNotes.note: Verses 18-27 lay out a week-long purification: a bull for the first day, then a male goat daily, with blood put on the horns, the four corners of the ledge and the rim. Exodus 29:35-37 and Leviticus 8:33-35 prescribe the same seven days. From the eighth day the altar is in ordinary service. The rite decontaminates the equipment, which is what the Hebrew term rendered sin offering is largely for.

stories.keyTakeaway: The glory of the LORD enters the temple from the east and fills it; God declares this will be his eternal dwelling place among Israel if they abandon their idolatry, then provides detailed measurements for the altar and regulations for its seven-day purification ritual.

headings.text: The Glory of the Lord Returns to the Temple

stories.title: 🧭 Ezekiel 44
summaryBullets: The man then brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary that faced east, but it was shut. (44:1).

And the LORD said to me, “This gate is to remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no man shall enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it will remain shut. (44:2).
Only the prince himself may sit inside the gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD. He must enter by way of the portico of the gateway and go out the same way.” (44:3).
Then the man brought me to the front of the temple by way of the north gate. I looked and saw the glory of the LORD filling His temple, and I fell facedown. (44:4).

The LORD said to me: “Son of man, pay attention; look carefully with your eyes and listen closely with your ears to everything I tell you concerning all the statutes and laws of the house of the LORD. Take careful note of the entrance to the temple, along with all the exits of the sanctuary. (44:5).
Tell the rebellious house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I have had enough of all your abominations, O house of Israel. (44:6).

In addition to all your other abominations, you brought in foreigners uncircumcised in both heart and flesh to occupy My sanctuary; you defiled My temple when you offered My food— the fat and the blood; you broke My covenant. (44:7).
And you have not kept charge of My holy things, but have appointed others to keep charge of My sanctuary for you.’ (44:8).
This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter My sanctuary — not even a foreigner who lives among the Israelites. (44:9).
Surely the Levites who wandered away from Me when Israel went astray, and who wandered away from Me after their idols, will bear the consequences of their iniquity. (44:10).

Yet they shall be ministers in My sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the temple and ministering there. They shall slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices for the people and stand before them to minister to them. (44:11).

Because they ministered before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I swore with an uplifted hand concerning them that they would bear the consequences of their iniquity, declares the Lord GOD. (44:12).
They must not approach Me to serve Me as priests or come near any of My holy things or the most holy things. They will bear the shame of the abominations they have committed. (44:13).
Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of all the work for the temple and everything to be done in it. (44:14).

But the Levitical priests, who are descended from Zadok and who kept charge of My sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from Me, are to approach Me to minister before Me. They will stand before Me to offer Me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD. (44:15).
They alone shall enter My sanctuary and draw near to My table to minister before Me. They will keep My charge. (44:16).

When they enter the gates of the inner court, they are to wear linen garments; they must not wear anything made of wool when they minister at the gates of the inner court or inside the temple. (44:17).
They are to wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them perspire. (44:18).

When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they are to take off the garments in which they have ministered, leave them in the holy chambers, and dress in other clothes so that they do not transmit holiness to the people with their garments. (44:19).
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but must carefully trim their hair. (44:20).
No priest may drink wine before he enters the inner court. (44:21).
And they shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but must marry a virgin of the descendants of the house of Israel, or a widow of a priest. (44:22).
They are to teach My people the difference between the holy and the common and show them how to discern between the clean and the unclean. (44:23).

In any dispute, they shall officiate as judges and judge according to My ordinances. They must keep My laws and statutes regarding all My appointed feasts, and they must keep My Sabbaths holy. (44:24).
A priest must not defile himself by going near a dead person. However, for a father, a mother, a son, a daughter, a brother, or an unmarried sister, he may do so, (44:25).
and after he is cleansed, he must count off seven days for himself. (44:26).
And on the day he goes into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he must present his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD. (44:27).
In regard to their inheritance, I am their inheritance. You are to give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession. (44:28).
They shall eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings. Everything in Israel devoted to the LORD will belong to them. (44:29).

The best of all the firstfruits and of every contribution from all your offerings will belong to the priests. You are to give your first batch of dough to the priest, so that a blessing may rest upon your homes. (44:30).
The priests may not eat any bird or animal found dead or torn by wild beasts. (44:31).
crossRefs: Leviticus 10:8-11: Priests forbidden wine before entering the tent, and charged to teach the difference between holy and common.
Leviticus 21:1-9: The rules for a priest on corpses, on marriage, and on shaving the head, taken up again in 44:20-25.
Numbers 18:20-24: The priests and Levites given no land inheritance, because the LORD Himself is their portion.
1 Samuel 2:35: A faithful priest promised who will do what is in God's heart, a promise the line of Zadok answers.
1 Kings 2:26-35: Abiathar removed and Zadok installed as priest, the division 44:10-16 reaches back to.

translationNotes.note: Verses 1-3 close the outer east gate permanently, because the LORD entered by it in 43:4. Only the prince may sit inside its gateway to eat bread in the LORD's presence, and he enters and leaves by the porch, not through the gate itself. A gate that is never opened again is the strongest possible statement that the departure of chapters 10 and 11 will not be repeated.

The word means one lifted up, a chief or leader, and the vision uses it for the ruler throughout instead of melekh, king. He has real duties, supplying the offerings for the feasts in 45:17, and real limits: 46:18 forbids him to take the people's inheritance by eviction, and 45:9 tells the princes to stop their violence and oppression. The office is described by what it may not do.

Zadok was David's priest, who stayed loyal through Absalom's revolt and anointed Solomon in 1 Kings 1:39, after which Solomon removed Abiathar and left Zadok in office. Verse 15 gives the reason his line keeps the altar: they kept charge of the sanctuary when Israel went astray. The other Levites in 44:10-14 are demoted to gatekeeping and slaughtering duty.

Verses 17-18 require linen turbans and linen undergarments in the inner court and forbid wool, with the reason stated: they must not wear anything that makes them sweat. Linen is a plant fibre that breathes; wool holds heat. Sweat was treated as a bodily discharge, and the sanctuary rules kept discharges away from the altar. It is a practical rule with a purity reason attached.

translationNotes.term: No land, because I am their inheritance
translationNotes.note: Verse 28 states it directly: you are to give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession. Numbers 18:20-24 gives the same arrangement and its mechanism, the tithe. A tribe with no farmland lives on what the other tribes bring, which is why 44:29-30 lists the grain, sin and guilt offerings, the devoted things and the firstfruits as their income.

Verse 24 assigns them to stand as judges in a dispute and rule by God's ordinances. Deuteronomy 17:8-13 sends the hard cases to the Levitical priests at the sanctuary, so this is the existing judicial system restated. The same verse adds keeping the appointed feasts and the Sabbaths, so teaching, judging and ritual belong to one office.

stories.keyTakeaway: God closes the eastern gate of the sanctuary because he entered through it, and he establishes strict regulations for the temple: only Zadok's descendants may serve as priests and enter the inner court, while Levites who turned to idols are restricted to gate duties and temple maintenance. Priests must observe detailed laws about clothing, diet, marriage, and handling the dead, receive no land inheritance but only offerings and firstfruits, and serve as judges and teachers for the people.

headings.text: The East Gate Assigned to the Prince

stories.title: 🧭 Ezekiel 45
summaryBullets: “When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you are to set aside a portion for the LORD, a holy portion of the land 25,000 cubits long and 20,000 cubits wide. This entire tract of land will be holy. (45:1).
Within this area there is to be a section for the sanctuary 500 cubits square, with 50 cubits around it for open land. (45:2).
From this holy portion, you are to measure off a length of 25,000 cubits and a width of 10,000 cubits, and in it will be the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place. (45:3).

It will be a holy portion of the land to be used by the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who draw near to minister before the LORD. It will be a place for their houses, as well as a holy area for the sanctuary. (45:4).
An adjacent area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple; it will be their possession for towns in which to live. (45:5).
As the property of the city, you are to set aside an area 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, adjacent to the holy district. It will belong to the whole house of Israel. (45:6).

Now the prince will have the area bordering each side of the area formed by the holy district and the property of the city, extending westward from the western side and eastward from the eastern side, running lengthwise from the western boundary to the eastern boundary and parallel to one of the tribal portions. (45:7).
This land will be his possession in Israel. And My princes will no longer oppress My people, but will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes. (45:8).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Enough, O princes of Israel! Cease your violence and oppression, and do what is just and right. Stop dispossessing My people, declares the Lord GOD.’ (45:9).
You must use honest scales, a just ephah, and a just bath. (45:10).
The ephah and the bath shall be the same quantity so that the bath will contain a tenth of a homer, and the ephah a tenth of a homer; the homer will be the standard measure for both. (45:11).
The shekel will consist of twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels will equal one mina. (45:12).
This is the contribution you are to offer: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley. (45:13).
The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each cor (a cor consists of ten baths or one homer, since ten baths are equivalent to a homer). (45:14).

And one sheep shall be given from each flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These are for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord GOD. (45:15).
All the people of the land must participate in this contribution for the prince in Israel. (45:16).

And it shall be the prince’s part to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings for the feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths— for all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He will provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel. (45:17).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘On the first day of the first month you are to take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary. (45:18).

And the priest is to take some of the blood from the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the gateposts of the inner court. (45:19).
You must do the same thing on the seventh day of the month for anyone who strays unintentionally or in ignorance. In this way you will make atonement for the temple. (45:20).
On the fourteenth day of the first month you are to observe the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten. (45:21).
On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land. (45:22).
Each day during the seven days of the feast, he shall provide seven bulls and seven rams without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD, along with a male goat for a sin offering. (45:23).
He shall also provide as a grain offering an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah of grain. (45:24).
During the seven days of the feast that begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he is to make the same provision for sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.’ (45:25).
crossRefs: Leviticus 19:35-36: Honest scales, honest weights and honest measures commanded, with the ephah and the hin named.
Deuteronomy 25:13-16: Two sets of weights and two sets of measures called detestable to the LORD.
Amos 8:4-6: Shrinking the ephah, inflating the shekel and cheating with dishonest scales.
Leviticus 25:8-13: The Jubilee, when property returns to the family that held it, behind the prince's land rule in 45:8.
Exodus 12:1-20: Passover and the seven days of unleavened bread, the feast 45:21-24 assigns to the prince.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵיפָה (ephah) - Hebrew: בַּת (bath) - Hebrew: חֹמֶר (chomer)
translationNotes.note: Verse 11 fixes the relationship: the ephah measures dry goods, the bath measures liquid, both hold exactly one tenth of a homer, and the homer is the standard both are cut from. A homer is roughly 58 gallons (220 litres), so an ephah or a bath is about 5.8 gallons (22 litres). Ruth 2:17 has Ruth carry home about an ephah of barley after a full day's gleaning, which is the everyday feel of the unit.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֶׁקֶל (sheqel) - Hebrew: גֵּרָה (gerah) - Hebrew: מָנֶה (maneh)
translationNotes.note: Verse 12 sets the weights: twenty gerahs make a shekel, and twenty plus twenty-five plus fifteen shekels make a mina, which is sixty shekels. A shekel is about two fifths of an ounce (11.4 grams), so a gerah is about half a gram and a mina about a pound and a half (684 grams). The Babylonian standard mina was also sixty shekels. These are weights on a balance, not coins; Judah had none yet.

translationNotes.term: Why the standards are in a temple vision
translationNotes.note: A measure fixed by the sanctuary is a measure nobody can quietly shrink. Leviticus 19:35-36 and Deuteronomy 25:13-16 already command honest weights, and Amos 8:5 describes the fraud they were aimed at: making the ephah small and the shekel large. Verses 9-12 put the reform between a rebuke of the princes for violence and the schedule of offerings, so the same list covers worship and market fraud.

translationNotes.term: A sixth of an ephah from a homer
translationNotes.note: Verses 13-14 set the contribution rates, and they are modest. Grain is one sixtieth, a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat or barley. Oil is a tenth of a bath from each cor, which is one hundredth. Verse 16 says all the people of the land are to give it to the prince, and 45:17 says the prince supplies the offerings out of it.

Verses 1-6 carve out a block of land before the tribal portions are assigned: 25,000 by 10,000 for the priests with the sanctuary at its centre, the same again for the Levites, and a strip 25,000 by 5,000 for the city and its farmland. The word is the one used for an offering lifted out and set aside. Land itself is being tithed here, and 48:8-20 lays out the same square in full.

stories.keyTakeaway: God establishes the sacred district's dimensions and allocates land for priests, Levites, the city, and the prince; then commands accurate weights and measures, prescribes offerings to be given to the prince, and details the purification ritual and festival observances the prince must provide.

stories.title: 🧭 Ezekiel 46
summaryBullets: “This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The gate of the inner court that faces east must be kept shut during the six days of work, but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened. (46:1).

The prince is to enter from the outside through the portico of the gateway and stand by the gatepost, while the priests sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings. He is to bow in worship at the threshold of the gate and then depart, but the gate must not be shut until evening. (46:2).
On the Sabbaths and New Moons the people of the land are also to bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway. (46:3).
The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six unblemished male lambs and an unblemished ram. (46:4).
The grain offering with the ram shall be one ephah, and the grain offering with the lambs shall be as much as he is able, along with a hin of oil per ephah. (46:5).
On the day of the New Moon he shall offer a young, unblemished bull, six lambs, and a ram without blemish. (46:6).
He is to provide a grain offering of an ephah with the bull, an ephah with the ram, and as much as he is able with the lambs, along with a hin of oil per ephah. (46:7).
When the prince enters, he shall go in through the portico of the gateway, and he shall go out the same way. (46:8).

When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship must go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate must go out by the north gate. No one is to return through the gate by which he entered, but each must go out by the opposite gate. (46:9).
When the people enter, the prince shall go in with them, and when they leave, he shall leave. (46:10).

At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain offering shall be an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and as much as one is able to give with the lambs, along with a hin of oil per ephah. (46:11).

When the prince makes a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or a peace offering, the gate facing east must be opened for him. He is to offer his burnt offering or peace offering just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and the gate must be closed after he goes out. (46:12).
And you shall provide an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning. (46:13).

You are also to provide with it every morning a grain offering of a sixth of an ephah with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour— a grain offering to the LORD. This is a permanent statute. (46:14).
Thus they shall provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every morning as a regular burnt offering.’ (46:15).
This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons as an inheritance, it will belong to his descendants. It will become their property by inheritance. (46:16).

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will belong to that servant until the year of freedom; then it will revert to the prince. His inheritance belongs only to his sons; it shall be theirs. (46:17).

The prince must not take any of the inheritance of the people by evicting them from their property. He is to provide an inheritance for his sons from his own property, so that none of My people will be displaced from his property.’” (46:18).
Then the man brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy chambers facing north, which belonged to the priests, and he showed me a place there at the far western end (46:19).

and said to me, “This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.” (46:20).
Then he brought me into the outer court and led me around to its four corners, and I saw a separate court in each of its corners. (46:21).
In the four corners of the outer court there were enclosed courts, each forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. Each of the four corner areas had the same dimensions. (46:22).
Around the inside of each of the four courts was a row of masonry with ovens built at the base of the walls on all sides. (46:23).
And he said to me, “These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple will cook the sacrifices offered by the people.” (46:24).
crossRefs: Numbers 28:1-15: The daily, Sabbath and New Moon offerings prescribed by weight and measure.
Exodus 20:8-11: The Sabbath command, the day the inner east gate is opened for in 46:1.
Leviticus 6:26-30: Where the sin offering is eaten and boiled, the kitchens shown in 46:19-24.
1 Kings 21:1-16: Naboth's vineyard seized by a king, exactly what 46:18 forbids the prince to do.
Leviticus 25:8-17: Property returning to its family at the Jubilee, the rule behind the prince's gifts in 46:16-18.

translationNotes.term: The gate opened on Sabbaths and New Moons
translationNotes.note: Verses 1-3 keep the inner east gate shut on the six working days and open it on the Sabbath and the New Moon. The prince stands at its post while the priests make his offering, and the people bow at that entrance. The New Moon was a marked day in Israel's calendar, in Numbers 28:11-15 and 1 Samuel 20:5, since the months ran on the moon and the new month was sighted, not calculated.

translationNotes.term: In one gate and out the other
translationNotes.note: Verse 9 sets a traffic rule for the festivals: whoever comes in by the north gate goes out by the south, and whoever comes in by the south goes out by the north; nobody leaves by the gate he entered. With a whole nation moving through one enclosure on a feast day, a one-way system is the only way the courts do not jam. It is crowd control, written into the law of the house.

translationNotes.term: The prince may not take a man's land
translationNotes.note: Verses 16-18 allow the prince to give land to a son, which stays with that son, or to a servant, which reverts in the year of liberty. Verse 18 then forbids him to take any of the people's inheritance by evicting them. That is Naboth's vineyard in 1 Kings 21 legislated against by name in all but the name.

translationNotes.term: Kitchens in the corners of the court
translationNotes.note: Verses 19-24 show the working kitchens: rooms at the west end where the priests boil the guilt and sin offerings and bake the grain offering, so those never leave the inner court, and four smaller walled courts in the corners of the outer court with hearths built round the base, where the temple servants boil the people's sacrifices. The vision ends its tour in the cookhouse.

translationNotes.term: A hin of oil for each ephah
translationNotes.note: Verses 5, 7 and 11 give the grain and oil ratio for each animal. A hin is about a gallon (3.8 litres) and an ephah about 5.8 gallons (22 litres) of flour, so roughly one part oil to six parts grain by volume. Numbers 28 sets similar proportions. The offering is a recipe, measured out, not an improvisation.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD establishes rules for the prince's worship and sacrificial offerings on Sabbaths and New Moons, along with regulations for the people's procession through the temple gates during festivals and directives about the prince's inheritance. A guide shows Ezekiel the priests' kitchen facilities where sacrifices are to be prepared.

headings.text: The Courts for Boiling and Baking

stories.title: 🌊 Ezekiel 47
summaryBullets: Then the man brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing from under the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east). The water was coming down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar. (47:1).
Next he brought me out through the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east, and there I saw the water trickling out from the south side. (47:2).
As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through ankle-deep water. (47:3).
Then he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through knee-deep water. Again he measured a thousand cubits and led me through waist-deep water. (47:4).

Once again he measured off a thousand cubits, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough for swimming — a river that could not be crossed on foot. (47:5).
“Son of man, do you see this?” he asked. Then he led me back to the bank of the river. (47:6).
When I arrived, I saw a great number of trees along both banks of the river. (47:7).
And he said to me, “This water flows out to the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah. When it empties into the Dead Sea, the water there becomes fresh. (47:8).

Wherever the river flows, there will be swarms of living creatures and a great number of fish, because it flows there and makes the waters fresh; so wherever the river flows, everything will flourish. (47:9).
Fishermen will stand by the shore; from En-gedi to En-eglaim they will spread their nets to catch fish of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea. (47:10).
But the swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt. (47:11).

Along both banks of the river, fruit trees of all kinds will grow. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail. Each month they will bear fruit, because the water from the sanctuary flows to them. Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing.” (47:12).
This is what the Lord GOD says: “These are the boundaries by which you are to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel; Joseph shall receive two portions. (47:13).
You are to divide it equally among them. Because I swore with an uplifted hand to give it to your forefathers, this land will fall to you as an inheritance. (47:14).
This shall be the boundary of the land: On the north side it will extend from the Great Sea by way of Hethlon through Lebo-hamath to Zedad, (47:15).
Berothah, and Sibraim (which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath), as far as Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran. (47:16).
So the border will run from the Sea to Hazar-enan, along the northern border of Damascus, with the territory of Hamath to the north. This will be the northern boundary. (47:17).

On the east side the border will run between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the Eastern Sea and as far as Tamar. This will be the eastern boundary. (47:18).
On the south side it will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea. This will be the southern boundary. (47:19).
And on the west side, the Great Sea will be the boundary up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This will be the western boundary. (47:20).
You are to divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel. (47:21).

You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners who dwell among you and who have children. You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; along with you, they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel. (47:22).
In whatever tribe a foreigner dwells, you are to assign his inheritance there,” declares the Lord GOD. (47:23).
crossRefs: Genesis 2:10-14: A river flowing out of Eden to water the garden and dividing into four headwaters.
Joel 3:18: A fountain flowing out of the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Acacias.
Zechariah 14:8: Living water going out from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western.
Revelation 22:1-2: A river of the water of life, with the tree of life bearing fruit every month and leaves for healing.
Numbers 34:1-12: The boundaries of the land as first assigned, the map 47:15-20 redraws.

translationNotes.note: Verses 3-5 turn the vision into a survey. The man walks east with a line, measures a thousand cubits and wades Ezekiel through ankle-deep water; a thousand more and it is knee-deep; a thousand more, waist-deep; a thousand more and it cannot be crossed, deep enough to swim. A thousand long cubits is about a third of a mile (560 m). A stream that deepens with no tributary joining it has no natural explanation, and the measuring is what makes that plain.

The water in 47:8 runs east down into the Arabah and into the sea, and the sea's water becomes fresh. That sea is the Dead Sea, roughly 1,400 feet (430 m) below sea level, the lowest exposed ground on earth, with a salt content around ten times that of the ocean. Nothing lives in it. Verses 9-10 put fish in it in great numbers, and fishermen spreading nets along the shore.

En-gedi means spring of the kid, an oasis of freshwater springs and palms on the western shore of the Dead Sea about halfway down, where David hid from Saul in 1 Samuel 24:1-2. En-eglaim is another shore site to the north. Verse 10 marks out the stretch of coast where the nets will be spread by naming the two points at its ends.

Verse 11 is a working exception in the middle of the promise: the swamps and marshes will not become fresh, they are left for salt. The shallow evaporation pans along the Dead Sea shore were and still are worked for salt, and salt was required with every grain offering under Leviticus 2:13. The supply is deliberately preserved.

Verses 22-23 assign resident foreigners who have settled and raised children in Israel a portion of land among the tribe they live in, counted as native-born. Under the older law a ger had legal protection and access to the feasts, in Leviticus 19:33-34 and Deuteronomy 10:18-19, but land inheritance was tribal. This gives them a share of the ground itself.

stories.keyTakeaway: A man shows Ezekiel water flowing from the temple that grows progressively deeper, healing the Dead Sea and bringing abundant fish and fruit trees to the land; the Lord then describes the boundaries of the restored land of Israel and instructs that it be divided equally among the twelve tribes, with portions also for foreigners living among them.

stories.title: 🌊 Ezekiel 48
summaryBullets: “Now these are the names of the tribes: At the northern frontier, Dan will have one portion bordering the road of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath and running on to Hazar-enan on the border of Damascus with Hamath to the north, and extending from the east side to the west side. (48:1).
Asher will have one portion bordering the territory of Dan from east to west. (48:2).
Naphtali will have one portion bordering the territory of Asher from east to west. (48:3).
Manasseh will have one portion bordering the territory of Naphtali from east to west. (48:4).
Ephraim will have one portion bordering the territory of Manasseh from east to west. (48:5).
Reuben will have one portion bordering the territory of Ephraim from east to west. (48:6).
Judah will have one portion bordering the territory of Reuben from east to west. (48:7).

Bordering the territory of Judah, from east to west, will be the portion you are to set apart. It will be 25,000 cubits wide, and the length of a tribal portion from east to west. In the center will be the sanctuary. (48:8).
The special portion you set apart to the LORD shall be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. (48:9).

This will be the holy portion for the priests. It will be 25,000 cubits long on the north side, 10,000 cubits wide on the west side, 10,000 cubits wide on the east side, and 25,000 cubits long on the south side. In the center will be the sanctuary of the LORD. (48:10).
It will be for the consecrated priests, the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray. (48:11).
It will be a special portion for them set apart from the land, a most holy portion adjacent to the territory of the Levites. (48:12).
Bordering the territory of the priests, the Levites shall have an area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The whole length will be 25,000 cubits, and the width 10,000 cubits. (48:13).
They must not sell or exchange any of it, and they must not transfer this best part of the land, for it is holy to the LORD. (48:14).
The remaining area, 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, will be for common use by the city, for houses, and for pastureland. The city will be in the center of it (48:15).
and will have these measurements: 4,500 cubits on the north side, 4,500 cubits on the south side, 4,500 cubits on the east side, and 4,500 cubits on the west side. (48:16).
The pastureland of the city will extend 250 cubits to the north, 250 cubits to the south, 250 cubits to the east, and 250 cubits to the west. (48:17).

The remainder of the length bordering the holy portion and running adjacent to it will be 10,000 cubits on the east side and 10,000 cubits on the west side. Its produce will supply food for the workers of the city. (48:18).
The workers of the city who cultivate it will come from all the tribes of Israel. (48:19).
The entire portion will be a square, 25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits. You are to set apart the holy portion, along with the city property. (48:20).

The remaining area on both sides of the holy portion and of the property of the city will belong to the prince. He will own the land adjacent to the tribal portions, extending eastward from the 25,000 cubits of the holy district toward the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 cubits to the western border. And in the center of them will be the holy portion and the sanctuary of the temple. (48:21).
So the Levitical property and the city property will lie in the center of the area belonging to the prince— the area between the borders of Judah and Benjamin. (48:22).
As for the rest of the tribes: Benjamin will have one portion extending from the east side to the west side. (48:23).
Simeon will have one portion bordering the territory of Benjamin from east to west. (48:24).
Issachar will have one portion bordering the territory of Simeon from east to west. (48:25).
Zebulun will have one portion bordering the territory of Issachar from east to west. (48:26).
And Gad will have one portion bordering the territory of Zebulun from east to west. (48:27).
The southern border of Gad will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt and out to the Great Sea. (48:28).
This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these will be their portions,” declares the Lord GOD. (48:29).
“These will be the exits of the city: Beginning on the north side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, (48:30).
the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. On the north side there will be three gates: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi. (48:31).
On the east side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan. (48:32).
On the south side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun. (48:33).
And on the west side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali. (48:34).
The perimeter of the city will be 18,000 cubits, and from that day on the name of the city will be: THE LORD IS THERE.” (48:35).
crossRefs: Joshua 13:1-19:51: The first division of the land by lot, tribe by tribe, that this chapter redraws.
Numbers 34:13-29: A leader named from each tribe to apportion the land as an inheritance.
Revelation 21:12-13: A city with twelve gates, three on each side, named for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Ezekiel 47:13-23: The outer borders of the land and the rule for allotting it, immediately before this list.
Genesis 49:1-28: Jacob blesses his twelve sons, the tribes whose names run down this map.

translationNotes.note: The old allotments in Joshua 13 to 19 followed terrain and were unequal, and Judah's portion dwarfed some others. This map ignores geography: thirteen parallel bands running east to west across the whole country, seven tribes north of the sacred district and five south, each the same width. Nobody gets the better hills, and the tribes descended from the slave-born sons, Dan, Asher, Naphtali and Gad, are no worse placed than the rest.

Verses 8-20 set aside a block 25,000 cubits on each side in the middle of the country: 25,000 by 10,000 for the priests with the sanctuary in it, the same for the Levites, and 25,000 by 5,000 for the city and its farmland. At the long cubit of 40:5 that square runs roughly eight miles (13 km) a side. The prince gets the land on either side of it, so he is next to the sanctuary and not in it.

Verses 30-34 give the city three gates on each of its four sides, each named for a tribe. Levi gets a gate, and Joseph is one gate instead of two, so Ephraim and Manasseh are counted together and the twelve comes out even. Revelation 21:12-13 describes the same arrangement, twelve gates with the names of the twelve tribes, three to a side.

The last line of the book, 48:35, gives the city a new name meaning The LORD Is There. Everything from chapter 8 onward has turned on presence: the glory leaving the temple, the exiles told in 11:16 that God had been a sanctuary to them in small measure, and the glory returning in 43:1-5. The book closes by naming the city after the one thing it had lost.

Verse 35 gives the city's perimeter as 18,000 cubits, four sides of 4,500 each, which at the long cubit is roughly one and a half miles (2.4 km) a side. That is a planned square, not the ridge-and-valley shape of the real Jerusalem. The name in the same verse, and not the dimensions, is what the chapter ends on.

stories.keyTakeaway: The twelve tribes receive their territorial allotments arranged north to south; a sacred square in the center contains the priest's portion, Levite lands, and the city with the LORD's sanctuary, and the city's gates are named after the tribes of Israel.

headings.text: The Portions for the Priests and Levites
The Portions for the Remaining Tribes

intro:
Ezekiel was written by Ezekiel son of Buzi (Ezekiel 1:3), a priest of the line of Zadok (Ezekiel 40:46; 44:15), during his prophetic ministry of at least twenty-two years from 593 BC to 571 BC (Ezekiel 1:1-2 dates the call; Ezekiel 29:17 dates the latest recorded oracle to the twenty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's exile). Ezekiel was born around 622 BC in or near Jerusalem into a priestly family, raised expecting to serve in the temple. He was deported to Babylon in 597 BC during the second Babylonian deportation alongside King Jehoiachin and ten thousand other exiles (2 Kings 24:10-16; Ezekiel 1:2), the same deportation in which the boy who would become King Zedekiah was left behind in Jerusalem to be installed as a puppet ruler. He settled at Tel Abib on the Kebar Canal in central Babylonia (Ezekiel 1:1; 3:15), near the ancient Sumerian city of Nippur, where the Babylonians had resettled the Judahite exiles. He was called as a prophet "in the thirtieth year" (Ezekiel 1:1), traditionally understood as his thirtieth year of life, the age at which a priest would normally have been ordained to serve in the temple; instead he received his commissioning vision by the Kebar in 593 BC, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile (Ezekiel 1:2). He was married to a woman whom God called "the delight of your eyes" (Ezekiel 24:16); she died suddenly on the day the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem began (Ezekiel 24:15-18), and God commanded him not to perform the customary mourning rites for her. His last dated oracle is from April 571 BC (Ezekiel 29:17). Ezekiel was a contemporary of Jeremiah (the older prophet still in Jerusalem and later in Egypt) and Daniel (the younger contemporary in the Babylonian court); Ezekiel 14:14 and 14:20 mention Daniel by name as a paragon of righteousness, indicating Daniel's reputation had already reached the exile community by Ezekiel's day.

The historical setting is the Babylonian exile under the Neo-Babylonian Empire of Nebuchadnezzar II (605-562 BC) and his successors. The Judahite exiles had been settled in agricultural communities along the Babylonian canals (the Kebar Canal was a major irrigation channel branching from the Euphrates near Nippur). Unlike the slaves of the Egyptian sojourn, the Babylonian deportees were free to work, marry, build houses, and conduct business (per Jeremiah's letter to the exiles, Jeremiah 29:4-7); some, like Daniel, even served in the imperial court (Daniel 1-6). Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar was at the peak of its splendor: the Ishtar Gate, the Hanging Gardens, the Etemenanki ziggurat (later legend identified the site with the Tower of Babel), and the great processional way of the Esagila temple complex marked the city as the cultural and economic center of the ancient world. Ezekiel's prophetic career spanned the final years of Judah (until 586 BC), the destruction of Jerusalem and Solomon's temple, and the years immediately following. Egypt under Pharaoh Hophra (Apries, 589-570 BC) and then Amasis II remained the only counterweight to Babylonian power. The Persian Achaemenid kingdom under Cyrus II was still consolidating in the east and had not yet risen.

Ezekiel is the twenty-sixth book of the Christian Old Testament and the third of the four Major Prophets (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel). The Hebrew name Yechezkel (יְחֶזְקֵאל) means "El (God) strengthens" or "God will strengthen," combining the verbal root chazaq ("to strengthen") with the divine name El. Hebrew manuscript fragments of Ezekiel were among the Dead Sea Scrolls discovered at Qumran (mid-20th century AD), with copies dating to the 1st century BC; the Masada Ezekiel scroll, discovered at the Herodian fortress of Masada in 1963, dates to the 1st century AD and was found buried beneath the synagogue floor in a genizah (a storage place for sacred but worn-out texts), confirming Ezekiel's status as Scripture in the Jewish community at the time of the Jewish-Roman War (AD 66-73).
